:::class-emblem Mystic
:::

*"The Veil does not ask you to understand it. It asks you to choose a side. You can change your mind, but never halfway."*

*initiate's instruction, Spire of Verita, Solari Prime*

### DESCRIPTION

Mystics hear the galaxy's heartbeat. For them, the Veil is not just energy, it is a living river that they swim in. They can read emotions like open books. They can bend spacetime with a thought. They can commune with artifacts that drive other people mad. In the wake of the Silence, they are guides through realities where our understanding of physics crumbles. Caution defines them. One wrong step in the Veil, and you might unravel your own mind. A Mystic at the table is the crew's sensitive, the one who feels the room's substrate-temperature shift before anyone else has noticed something is wrong.

### CORE STATS

- **Domains:** Neural & Lux *or* Void *(Veil Alignment, chosen at character creation)*

- **Starter Loadout.** Choose **2** Level 1 Powers from the **6** available to your Domains (three per Domain; the catalog is Chapter 19). A sturdy first pair: *Veil Sensitivity* and one Level 1 Power from your chosen alignment.

- **Spellcast Trait:** Instinct

- **Starting Evasion:** 10

- **Starting Hit Points:** 6

- **Class Items:** Whispering Veil-Crystal · Starlight Blindfold

### HOPE FEATURE: REALITY UNFOLD (3  HOPE)

Spend 3 Hope to gain **Advantage on all Rolls** until you resolve a Fear-dominant noncritical Roll. After that Roll resolves, mark **1d4 Stress** and end this effect. Matching dice remain a Critical Success and do not end it.

The Mystic's Hope Feature is a sustained alteration of the substrate around them, the universe briefly becomes slightly more cooperative, and the cost is always paid at the end, when reality reasserts itself.

### CLASS FEATURES

**Psychic Resonance (once per scene).** Before making a **Spellcast Roll** for a Mystic Power or a **Duality Roll** explicitly called for by a Mystic Feature, you may mark **1 Stress** to add **+2** to that Roll. This bonus does not apply to damage, Hope, Stress, a Reaction Roll, or a Roll that does not use the stated Mystic Power or Feature.

The bonus may turn a Failure into a Success, but it does not change whether Hope or Fear is higher and cannot create a Critical Success.

---

**Veil Alignment (Lux / Void).** At character creation, the Mystic chooses a **Veil Alignment**: Lux (the burnished gold of the Hope Frequency) or Void (the deep black of substrate entropy). This determines your second Domain. You may only equip Domain Cards from your chosen alignment, never both. At each Tier threshold (Levels 2, 5, and 8), you may switch your alignment during the level-up process. When you switch, all cards from your previous alignment become **dormant** (inaccessible until you realign), and you gain immediate access to the new domain's card list up to your current level, subject to normal Loadout and Vault limits. The Keeper should narrate the transition, switching from Void to Lux, or the reverse, is not a casual decision.

> **GEAR 1, MYSTIC VEIL ALIGNMENT AT A GLANCE** *(REFERENCE TABLE)*

| IF YOU ALIGN TO... | YOUR SECOND |
| --- | --- |

**IF YOU ALIGN TO...YOUR SECOND DOMAIN BECOMES... POWER FLAVOR**

Lux (gold sun)LuxDefense, illumination, anti-Void work Void (black spiral)VoidStealth, displacement, probability manipulation

|  |  | POWER FLAVOR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Lux *(gold sun)*** | Lux | Defense, illumination, anti-Void work |
| **Void *(black spiral)*** | Void | Stealth, displacement, probability manipulation |

A Mystic can only ever equip Powers from one alignment at a time. The dormant alignment's Powers do not vanish from the character's history, they remain in the Mystic's Vault, but cannot be slotted into the active Loadout until the Mystic realigns. The Keeper should make alignment switches into scenes; the friction is part of the Mystic's identity.

### BACKGROUND QUESTION

*What glimpse of the Veil's truth nearly cost you your mind?*

### SUBCLASSES


Veil Walker (Instinct), the unseen-paths walker. You walk the unseen paths between realities. By bending space and time, you can step through walls, evade attacks, and find sanctuary in dimensions that exist only for you.

- **Foundation, Phase Step (Reaction).** When you are the target of an attack or need to move through an obstacle, you can spend 1 Stress to "blink" to a location in Close range, evading the attack or obstacle. Once per short rest, you can create a pocket dimensional sanctuary that lasts 10 minutes, invisible and inaccessible.

- **Specialization, Temporal Distortion (Action).** Once per scene, you can spend 1 Hope to briefly manipulate time around an enemy. That enemy must reroll all dice on their next action and choose the lowest result.

- **Mastery, Causality Reverse (Reaction).** Once per session, immediately after one Action resolves within Close range, spend 3 Stress to restore positions, HP, Conditions, and damaged objects to their state immediately before that Action. Costs, Fear, Hope, Effort, Resolve, and once-per-use limits remain spent, so the reversal creates no duplicate resources. It cannot reverse ordinary death, a completed Death Move, or an event older than the immediately preceding Action.


Mind-Touched (Presence), the conduit of thought. You are a telepath, a living conduit for thoughts and emotions. You forge psychic links, share skills, and can shield your allies' minds from the horrors of the void.

- **Foundation, Thought Tide (Action).** Spend 1 Hope to allow an ally to use your Presence or Instinct modifier for one roll. Once per rest, you can spend 1 Stress to grant your entire crew a mental shield, giving them Advantage on rolls to resist fear or psychic influence for one scene.

- **Specialization, Implant Suggestion (Action).** Make a Presence vs. Presence or Instinct (defender chooses the higher) contest. On a success, you plant a single, subtle command in a target's mind (e.g., *forget my face*, *trust me*, *drop your weapon*). The target believes the thought is their own.

- **Mastery, Collective Consciousness (Action).** Once per session, you can spend 3 Hope to merge your mind with up to 3 allies in Close range for one scene. You share senses, emotions, and thoughts, gaining Advantage on all group rolls and on Instinct rolls to detect dangers.


Precursor Touched (Presence), the artifact-listener. You hear the whispers of ancient machines. Your mind connects with the relics of vanished civilizations, allowing you to awaken, interpret, and sometimes control technology that defies all known laws of physics.

- **Foundation, Ancient Echo (Action).** Spend 1 Hope to open your mind to a Precursor artifact or site. The Keeper will give you a cryptic, dream-like vision related to its purpose or history. You gain Advantage on all rolls to interact with it for the scene.

- **Specialization, Waken the Sleepers (Action).** Mark 1 Stress. You can temporarily awaken a dormant Precursor device. The device will perform its most basic function for one minute. The results are often unpredictable and dangerous.

- **Mastery, Cosmic Truth (Action).** Spend 3 Stress to ask one specific, actionable question about the current story arc. The Keeper answers truthfully with one established fact sufficient to act on. The Keeper gains 2 Fear, subject to the hard maximum of 12; no additional complication is created by this feature.

### TECHNOLOGY ACCESS


| ACCESS TIER & LEVEL | GEAR CATEGORIES |
| --- | --- |
| **Common (Tier 1)** · Level 1 | Light Armor, Melee/Pistols, Neural/Physical Augments |
| **Military (Tier 2)** · Level 2 | Light Armor, Melee/Pistols, Neural/Physical Augments |
| **Experimental (Tier 3)** · Level 5 | Light Armor, Melee/Pistols, Neural/Physical Augments, now at Experimental grade |

*Outside-access penalties are described in Chapter 13. Precursor (Tier 4) access is story-gated.*


:::class-emblem Pilot
:::

***Black Spiral + Teal Core.*** The Pilot's banner reads dark-and-precise, the slow Spiral of Void over the radiant Core of Tech. The colors of the substrate's gaps and the machine's heart, of the path through the unmappable and the engine that holds while you find it.

*"There's no such thing as a bad route. Only routes that take longer to kill you."*

*Captain Eva Rostova, The Stubborn Echo, Free Fleet*

### DESCRIPTION

Pilots see the void not as emptiness, but as a map of possibilities. In the fractured post-Silence galaxy, they are both explorers and lifelines. They are masters of intuition and technology. They thread ships through treacherous Veil currents. Their split-second decisions keep crews alive amid asteroid fields and cosmic storms. Whether they are charting unknown routes or outmaneuvering pirates, a true Pilot blends gut instinct with sharp reflexes. They are not just button-pushers. They are the souls who dance with stardust. A Pilot at the table is the crew's reason to trust the ship, and frequently the reason the ship is still flyable when the smoke clears.

### CORE STATS

- **Domains:** Void & Tech

- **Starter Loadout.** Choose **2** Level 1 Powers from the **6** available to your two Domains (three per Domain; the catalog is Chapter 19). A sturdy first pair: *Slipstream Jolt* and *Drone Whisper*.

- **Spellcast Trait:** Instinct

- **Starting Evasion:** 11

- **Starting Hit Points:** 6

- **Class Items:** Frayed Star Chart · Veil-Energy Control Crystal

### HOPE FEATURE: VEIL SURGE (3 HOPE)

Spend 3 Hope as a free effect before a Finesse (Pilot/Navigate) or starship Pilot Instinct Roll. Until the scene ends, those Rolls have Advantage. Once before the effect ends, after one hit would remove 3 or more Hull from your ship, reduce that Hull loss by 1; Armor Slots, System Integrity loss, tags, and other effects resolve normally. The protection expires unused when the scene ends.

### CLASS FEATURE: STELLAR INSTINCT

**Stellar Instinct.** Gain **+2** on **Finesse (Pilot/Navigate) Rolls** made to pilot a vessel, plot a course, dock, evade a hazard, or execute a ship maneuver. Once per session, after you fail one of those Rolls, reroll one of its two Duality dice and use the new result.

**Pilot Surge Die.** Your Pilot Surge Die is **1d6 at Tier 1, 1d8 at Tier 2, and 1d10 at Tier 3**. When you spend Hope to activate a Pilot Class Feature or Pilot Subclass Feature that calls for a Finesse (Pilot/Navigate) Roll, roll the Pilot Surge Die and add its result to that Roll. This die represents a risky surge of instinct: it does not create a Critical Success and cannot be added twice to the same Roll.

---
### BACKGROUND QUESTION

*What lost route drove you to risk everything in the Veil's currents?*

### SUBCLASSES


Void Runner (Instinct), the Veil dancer. You do not just fly a ship; you dance with the Veil's impossible currents. Relying on pure instinct, you see paths where others see only chaos, navigating the unnavigable.

- **Foundation, Pathfinder's Sense (Action).** Mark 1 Stress to sense the safest or fastest route through a dangerous area (asteroid field, nebula, contested system). You and your ship gain Advantage on all Piloting and Evasion rolls while following this route during the scene.

- **Specialization, Sensor Savant (Action).** When you make a sensor or Finesse (Pilot/Navigate) Roll, you can spend 1 Hope to gain Advantage. If you succeed with Hope, you also discover a hidden detail, a cloaked ship, a secret passage, a valuable resource.

- **Mastery, Veil Dancer (Passive / Action).** You no longer suffer penalties for navigating through Veil storms. Once per session, spend 3 Hope as an Action to fold space: transport your ship to any known location within the same star system, or transport yourself to a known place within Very Far range. This movement avoids all intermediate hazards.


Combat Ace (Agility), the kinetic dueler. For you, a starship is a weapon, and the void is your arena. You thrive in the chaos of battle, executing aggressive, high-G maneuvers that turn your vessel into a deadly extension of your will.

- **Foundation, Tactical Grace (Reaction).** When you or your ship is the target of an attack, you can spend 1 Stress to add your Agility modifier to the ship's Evasion for that attack.

- **Specialization, Combat Analysis (Action).** Mark 1 Stress and choose one visible enemy or enemy ship. For the rest of the scene, attacks made by you or your allies against that target gain +1d4 damage. This is not a starship Sensor Lock.

- **Mastery, Ace Maneuver (Action).** Once per scene, spend 2 Hope and choose one effect: **Evasive Pattern** (attacks against you or your ship have Disadvantage for the scene); **Attack Run** (your next personal attack prevents the target from spending Armor Slots, or your next naval attack bypasses the targeted arc and converts its damage directly to Hull through the naval damage table); or **Expose Weakness** (the target is Vulnerable for the scene).


System Jockey (Finesse), the ghost in the machine. For you, a starship is a complex instrument, and the void is a symphony you conduct. You do not just fly; you interface, tweaking power levels, spoofing sensors, and pushing the ship's technology beyond its designed limits.

- **Foundation, Orbital Whisperer (Action).** When attempting to dock, land, or navigate in tight spaces, you can spend 1 Stress to automatically succeed. You can also spend 1 Hope to obtain a complete and detailed map of all defenses and active security systems in the area.

- **Specialization, Gravity Slingshot (Action).** When performing a gravity-assist maneuver, make a Finesse (Pilot/Navigate) Roll, DC 10. On success, you reach your destination in half the time and consume no fuel for the maneuver. On failure, you reach the correct destination but the journey is rough, causing 1 Stress to every crew member.

- **Mastery, Ghost in the Machine (Action).** Once per session, you can spend 3 Hope to seamlessly integrate into the systems of a station or capital ship during a scene. You can control any of its automated functions (defenses, communications, life support, docking bays) as if you were the designated operator, without needing to make hacking rolls.

### TECHNOLOGY ACCESS


| ACCESS TIER & LEVEL | GEAR CATEGORIES |
| --- | --- |
| **Common (Tier 1)** · Level 1 | Light/Medium Armor, Pistols/Rifles, All Augmentations |
| **Military (Tier 2)** · Level 2 | Light/Medium Armor, Pistols/Rifles/Heavy Weapons, All Augmentations |
| **Experimental (Tier 3)** · Level 5 | Light/Medium Armor, Pistols/Rifles/Heavy Weapons, All Augmentations, now at Experimental grade |

*Outside-access penalties are described in Chapter 13. Precursor (Tier 4) access is story-gated.*


:::class-emblem Scholar
:::

*"Three hundred years of records, four contradictory primary sources, two fragments of recovered Precursor inscription, and a thousand assumptions nobody has ever tested. You wanted me to find the truth. I found the place where the truth used to be."*

*Senior Archivist Solene Ashar-Vell, House Amaranth Inner Library, presentation to the Council of Wisdom*

### DESCRIPTION

Scholars are galactic detectives, chasing lost truths in a fractured universe. They piece together fragments of forgotten sciences, alien biologies, and Precursor riddles. Their labs range from dusty archives to toxic alien ecosystems. They are always hunting for the *why* beneath the chaos. When others see ruins, they see stories. When others fear anomalies, they see breakthroughs. In the wake of the Silence, knowledge is not just power, it is oxygen. A Scholar at the table is the crew's lens onto everything the Pearl Era did not bother to preserve, and frequently the reason the crew survives the Vault that the rest of them thought was empty.

### CORE STATS

- **Domains:** Tech & Social

- **Starter Loadout.** Choose **2** Level 1 Powers from the **6** available to your two Domains (three per Domain; the catalog is Chapter 19). A sturdy first pair: *Quantum Firewall* and *Linguistic Patch*.

- **Spellcast Trait:** Knowledge

- **Starting Evasion:** 10

- **Starting Hit Points:** 5

- **Class Items:** Cracked Data-Slate · Vial of Alien Sample

### HOPE FEATURE: EUREKA MOMENT (3  HOPE)

Spend 3 Hope instead of rolling one Knowledge Roll to research or analyse an established subject at DC 20 or lower. Treat it as Success with Hope, not a Critical Success: no dice are rolled and it generates no Fear or additional path resource. Ask one question about a connection between established facts; the Keeper answers truthfully or says that the evidence does not establish one. It cannot create a new faction, culprit, clue, or fact.

### CLASS FEATURE: PATTERN WEAVER

**Pattern Weaver.** Gain **+2** on **Knowledge Rolls** made to analyse a document, object, creature, location, system, or recorded evidence. Once per session, mark **1 Stress** to ask the Keeper one question: *What is the most important hidden connection here?* or *What is the most exploitable vulnerability here?* The answer is truthful but cannot reveal information that does not yet exist in the fiction.

During a Long Rest, you may work on one recorded Research Project. After **three successful Knowledge Rolls** made during different Long Rests, the project is complete. A Critical Success counts as one successful Roll for this Feature. When you begin the project, choose its reward: a named Contact, a verified lead, a Tier-appropriate schematic, or permission to attempt a specific project-related action without needing new research.

---
### BACKGROUND QUESTION

*What lost fragment of pre-Silence lore became your obsession?*

### SUBCLASSES


Xenobiologist (Instinct), the alien-life student. You are a student of alien life in its purest form. By studying strange ecosystems and bizarre biologies, you access the secrets of adaptation and survival in the galaxy's harshest corners.

- **Foundation, Life Reader (Action).** Spend 1 Hope to study an organism (living or dead) and learn its biology, behavior, and weaknesses. The Keeper will reveal a mechanical weakness (e.g., Vulnerable to an energy type) or a narrative weakness (e.g., afraid of light).

- **Specialization, Ecosystem Decoder (Passive).** You have Advantage on all Instinct Rolls to survive alien biomes and Finesse (Pilot/Navigate) Rolls made there. Additionally, you can spend 1 Stress to identify a native plant or animal that can be used as a resource, poison, medicine, food.

- **Mastery, Evolutionary Forecast (Action).** Once per session, you can spend 3 Hope to predict a significant environmental change in a star system (a solar storm, massive creature migration, disease outbreak). The Keeper will give you vital information about this event, allowing you to prepare for or exploit it.


Precursor Archaeologist (Knowledge), the relic- reader. You study what no one else can read. The dead languages, the silent sites, the artifacts that mainstream archaeology has filed away as inert. You believe the Precursors were trying to communicate, and you intend to listen.

- **Foundation, Artifact Whisper (Action).** Spend 1 Hope to attune to a Precursor artifact. The Keeper will reveal a fragment of its history or a clue about how to use it. You have Advantage on all rolls to activate Precursor technology for the scene.

- **Specialization, Cultural Reconstructor** **(Passive).** When interacting with a faction you have studied, you gain +2 to all Presence Rolls made for social interaction. Additionally, you can spend 1 Stress to recall a key custom or taboo, avoiding a serious social mistake.

- **Mastery, Philosophy Engine (Action).** Once per session, you can spend 3 Hope to decipher a fundamental principle of pre-Silence wisdom. This allows you to create a single-use, relic-tier invention that can drastically alter a situation, a device that nullifies local gravity, a translator that works on any speech, a scanner that briefly maps the Veil itself.


Information Theorist (Knowledge), the data-stream analyst. You study patterns, networks, and the hidden architecture of how information moves through systems and societies. To you, every faction is a network, every economy is a graph, and every secret is a node waiting to be reached.

- **Foundation, Data Storm (Reaction).** When you fail a decryption or hacking roll, you can spend 1 Stress to reroll the dice. If you succeed, you can also create a temporary firewall that protects that system for one scene.

- **Specialization, Social Algorithm (Passive).** You have Advantage on all Presence Rolls made for social interaction against any organization you have previously analyzed. You can spend 1 Stress to predict an organization's next move, gaining a key clue.

- **Mastery, Quantum Network (Action).** Once per session, you can spend 3 Hope to establish an instant and undetectable quantum communications network across a star system for the duration of the scene.

:::class-emblem Scoundrel
:::

*"Never love anything you can't abandon in ten seconds flat."*

*Operating principle, Free Fleet Scoundrel's Code, attributed to Jax of the Three Names*

### DESCRIPTION

Scoundrels are ghosts in the machine. They slip through security grids. They wear identities like cheap suits. They trade secrets like currency. In a galaxy of shattered surveillance, they are the rats in the walls, always listening, stealing, and surviving. Charm is their lockpick. Paranoia is their armor. A Scoundrel at the table is the crew's professional liar, and frequently the reason the crew gets out of the building before the alarms have finished thinking about going off.

### CORE STATS

- **Domains:** Social & Void

- **Starter Loadout.** Choose **2** Level 1 Powers from the **6** available to your two Domains (three per Domain; the catalog is Chapter 19). A sturdy first pair: *Perfect Facade* and *Temporal Cloak*.

- **Spellcast Trait:** Finesse

- **Starting Evasion:** 12

- **Starting Hit Points:** 6

- **Class Items:** Morphic Skeleton Key · Influential Holo-Mask

### HOPE FEATURE: VANISHING ACT (3  HOPE)

Spend 3 Hope as an Action to become Hidden for up to 1 minute. Visual, audio, thermal, network, and psionic detection Rolls cannot locate you unless a feature explicitly penetrates Vanishing Act. The effect ends immediately after you attack, activate a Power, transmit, move an object another creature carries, or interact physically with an unwilling creature. It does not erase tracks made before activation, bypass a sealed barrier, or make allies Hidden.

### CLASS FEATURE: SHADOW OPERATIVE

**Shadow Operative.** Gain Advantage on Agility Rolls to avoid detection. Once per session, you may reroll one failed Agility Roll made to evade an immediate danger and use the new result.

**Sneak Attack.** When an Attack Roll with Advantage hits, add **1d6 damage** once to that attack. Add **2d6** at Tier 2 and **3d6** at Tier 3 instead. Any source of Advantage can arm Sneak Attack, but additional sources of Advantage do not increase its damage.

---
### BACKGROUND QUESTION

*What prize was worth abandoning your identity for ten seconds flat?*

### SUBCLASSES


Assassin (Finesse), the disguised killer. You are a deadly ghost who wears faces like masks. A master of disguise and lethal precision, you can become anyone and get anywhere, ensuring your target never sees the end coming.

- **Foundation, Deadly Masquerade (Action).** Spend 1 Stress to create a flawless disguise and identity for one scene. You can spend 1 Hope to make this identity stand up to any level of scrutiny for 24 hours.

- **Specialization, Viper's Kiss (Passive).** When you score a Critical Success on an attack, the target is automatically Stunned. You can also choose to spend 1 Stress to apply a potent neurotoxin (Poisoned effect) to any successful attack.

- **Mastery, Perfect Kill (Action).** Once per combat, you can spend 2 Hope to declare your next attack against a target who is unaware of you, Surprised, or Helpless is a perfect kill. It is an automatic Critical Success and deals maximum damage.


Ghost (Agility), the silent infiltrator. You are a whisper in the dark, a true master of infiltration. You move without a sound and leave no trace, bypassing the most advanced security systems as if they were not there.

- **Foundation, Ghost (Action).** Mark 1 Stress to become invisible for one round, or to remove all traces of your passage through an area. If you succeed with Hope on an Agility Roll to avoid detection while invisible, you remain invisible.

- **Specialization, Like a Whisper (Passive).** You are a ghost to machines. You cannot be detected by non-psionic sensors, cameras, or automated systems unless you choose to be.

- **Mastery, Shadow Network (Action).** Once per session, you can spend 2 Hope to call upon your network of spies and informants. You can either gain a key piece of information about any target in the sector, or have your network create a diversion or provide a safehouse.


Contrabandist (Presence), the rogue with the cargo hold. The charming rogue with a fast ship and a hidden cargo hold. You know the price of everything and the location of every crooked port official. You are not necessarily a hacker, but you are a master of logistics, bluffing, and improvisation.

- **Foundation, Hidden Cargo (Action).** Spend 1 Stress to declare you have a small, useful, or contraband item secreted on your person or ship that you have not previously mentioned. The Keeper has final say on what is plausible. Once per session, you can spend 1 Hope to upgrade this declaration to a Tier 1 piece of gear or a small quantity of valuable contraband.

- **Specialization, Dock Authority (Passive).** You have Advantage on all Presence Rolls made for social interaction with port officials, dockmasters, customs agents, and the working staff of stations and waystations. You can spend 1 Hope to ensure that a routine inspection of your ship turns up nothing of interest, regardless of what you are actually carrying.

- **Mastery, The Long Con (Action).** Once per story arc, you can spend 3 Hope to declare that an elaborate scheme you set up months or years ago has just paid off. The Keeper and you negotiate the specifics, what was the con, who was the mark, what did you get, but the payoff is real and meaningful (a major resource, a significant piece of intelligence, a powerful favor).

:::class-emblem Soldier
:::

*"You hold the line. The line holds you. That is the whole of the work."*

*Sergeant-Instructor Hira Volkov, Joric Defensive Academy, instruction to first-year cadets*

### DESCRIPTION

Soldiers are unbreakable walls in a crumbling galaxy. They stand between innocent refugees and ruthless raiders. They are the line between hope and the endless void. Some wear heavy powered armor. Others wield nothing but their own grit and determination. Their strength is not just in muscle, it is in reading threats before they strike. It is in turning a panicked crowd into a disciplined unit. It is in knowing when to break bones in order to save lives. A Soldier at the table is the crew's reliable wall, the one whose presence in a corridor changes how everyone else moves through it.

### CORE STATS

- **Domains:** Kinetic & Synthesis

- **Starter Loadout.** Choose **2** Level 1 Powers from the **6** available to your two Domains (three per Domain; the catalog is Chapter 19). A sturdy first pair: *Kinetic Blast* and *Rapid Regeneration*.

- **Spellcast Trait:** Strength

- **Starting Evasion:** 9

- **Starting Hit Points:** 7

- **Class Items:** Dented Riot Shield · Fallen Comrade's Dog-tag

### HOPE FEATURE: COMBAT SURGE (2 HOPE)

**Combat Surge (2 Hope).** After you hit with an attack, spend **2 Hope** to deal an additional **1d6 damage** to that attack. You may use Combat Surge once per attack.

---
### CLASS FEATURE: COMBAT FOCUS

**Combat Focus (once per scene, voluntary after a hit).** After you hit with a weapon attack, you may enter **Focus** and set your **Focus Die** to **1**. Your Focus Die is **1d4 at Tier 1, 1d6 at Tier 2, and 1d8 at Tier 3**. The Focus Die is a step track, not a die you roll: its current value starts at 1 and cannot exceed the highest face of its current Tier.

Focus lasts until the scene ends, you become Dazed or Stunned, or the Focus Die would increase above its maximum. While Focused, before each weapon attack, choose **one** benefit: reroll one weapon damage die for that attack, **or** add the current value of your Focus Die to that attack’s damage if it hits. You cannot add the Focus Die to the Attack Roll.

At the end of each Spotlight you take while Focused, if you dealt damage during that Spotlight, increase the Focus Die by 1. When the Focus Die would increase above its Tier maximum, end Focus and reset the die to 1. Once per Focus, while you hold Spotlight, you may give one ally **+2** on their next Roll or **+2 Evasion** until they next hold Spotlight; then yield Spotlight to that ally. The +2 bonus is a flat bonus and does not create or stack with Advantage.

---
### BACKGROUND QUESTION

*What made you stand your ground when all others fled?*

### SUBCLASSES


Guardian (Strength), the unbreakable shield. You are the crew's unbreakable shield. Standing between your allies and harm, you absorb punishment with sheer will and grit. Where you stand is where the line is drawn, and it will not break.

- **Foundation, Bodyguard Protocol (Reaction).** When an ally within Close range is hit by an attack, you can spend 1 Stress to intercept it, taking the damage yourself. When you do, you gain Advantage on your next Melee attack against that attacker.

- **Specialization, Hold the Line! (Action).** Mark 1 Stress. You become a point of mobile cover. Allies adjacent to you gain the benefit of cover (+2 to their Evasion) and can ignore the effects of Stagger or forced movement until your next Spotlight.

- **Mastery, Unbreakable (Reaction).** Once per session, when one or more allies would take damage, you can spend 3 Hope to negate all of it. Describe how you absorb or deflect the assault. For the rest of the scene, your armor's Major and Severe thresholds are reduced by 2.


Military Officer (Finesse), the battlefield conductor. You are a battlefield conductor, orchestrating victory through superior tactics and decisive commands. You do not just fight; you lead, turning a chaotic firefight into a symphony of coordinated destruction.

- **Foundation, Call the Shot (Action).** Mark 1 Stress to grant an ally one of the following benefits on their next action: gain Advantage, their attack ignores cover, or their action does not draw the spotlight.

- **Specialization, Exploit Weakness (Action).** Spend 1 Hope to analyze an enemy's tactics or equipment. For the rest of the scene, all attacks made by your allies against that enemy have the *Armor Piercing* quality.

- **Mastery, Battlefield Symphony (Action).** Once per session, spend 3 Hope. Every other crew member may immediately take one Action without spending their Spotlight, in an order chosen by those players. An Action granted this way cannot grant another Action or another Spotlight.


Peacekeeper (Presence), the order without violence. You believe true strength lies in control, not destruction. You enforce order with an intimidating presence and non-lethal tactics, proving that a firm word can be far mightier than a plasma rifle.

- **Foundation, Unspoken Authority (Action).** Spend 1 Hope to halt a conflict for a single, tense moment. No one can take hostile action until you speak or act. This gives you a key window to negotiate, intimidate, or create an escape route.

- **Specialization, Common Ground (Action).** Spend 1 Stress and make a Presence Roll. On a success, you find a point of leverage or empathy with one enemy. You can turn them into a temporary ally or remove them from the fight as they question their loyalties. If you succeed with Hope, they reveal a key secret about their leader.

- **Mastery, Sanctuary (Action).** Once per session, spend 3 Hope to declare a zone around you as neutral ground. For the scene, no one can willingly initiate violence within this zone, enforced by your sheer presence.

:::class-emblem Vanguard

*"The body is the strike. The mind is the line of the strike. There is no daylight between them."*

*Master Vanguard Tenshi-Ko, on the discipline of Supreme Focus*

### DESCRIPTION

The Vanguards are warriors who seek perfection through the synthesis of mind (**Neural**) and body. They reject over-reliance on technology as a distraction, trusting instead in discipline and their connection to the substrate to attain a state of **Supreme Focus**. For them, combat is not mere violence but a perfectly executed ritual, a dance of control. They use their minds to anticipate movements, augment their kinetic reflexes, and project their will onto the battlefield. They are the living expression of *mind over matter*. A Vanguard at the table is the crew's centered presence, the one whose stillness in a crisis steadies everyone else's hands.

### CORE STATS

- **Domains:** Neural & branch *(Void / Kinetic / Lux, determined by Subclass)*

- **Starter Loadout.** Choose **2** Level 1 Powers from the **6** available to your Domains (three per Domain; the catalog is Chapter 19). A sturdy first pair: *Mind Shield* and one Level 1 Power from your branch Domain.

- **Spellcast Trait:** Presence

- **Starting Evasion:** 11

- **Starting Hit Points:** 6

- **Class Items:** Light Staff *(Melee)* · Meditation Orb · Spiced Tea Mix

### HOPE FEATURE: PATH TO NIRVANA (3 HOPE)

**Path to Nirvana (3 Hope).** Spend 3 Hope to enter the **Nirvana State**. As you enter, set your **Integrity Die** to its highest face by Tier: a **d4** at Tier 1, a **d6** at Tier 2, or a **d8** at Tier 3 or higher. Choose **Agility, Instinct, or Strength** as you enter. For the duration:

- You have Advantage on Rolls using the chosen Trait.
- You are immune to the Stunned and Dazed conditions.
- Your first Melee attack against an enemy during the state deals an additional **2d6** damage of your subclass branch type.

Each time you roll with Fear during the state (including on a Reaction), reduce your Integrity Die by 1; it is never reduced on matching dice. The state ends when your Integrity Die reaches 0 or when the scene ends, whichever comes first.

**Breaking Point.** At any point during the state, you may end it as a free effect on your action to unleash a closing strike: that action deals an additional **(Proficiency)d6** damage of your subclass branch type. This bonus is added once, after any multipliers, and is never doubled on a Critical.

The state does not grant an additional Action, Spotlight, Reaction, or automatic success.

---
### CLASS FEATURE: UNBROKEN FOCUS

Your mental discipline allows you to channel psionic energy into movement and combat.

- While not wearing **Heavy** or **Very Heavy** armor, you gain **+1 Evasion**.

- Your unarmed attacks (or attacks with **Melee** weapons that possess the *Lightweight* feature) count as possessing the **Energy Tag** (Void damage).

- **Internal Alignment (Passive).** Once per Spotlight, spend **1 Stress** to ignore negative modifiers to your Evasion until the end of the round. This does not remove Conditions or grant a bonus above your unmodified Evasion.

### SUBCLASSES


Ghost Blade (Finesse), the deadly grace. Your body is a weapon honed to impossible sharpness. You move with a fluid, deadly grace, your every deflection and strike a perfect synthesis of psionic anticipation and physical execution. Second Domain: Void.

- **Foundation, Perfect Deflection (Reaction).** Spend 1 Stress to gain +3 Evasion against one incoming attack. If the attack misses due to this bonus, you gain Advantage on your next Melee attack against that attacker.

## CHOOSING YOUR CLASS

A few notes on the selection.

**Class is the kit, not the character.** Two players who pick the same Class can produce wildly different characters depending on their Ancestry, their Community, their Background Question answer, and their roleplay choices. A Volkov-trained human Soldier from a Frontier Colony plays differently from a Bloomstrider Soldier from the Verdant Conclave, even if they have identical mechanical sheets. Choose the Class whose *kit* matches the work you want to do, and let the rest of your character sheet handle the texture.

**Class fit with crew composition.** A balanced crew has a healer-coded role (Engineer, Explorer, certain Mystic builds), a face-coded role (Diplomat, Scoundrel, Scholar), a combat-coded role (Soldier, Vanguard, certain Pilot builds), and a substrate-perception role (Mystic, certain Vanguard builds). You do not need all four covered, and you can double up on roles deliberately, but think about where your character will be most useful before locking in the choice. The Keeper can also help you read the crew.

**Awakened vs Sleeping at the same Class name.** As noted in the introduction, several Class names appear in both the Awakened catalog (this chapter) and the Sleeping catalog (Chapter 7). They are not the same character. An Awakened Soldier has Hope-spending Powers; a Sleeping Soldier has Effort-and-Recovery mechanics. Both are mechanically supported and both produce satisfying play. The choice between them is the choice you made in Chapter 2 (Two Paths), and it is a choice about *what kind of being your character is*, not just about which page of the rulebook to read.

**The two variable-Domain Classes.** The Mystic and the Vanguard both have second-Domain choices that warrant extra thought. A Mystic's Veil Alignment can be switched at later Tier thresholds, but each switch is a substantive event in the fiction; pick an alignment that the player wants to explore for at least the first few sessions. A Vanguard's Subclass branch is fixed, so spend the time at character creation to make sure the branch's tactical role (stealth-and-strike, precognitive dodge, projected force) matches the play you are excited for.

**Class and Spellcast Trait.** The **Class fixes the Spellcast Trait**; a Subclass only overrides it where its entry explicitly lists a different Trait in parentheses. The Class value is the *default*, the Trait used when a Power card calls for a Spellcast Roll without specifying a different Trait. Many Subclasses have their own Trait listed in parentheses after the Subclass name; those Subclass abilities use the listed Trait, even if it differs from the Class default. A Soldier's default Spellcast Trait is Strength, but a Soldier who is also a Military Officer uses Finesse for the Subclass abilities. Powers that explicitly list Trait alternatives let you choose at activation time. The system is more flexible than a single per-Class Spellcast Trait would be.

## WHAT COMES NEXT

You now have an Awakened Class (this chapter), and the Subclass within it. The next layer of decision is **Traits and Experiences** (Chapter 8), your character's six numerical Trait modifiers and their formative key moments. After that comes **Equipment** (Chapter 8 / Chapter 9) and finally any **Connections** you want to establish with your crewmates before play begins.

The Class catalog above is the system's way of telling you what kinds of work the Pearl Era post-Silence galaxy needs done. The character you build out of one of these Classes is your way of telling the table what kind of person is going to do that work, in your specific campaign, alongside your specific crew, against the specific shape of trouble the Keeper is preparing.

Pick the kit that excites you most. The character will follow.

# CHAPTER 7: THE SLEEPING

*The Silence left two kinds of people. Some woke to the Hope Frequency and can bend the Veil. The rest are deaf to it, and run on something the universe never gave them: themselves. This chapter is for the second kind. (Why the split exists at all is cosmology, and lives in "The Galaxy in Depth"; here we teach how to play one.)*

***At a glance.*** A Sleeping character runs on two resources. Effort is your everyday currency, the Sleeping answer to Hope, generated through play and spent on your class's Effort Feature and reactions. Resolve is a small, scarce reserve of d4 that powers your signature Moves (1 at a time, up to your pool). On top of both, you hit harder every level (Honed Edge) and invoke your Experiences for free. Pick a class, note a

Recovery Anchor, and you are ready.

## HOW THE SLEEPING WORK

### EFFORT, THE EVERYDAY RESOURCE

Effort is what you summon when there is no song to lean on: breath, discipline, and the muscle memory of a thousand drills. You begin play with **2 Effort** and hold a maximum of **6**. You spend Effort on your class's **Effort Feature** and on reactions, exactly where an Awakened character would spend Hope.

**Generating Effort: the Effort Track.** Your sheet shows an **Effort Track** with two segments. When Hope is the higher die on a meaningful Duality Roll, mark one segment whether the roll succeeds or fails; when both segments are marked, clear them and gain **1 Effort**. Trivial, repeated, or consequence-free rolls never mark the Track. On a **Critical Success**, clear 1 Stress, mark both Track segments, resolve the completed Track for 1 Effort, then gain **1 further point** placed in either Effort or Resolve; if Effort is full, place that further point in Resolve. The Track payout and the further point are separate and both occur. Recovery and class features never generate Effort unless they state an explicit exception.

**Burnout.** At 0 Effort, you may still invoke a feature by paying **1 HP** instead. You are then **Burned Out**: your Stress maximum is reduced by 1 until your next Recovery. While Burned Out you still mark the Effort Track and gain Effort normally; the engine dims, it does not stop. The Awakened bargain with the substrate; the Sleeping bargain with their own body, and some nights the body does not forgive it.

### RESOLVE, THE RESERVE FOR MOVES

Resolve powers your **Moves**, the signature plays that make the Sleeping more than a steady professional. It is deliberately scarce.

- **Pool.** Maximum Resolve begins at **2**, and rises by 1 at levels **3, 5, 7, and 9** (so 2 / 3 / 4 / 5 / 6 across a campaign, reaching 6 at level 9). Resolve Dice are **d4**. You begin play with the pool full.

- **Refill.** Resolve never recovers automatically from a rest. During a Short Rest, choose **Prepare** as one of the two different rest moves to recover 1 Resolve; during a Long Rest, choose **Prepare** to restore Resolve to its pool maximum. Chapter 9 is the authoritative rest procedure. Resolve is a reserve, not a meter; a Move is a moment, not a habit.

- **Spending.** Each Move lists a cost in dice. Some are a flat spend; some are *spend and roll*, where you roll the dice and apply their total. You may spend up to your whole pool on a single Move.

- **The limit.** Resolve adds to a roll's **total** only. It never changes which die, Hope or Fear, came up higher, and never makes a critical. You can grind a failure into a success and still pay the Fear that came with it.

> **EFFORT VS RESOLVE.** Use Effort often. Spend Resolve when the scene should remember it.

**Session refresh and the broken scene.** A new calendar session does not by itself reset Effort or Resolve; use the rest and downtime procedures in Chapter 9. If a session ends mid-scene with the tension unresolved, resume it with the same marked resources unless the fiction included a completed rest or downtime.

Every Sleeping character has two Class Moves from their primary Class. Most subclasses add one Subclass Move, gained when you take that subclass; you will find them inside each class entry, under Resolve Moves. A multiclass grants only the one eligible secondary Class Resolve Move selected through Chapter 11. The Sleeping Mystic is the documented exception: its subclasses directly modify its ritual, manifestation, or research engine instead of adding a separate Resolve Move. Spend Resolve Dice (d4) to use them; "spend and roll" means roll the dice and apply their total. Costs are starting values, tune freely. Moves sit alongside each class's Effort Feature and Class Feature; they do not replace them. One Move is universal to every Sleeping character:

- **Bear Down** *(spend and roll, any number)*. After any Duality Roll, attack, reaction, or damage roll, before the outcome is narrated, spend Resolve Dice and add their total. The plainest refusal to fail.

### BEARING DOWN: COMMON EFFORTS

Beyond your class's Effort Feature, every Sleeping character can spend Effort on a short list of general plays. None of these is an automatic success; each one bends a roll or the fiction in a measurable way, and the Duality Roll, with its risk of Fear, still happens. These are the shared vocabulary of the Sleeping craft; your subclass and Moves add to it.

**Costing 1 Effort:**

- **Steady Hands.** Before you make a Core Trait Roll that draws on something genuinely practiced, spend 1 Effort to add **+2**; justify the practice in the fiction.
- **Read the Room.** Ask the Keeper one question about the immediate tactical or social situation, exits, who holds power here, where the tension sits, and they answer truthfully.
- **Push Through.** Ignore one minor environmental or condition penalty on your next action (smoke, partial darkness, awkward footing).

**Costing 2 Effort:**

- **The Opening.** You gain **Advantage** on your next roll, the product of preparation, position, or hard experience.
- **Try Again.** After you roll, reroll **one** of your two Duality dice (the Hope die or the Fear die) and use the new result. You do not get to keep the better of the two automatically; if you reroll the Fear die and it comes up higher, you live with it. Rerolling a die is control, not a guarantee.
- **Brace.** Against harm you see coming, drop the next hit you take by one severity band (Severe to Major, Major to Minor), gritting through it. This spends no Armor Slots.
- **Cover the Angle.** Give your Reaction to an ally within range: the next Core Trait Roll they make before the start of your next Spotlight gains **+2** as you cover, guide, or warn them.

**Optional module, costing 3 Effort:** Adopt both options before the session begins and tell the players; otherwise neither is available. Adoption cannot change during a scene.

- **Second Wind.** Clear **2 Stress** outside of a rest, catching your breath mid-action.
- **Seize the Moment.** After a success, add one extra favorable consequence to the fiction, which the Keeper validates. This is not a second success; it is a branch (you open the door, and you also overhear what is being said on the other side).

### HONED EDGE (PASSIVE)

Your damage rolls gain a flat bonus equal to your **level minus 1** (+1 at level 2, up to +9 at level 10), added once. No resource, no roll: the steady mastery that makes a Sleeping veteran the hardest reliable hitter in any crew.

### YOUR EXPERIENCES ARE FREE

You invoke an Experience **without spending any resource**: once per roll, add a relevant Experience's flat bonus for free. You also begin play with **one additional Experience** beyond the standard array. You are, more than anyone, the sum of what you have done.

### RECOVERY, THE SLEEPING PRACTICE

Recovery is how the Sleeping clear Stress, and it follows the Corebook's rest rules rather than adding a check. During a **Short Rest**, choose **Clear Stress** as one of your two different rest moves to perform a Recovery and clear `1d4 + Tier` Stress; during a **Long Rest**, choose **Decompress** as one of your two different rest moves to clear your whole Stress track (Chapter 9). What makes it the Sleeping's own is the **Recovery Anchor**: a specific, lose-able practice you choose at creation (a knife to sharpen, a letter reread, a precise way of breathing). The Anchor is not a die roll; it is a requirement and a story handle. With it to hand, your chosen recovery move works automatically. If the story has taken it from you, lost, broken, confiscated, left behind, you cannot choose Clear Stress or Decompress until you recover the Anchor or establish a new one over a Long Rest. Make the Anchor specific enough that the table can deny it to you when the story needs the weight. Recovery never generates Effort; Effort is earned at the table, half a step at a time, through the Effort Track.

## THE NINE SLEEPING CLASSES

### HOW TO READ A SLEEPING CLASS ENTRY

Each entry uses the same frame, so once you can read one you can read all nine:

- **Description.** Who this professional is in the fiction, and the table problems they solve.
- **Core Stats.** HP, Stress, Evasion, starting Trait guidance, and the Signature Trait the class leans on.
- **Effort Feature.** The class engine: the thing you do often, paid in Effort from the Effort Track.
- **Class Feature.** The permanent, always-on edge that needs no resource at all.
- **Resolve Moves.** The signature plays: two Moves from the primary Class plus one Move per subclass, paid in Resolve Dice; rare by design (see Resolve, above). A multiclass adds only the one eligible secondary Class Resolve Move specified in Chapter 11. The Sleeping Mystic is the exception, with subclass features that modify its two Class Moves and its research system directly.
- **Background Question.** One question that ties the profession to your past; answer it before play.
- **Subclasses.** Foundation, then Specialization, then Mastery: the arc your craft follows as you advance.

Two chapter-level systems apply to every class and live earlier in this chapter rather than in each entry: **Honed Edge**, the passive competence of the Sleeping, and the **Recovery Anchor**, the specific, lose-able practice your character recovers by, named at creation (Chapter 8).

What follows is the catalog of the nine classes as they appear on the Sleeping Path. Each entry mirrors the Awakened version in traits and silhouette, and usually in Domains. The Sleeping Mystic is the deliberate exception: it begins with two studied Domains and may reconstruct others through research. What differs, and what differs deeply, is the Effort Feature, the Class Feature's emphasis, and the Subclasses' grounding. Sleepers do not forfeit power. They simply pay for it differently.

The class emblems, banners, and visual identities are shared with Chapter 6. A Diplomat is a Diplomat regardless of Path. The flags fly the same.


:::class-emblem Diplomat
:::

*"Your mystics tell me the substrate sang under their feet at the Hydros Accord. Mine slept through the whole conference. We signed the paper anyway."*

*Senior Liaison Dom Eskal, House Valerius observation, the night of the Hydros Accord*

### DESCRIPTION

The Sleeping Diplomat is the version of the trade you will meet most often in actual rooms. They have read the files. They have memorized the names of the spouses and the children and the exes. They have prepared three concessions they are willing to make and three they will pretend to consider. They have not heard the Hope Frequency in their lives, and they do not expect to. They will save your fleet anyway, by talking, by writing, by knowing the man across the table better than he knows himself.

### CORE STATS

- **Domains:** Social & Lux

- **Spellcast Trait:** Presence

- **Starting Evasion:** 10

- **Starting Hit Points:** 6

- **Class Items:** Annotated Briefing Folio · Treasured Token (a personal anchor; an old letter, a worn coin, a scarred datapad)


### EFFORT FEATURE: THE PREPARED MIND (2 EFFORT)

You can spend 2 Effort to choose one of three powerful effects. Where the Awakened Diplomat's *Power of Suggestion* runs on charisma and the universe's quiet cooperation, the Prepared Mind runs on the work you have already done before the scene began.

- **Cite the File.** Declare you have read about this person, this house, this faction, or this situation in advance. The Keeper provides one true and useful fact about them, a vulnerability, a recent event, a relationship, a stated position, that you may not have learned yet but that fits what your character could reasonably have prepared.

- **Anticipated Move.** When an NPC declares a social or political Action in the scene but before its Roll or effect resolves, use your Reaction and choose one response: **Expose**, make an Instinct or Knowledge Roll, DC 15, with Advantage; on success one willing ally gains Advantage on their next Roll against that NPC before the end of the round. **Interpose**, make a Presence Roll, DC 15, with Advantage; on success the NPC's declared Roll has Disadvantage. Failure changes nothing. This never cancels an Action without a Roll or dictates an NPC's belief.

- **The Quiet Word.** You speak privately to one NPC currently in the scene. Whatever you say, the NPC takes seriously, not necessarily favorably, but seriously. They consider it as a credible signal. Where this leads is between you, them, and the table.

> **INFLUENCE SCALES WITH THE ROLL.** Success: those present, this scene. With Hope: it holds after you leave. Critical: it spreads beyond the room. With Fear: it turns on you.

### CLASS FEATURE: STANDING REPUTATION

Sleeping Diplomats build influence the slow way, by being reliable, but they spend the same currency every Diplomat does: **Favor Tokens**. The pool, the cap, the way they are earned, and the way they are spent are identical to the Awakened Diplomat's Cultural Lens (Chapter 6), so a character who Awakens or who came up Sleeping never has to relearn how their social capital works. The path changes how you fight and rest, through Effort and Resolve; it does not change how you trade in favors.

You begin each session with **2 Favor Tokens** and hold a maximum of **4** (raised cumulatively by background and subclass, so a Core World Sleeping Diplomat holds up to 6). The first time each scene you succeed on a meaningful Presence Roll to persuade or deceive, gain 1; you also gain 1 on every Long Rest. You spend them through your subclass abilities, through House and Free Fleet contacts (Chapter 5), to automatically succeed on an institutional task (1 Favor), or by spending 5 at once to raise your Reputation with one faction by 1 RP (Chapter 16), bought standing that can be lost again by how you act.

What "Standing Reputation" names is not a separate resource but the Sleeping Diplomat's reading of the same one: every Favor is a debt of trust earned by being dependable where it was witnessed, not by performance or spectacle. Favor Tokens are not Effort. They are the slower, longer-running currency of the Diplomat's career, the same on either path.

**Protocol.** You always know the correct form (title, gift, taboo, precedence) for any culture in common knowledge; no roll. For isolated or unknown cultures, roll Knowledge (DC set by how removed they are) to read their norms from behavior alone. Once you know the protocol, you cannot offend by accident, only by choice.

### BACKGROUND QUESTION

*Whose trust did you betray to get where you are, and what would it cost you to repair it?*

### SUBCLASSES


Cultural Attaché (Presence), the bridge-builder. You speak more languages than is reasonable and have lived in more cultures than is comfortable. You translate not only words but assumptions.

- Foundation, Mother Tongue (Passive). You speak fluently any galactic language that has at least 100 living speakers. For dead languages or extremely rare tongues, you have working competence with a Knowledge roll at advantage.

- Specialization, The Listening Posture (Action). Spend 1 Effort. For the next minute of conversation, you understand not only what the NPC is saying but what they mean to say but cannot. The Keeper provides a brief paraphrase of the subtext after each significant statement.

- Mastery, The Reconciliation (Action). Once per story arc, mediate between two conflicting parties willing to sit. Roll Presence; the DC scales with the depth of the grievance. On success they agree terms; influence scales with the roll. A critical buries the grievance itself.


The Steward (Knowledge), the keeper of letters. Where the Icon performs charisma at the cosmic register, the Steward keeps records. You know who owes whom, who married whom, who buried whom. You do not forget, and you do not let others forget.

- Foundation, The Standing File (Passive). You maintain a private dossier on every named NPC the party has met. At the start of any scene featuring a returning NPC, you may ask the Keeper one question about that NPC's recent activities; the Keeper answers truthfully (omissions are permitted; lies are not).

- Specialization, Cited Precedent (Action). Spend 1 Effort during a social roll. You cite a specific past event, a treaty, a debt, a kindness, a betrayal, that bears on the present moment. The Keeper grants advantage and adjusts the scene's stakes to acknowledge the citation.

- Mastery, The Long Memory (Action). Once per story arc, you may declare that you have been preparing for this exact meeting for years. You produce a document, an heirloom, a witness, or a recorded confession that decisively changes the conversation. The Keeper and you negotiate what it is. Once produced, it is spent.


Political Operative (Finesse), the back-channel. The Sleeping back-channel does not run on charm. It runs on leverage, leverage, and leverage. The Operative is the version of the trade nobody puts on the recruiting brochures.

- Foundation, The Quiet Map (Passive). At the start of any new political environment (a city, a station, a fleet), you may spend a Short Rest mapping the informal power structure. The Keeper provides three significant relationships, debts, or grievances that are not common knowledge.

- Specialization, Lever (Action). Spend 1 Effort. You apply a piece of known leverage to an NPC during a social scene. The Keeper describes the NPC's resistance and what concessions, if any, are now possible. Successful application of leverage may also incur a permanent enmity, leverage is remembered.

- Mastery, The Dossier (Action). Once per story arc, you produce a sealed dossier on a named NPC. Its contents, if released, would destroy that NPC's position. You may threaten its release; you may release it; you may, most dangerously of all, use its existence as a private gift. The Keeper helps you determine the dossier's exact contents only at the moment of use.


### RESOLVE MOVES

**Class Moves**

- **Force of Presence** *(spend and roll 1+)*. Add the rolled total to a Presence roll, or make a single NPC of lesser standing yield a minor concession with no roll. What they yield, they yield in front of witnesses.

- **Read the Table** *(spend 1)*. In any negotiation, learn each present NPC's true priority and which of them will break first.

**Subclass Moves**

- **Cultural Attaché, Common Ground** *(spend 1)*. Bridge a cultural divide instantly; treat a stranger as a known contact for the scene.

- **The Steward, The Ledger Remembers** *(spend and roll 1+)*. Add the rolled total to a roll that leverages who owes whom, or surface a true obligation an NPC is bound by. Either way, the obligation becomes established fact; the debt outlives the scene.

- **Political Operative, Leverage** *(spend 2)*. Produce a piece of usable leverage on a target you have had time to study. One use.

### TECHNOLOGY ACCESS

Your class trains with the gear below; even at **Common (Tier 1)**, not every class is trained for every basic item (a Diplomat is not trained on rifles, and never becomes so). Using gear outside your access is at a penalty (Chapter 13), and Precursor (Tier 4) is story-gated.


| Access Tier | Level | Gear Categories |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Common (Tier 1) | 1 | Light Armor, Melee/Pistols, Neural/Physical Augments |
| Military (Tier 2) | 2 | Light Armor, Melee/Pistols, Neural/Physical Augments |
| Experimental (Tier 3) | 5 | Light Armor, Melee/Pistols, Neural/Physical Augments, now at Experimental grade |


:::class-emblem Engineer
:::

*Sergeant-Engineer Iva Kurogane-Born, on her family's heirloom drive core*

### DESCRIPTION

The Sleeping Engineer is the working version of the trade, the one whose hands are stained with the same compounds in the same patterns regardless of which Domain Frequency happens to be cooperative this week. They do not call on the substrate to favor the repair. They strip the panel, find the failure, and fix it. If the fix takes thirty hours, they take thirty hours. The engine runs because they made it run. There is no further explanation.

### CORE STATS

- **Domains:** Tech & Synthesis

- **Spellcast Trait:** Knowledge

- **Starting Evasion:** 9

- **Starting Hit Points:** 7

- **Class Items:** Toolbelt with Logged Inventory · Personal Wrench (named, tracked)


### EFFORT FEATURE: BRUTE-FORCE DIAGNOSTIC (2 EFFORT)

You can spend 2 Effort to choose one of three effects. The Sleeping Engineer's signature is not inspiration but *thoroughness*. You have ruled out everything else; what remains is the answer.

- **Find the Failure.** Spend 1 minute of in-fiction time examining a malfunctioning system. The Keeper tells you exactly what is wrong with it, in detail, including any concealed sabotage. (You still need parts, time, and tools to fix it.)

- **Never Rated For This.** Choose one non-Precursor machine, vehicle subsystem, or piece of equipment you can touch. Until the end of the scene, it ignores one penalty caused by damage or the environment, **or** it completes one task in half the normal fictional time. At the end of the scene, it is disabled and cannot be used until repaired during downtime. This is ordinary descriptive language, not a Condition. It cannot increase damage, Armor Slots, Evasion, thresholds, Power level, or access Tier.

- **The Field Manual.** You produce, from memory, a procedure for handling a specific technical situation, the procedure is one your character has practiced or read, not improvised. The Keeper grants advantage on the next four rolls related to executing it, by you or by an ally you instruct.

### CLASS FEATURE: LOGGED TOOLS

Sleeping Engineers do not jury-rig from cosmic confidence; they jury-rig from *kit.* Record three tool types: `cutting`, `diagnostic`, `medical`, `security`, `signal`, or `fabrication`. Once per scene, when one recorded type is relevant to a technical Roll, gain **+2** to that Roll. A Logged Tool supplies what is needed to attempt the task; it never solves the task automatically or creates Tiered gear. A type is depleted only when a printed Feature explicitly consumes it; restore every depleted type during Downtime with ordinary supplies and no Roll.

### BACKGROUND QUESTION

*What broke that you couldn't fix, and what did you build to make sure the next one wouldn't?*

### SUBCLASSES


Tech Specialist (Knowledge), the digital tradesman. You do not believe networks have personalities. You believe networks have logs.

- Foundation, The Audit (Action). Spend 1 Effort to audit any networked system you have access to. The Keeper tells you what processes are running, what data has moved in the last hour, and what anomalies, if any, are present.

- Specialization, The Quiet Hand (Action). Spend 1 Effort. You modify a system you have audited; the modification persists until discovered. The Keeper describes the realistic parameters of the modification's stealth.

- Mastery, The Dead Drop (Passive). You maintain a permanent, hidden access channel into any system you have administered for at least one week. The Keeper tracks these channels; they may be discovered, but they do not expire.


Xenotech Savant (Knowledge), the documentarian of impossible objects. The Awakened version of this subclass interprets Precursor artifacts; the Sleeping version catalogs them, and is wary of every word that begins with the prefix xeno-.

- Foundation, The Catalog (Passive). When you encounter unfamiliar technology, you may consult your catalog (a large, ugly, hand-written document the character keeps). The Keeper tells you whether your catalog has a relevant entry, and if so, what it says, including its limits.

- Specialization, The Procedure (Action). Spend 1 Effort and name one printed hazard of an unfamiliar artifact that your catalog could address. You or one ally gains Advantage on the next Roll made this scene to handle that hazard. On Failure with Fear, the attempt fails and the artifact applies only its printed consequence; no additional hazard is invented.

- Mastery, The New Page (Action). Once per story arc, after extensive observation, you add an unfamiliar artifact's behavior to your catalog. From that point forward, you and your party have working competence with that class of artifact.


Medical Technician (Instinct), the field surgeon, the mortician, the keeper of bodies. Sleeping medics do not believe in miracles. They believe in protocols.

- Foundation, The Triage (Action). Spend 1 Effort. You assess the medical state of every conscious or unconscious creature within Close range. The Keeper tells you who is dying, who is stable, and who is faking.

- Specialization, Stabilize (Action). Spend 1 Effort while adjacent to a Dying or Final creature. Clear all Dying and Final Progress; the creature is stable at 0 HP. This requires no Roll, restores no HP, and never reverses a completed Death Move.

- Mastery, The Last Rite (Action). Once per story arc, perform a six-hour procedure on the recoverable body of a named character who died through ordinary Final Progress during the previous 24 hours. They return with 1 HP and a permanent narrative Scar chosen by that character's player; a mechanical Scar requires that player's agreement. This cannot reverse a completed Death Move or restore a body made unrecoverable by an explicit rule.


### RESOLVE MOVES

**Class Moves**

- **Field Improvisation** *(spend and roll 1+)*. Choose one: restore personal or vehicle Armor Slots, drone HP, or one ship arc's Armor Slots equal to the total; restore 1 Hull per full 5 points in the total, maximum 3 Hull and once per ship per scene; return one offline Common or Military device to service for the scene; or assemble a single-use device that grants Advantage on one declared Core Trait Roll before the scene ends. It requires suitable scrap but no workshop and never raises a maximum.

- **Hot-Wire** *(spend 1)*. Bypass one non-Precursor lock or activate one non-Precursor machine without a Roll until the end of the scene. The device immediately records an unauthorized-access alert detectable by its owner or local security; Hot-Wire grants no credentials and cannot override a safety rule that names a higher requirement.

**Subclass Moves**

- **Tech Specialist, Ghost in the Logs** *(spend and roll 1+)*. Add the total to one Knowledge Roll for network access or intrusion, or read the system's recorded activity from the previous 24 hours. If the system contains credentials for an established identity, you may attribute the intrusion to that identity; this cannot create a person, credential, or access level that was not already present.

- **Xenotech Savant, Safe Handling** *(spend 1)*. Before handling a Precursor artifact, name one hazard printed in its entry. Suppress that hazard for you and willing assistants until the scene ends. This does not suppress costs, Corruption, or any other effect and cannot affect an unidentified hazard.

- **Medical Technician, Stabilize** *(spend and roll 1+)*. Clear HP marks from a downed or wounded ally equal to the rolled total. Field medicine, not magic.

### TECHNOLOGY ACCESS

Your class trains with the gear below; even at **Common (Tier 1)**, not every class is trained for every basic item (a Diplomat is not trained on rifles, and never becomes so). Using gear outside your access is at a penalty (Chapter 13), and Precursor (Tier 4) is story-gated.


| Access Tier | Level | Gear Categories |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Common (Tier 1) | 1 | Light/Medium Armor, Pistols, All Augmentations, All Equipment |
| Military (Tier 2) | 2 | All Armor, Pistols/Rifles, All Augmentations, All Modifications, All Equipment |
| Experimental (Tier 3) | 5 | All Armor, Pistols/Rifles, All Augmentations, All Modifications, All Equipment, now at Experimental grade |


:::class-emblem Explorer
:::

Cartographer-Adept Varra Lakhamen, Explorers' Guild

### DESCRIPTION

Explorers map. The Awakened Explorer feels the system she is mapping; the Sleeping Explorer measures it. Both produce useful charts. The Sleeping version produces charts you can hand to a stranger and have them follow.

### CORE STATS

- **Domains:** Synthesis & Lux

- **Spellcast Trait:** Instinct

- **Starting Evasion:** 11

- **Starting Hit Points:** 6

- **Class Items:** Survey Instruments · Personal Logbook (every entry by hand)


### EFFORT FEATURE: METHODICAL RECONNAISSANCE (2 EFFORT)

You spend 2 Effort to choose one:

- **The Margin Note.** Declare one plausible physical feature your logbook recorded: a culvert, ledge, or forgotten hatch. It grants Light Cover or permits one ordinary one-band movement that the current terrain blocked, chosen when declared. It cannot open a sealed area, resolve a Clock, negate a revealed danger, or contradict an established fact; no extra complication is added.

- **The Trail.** Examine ground or wreckage. The Keeper tells you who came through, in what numbers, in what direction, and approximately when. Sleeping Explorers track by sign, not by sense.

- **The Charted Route.** Declare a plausible logged route through the current difficult environment. The crew gains Advantage on its next two movement or navigation Rolls made to follow that route in this scene. It cannot create an exit in a sealed area, resolve a Clock, negate a revealed danger, or contradict an established fact; no unprinted complication is added.

### CLASS FEATURE: THE LOGBOOK

You maintain a personal Logbook of every place your character has been. Entries are handwritten, dated, and detailed. Once per session, when arriving in a location your character has previously logged, you may consult the Logbook for one specific recalled detail, a name, a hidden passage, a former contact's address. The detail is correct as of the time of the log entry.

### BACKGROUND QUESTION

*What is in your logbook that you have not shared with the crew, and why?*

### SUBCLASSES


Cartographer (Instinct), the patient mapmaker.

- Foundation, Dead Reckoning (Passive). You can determine your position on any planet, station, or vessel without instrumentation, with at most a 5% error.

- Specialization, The Marked Route (Action). Spend 1 Effort. You leave a permanent, subtle trail along your route. Anyone in your party (or anyone you teach the marks to) can follow this trail without rolling.

- Mastery, The Chart (Action). Once per story arc, you complete a definitive chart of a region, system, or sector. The chart functions as a faction asset, sold, gifted, or referenced, and earns you standing with the Explorers' Guild and any party that uses it.


Wilderness (Strength), the survivor.

- Foundation, Self-Reliant (Passive). You and one ally ignore mechanical penalties caused solely by ordinary hunger, thirst, or lack of sleep in an environment that supports Class-IV humanoid life. These words are environmental causes, not additional Conditions, and this feature does not prevent printed starvation, dehydration, or exposure damage.

- Specialization, The Old Craft (Action). Spend 1 Effort, choose one. We Camp Here: declare a defensible camp in hostile terrain; during a rest here the environment cannot reach you, one watch suffices, and the party clears 2 additional Stress. The Weather Turns: read sky, current, or pressure; declare what the environment will do in the coming hours, and it does. Live Off This: in any living environment, produce the food, water, or remedy the scene needs.

- Mastery, The Old Way (Passive). You and any allies under your guidance can travel through hostile environments at full pace and without injury. The Keeper still adjudicates encounters, but the environment itself does not harm you.


The Stalker (Finesse), the hunter. The Sleeping Stalker's hunt is patience, not communion.

- Foundation, Mark Quarry (Action). Mark a target. For the next 24 hours, you have advantage on Instinct rolls to track them and your first successful attack each round against them deals an extra 1d6 damage.

- Specialization, Unrelenting Pursuit (Action). Spend 1 Effort. While pursuing your marked quarry, you cross one significant environmental obstacle without losing time or momentum.

- Mastery, The Trap is Sprung (Action). Once per session, spend 3 Effort to declare you set a trap for your marked quarry in the current location. The trap's nature is yours to describe; the quarry, on entering, is Restrained or Cornered for the scene.


### RESOLVE MOVES

**Class Moves**

- **Find a Way** *(spend 1)*. There is always a route. Discover a viable path through terrain, a blockade, or a sealed approach.

- **Read the Ground** *(spend 1)*. Learn the chief hazard and one resource or landmark of unfamiliar terrain before crossing.

**Subclass Moves**

- **Cartographer, Perfect Recall of Place** *(spend and roll 1+)*. In any place you have mapped, add the rolled total to a relevant roll, and you never lose your way.

- **Wilderness, Endure** *(spend 1)*. You and the crew ignore one environmental hazard (heat, toxin, an exposure window) for a meaningful stretch.

- **The Stalker, Run It Down** *(spend and roll 1+)*. When tracking or pursuing, add the rolled total; on a hit, close to your quarry. Your quarry now knows it is hunted.

### TECHNOLOGY ACCESS

Your class trains with the gear below; even at **Common (Tier 1)**, not every class is trained for every basic item (a Diplomat is not trained on rifles, and never becomes so). Using gear outside your access is at a penalty (Chapter 13), and Precursor (Tier 4) is story-gated.


| Access Tier | Level | Gear Categories |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Common (Tier 1) | 1 | Light Armor, Pistols, Exploration & Survival Equipment, Physical Augments |
| Military (Tier 2) | 2 | Light Armor, Pistols/Rifles, Exploration & Survival Equipment, Physical Augments |
| Experimental (Tier 3) | 5 | Light Armor, Pistols/Rifles, Exploration & Survival Equipment, Physical Augments, now at Experimental grade |


:::class-emblem Mystic
:::

*"The Veil does not speak to me. It has never spoken to me. I have spent thirty years studying what it is anyway. I know more about it than most who hear it sing. Hearing is not understanding. Sometimes hearing is the obstacle to understanding."*

*Doctor Emeline Skarrh, Spire of Verita, on her sixth published volume*

### DESCRIPTION

The Sleeping Mystic is a ritualist, occult scholar, and dangerous experimentalist who cannot naturally perceive the Veil. They work from testimony, instruments, correspondences, recovered procedures, and notes written by people who did not survive their discoveries. An Awakened Mystic reaches into a narrow part of the substrate by instinct. A Sleeping Mystic learns how to make the substrate answer through preparation, exact language, and unacceptable risk.

A Sleeping Mystic is not a lesser Awakened Mystic. Their reliable work is slower and communal, their direct manifestations are costly, and every forced opening may attract attention. In exchange, their Archive can eventually contain patterns from every Domain.

### CORE STATS

- **Starting Archive:** Choose two different Domains. You unlock every Level 1 Power in both Domains.
- **Spellcast Trait:** Knowledge
- **Starting Evasion:** 10
- **Starting Hit Points:** 6
- **Class Items:** Veil-Crystal Recorder *(takes readings the user cannot directly perceive)* · Bound Notebook of Annotations

### EFFORT FEATURE: THE READING (2 EFFORT)

Spend 2 Effort and study a person, place, object, active Power, or Veil phenomenon with your instruments and notes. Ask one question about its Veil exposure, Domain signature, history, instability, likely behavior, or the procedure required to interact with it. The Keeper answers with one fact, uncertainty, lead, or limitation supported by the evidence. You did not perceive this truth. You reconstructed it.

### CLASS FEATURE: UNCANNY ARCHIVE

Your Archive records complete procedural patterns rather than prepared Powers. It has no Loadout and no Vault. Every Power in an unlocked Domain Path is available through **Uncanny Power**, subject to its access roll.

**Starting Archive.** At character creation, choose two different Domains and unlock Level 1 in both. Unlocking a Domain at a specific level gives you every Power from that Domain at exactly that level.

**Domain Study Project.** To unlock a new Domain Path, begin a Study Project with a clock equal to:

> **4 + the selected Domain level**

The selected level cannot exceed your character level. During a Long Rest, you may choose **Study the Archive** as one of your two Long Rest moves to mark 1 segment on one active Domain Study Project. A project may also receive one source-assisted attempt per session: spend a scene studying one newly acquired relevant text, willing teacher, artifact, or direct exposure, then make a Knowledge Roll, DC 15. A Critical Success marks 2 segments; any other success marks 1; Failure with Hope marks none; Failure with Fear marks none and the Mystic marks 1 Stress. A given source contributes to a given project only once. Downtime creates no additional progress beyond these stated procedures.

**Breadth requirement.** To begin research at Level 2 or higher, you must already have at least two different Domains unlocked at the immediately preceding level. The new research does not need to continue either of those Domains.

For example, Lux 1 and Neural 1 allow you to research Void 2 and Synthesis 2. Once both are complete, those two Level 2 Paths allow research into any Level 3 Domain, even a Domain you have never studied before.

Completing the clock unlocks every Power in the selected Domain at that level. Your Archive is intentionally irregular. You might know Lux 1, Neural 1, Void 2, Synthesis 2, Kinetic 3, and Social 3 without knowing the missing levels between them.

### BACKGROUND QUESTION

*What procedure worked when every expert insisted it could not, and what noticed you when it did?*

### SUBCLASSES

The Sleeping Mystic is an exception to the usual subclass Resolve Move structure. Its subclasses do not add a separate Resolve Move. Instead, each subclass develops one of the class's three engines: ritual, raw manifestation, or research.


Veil Walker (School of the Lattice) (Knowledge), the architect of shared conditions. You do not step through the Veil. You build a stable procedural lattice around the people who trust you.

- Foundation, Layered Working (Passive). When you perform a Calibrated Minor Ritual, choose two different ritual effects instead of one. Every affected creature receives both effects. You cannot select the same effect twice.

- Specialization, Enduring Formula (Passive). Double the rolled duration of every Calibrated Minor Ritual you perform. You also gain the Protective Geometry ritual effect: choose either +1 Evasion or +1 to all damage thresholds. The same benefit applies to every affected creature.

- Mastery, Shared Lattice (Passive). Improve every ritual effect you provide: Group Calibration grants +2 instead of +1; Group Adaptation protects against two specific environmental hazards instead of one; Sustained Restoration clears 2 HP at the end of each complete hour; Protective Geometry grants +2 Evasion or +2 to all damage thresholds. All affected creatures may also communicate telepathically with one another for the ritual's duration.
