Emergency Stabilization still consumes all remaining duration and ends every effect, including telepathy.


Mind-Touched (School of Apprehension) (Knowledge), the impossible conduit. Repeated exposure has changed the architecture of your mind. You still cannot hear the Veil, but you can contain complete power-patterns that should not fit inside a Sleeping consciousness.

- Foundation, Perfect Invocation (Special). Once per Short Rest, manifest one Power from a Domain Path you have unlocked, at a level no higher than your character level. Spend no Resolve, make no access roll, and make no Spellcast Roll. The Keeper gains 1 Fear, subject to the hard maximum of 12. Ignore the Power's Hope cost, but pay any Stress, HP, material, frequency, or other printed cost. Use the Power's normal activation timing; Passive Powers cannot be invoked this way.

- Specialization, Reach Beyond (Action). Once per session, attempt one unknown Power exactly one level higher than your character level from any Domain in which you have at least one unlocked Domain Path. Spend no Resolve and make no access roll. The Keeper gains 1 Fear, subject to the hard maximum of 12. Make a Knowledge Spellcast Roll against a DC set by the Power's Tier (Tier 1 DC 15, Tier 2 DC 20, Tier 3 DC 25). On success, resolve the Power and pay every non-Hope printed cost. On failure, it does not manifest. This does not add the Power to your Archive, and it cannot reproduce a Reaction or Passive Power.

- Mastery, Impossible Efficiency (Special). Once per session, when you use Uncanny Power, each Resolve spent contributes two Resolve Dice to the access Roll instead of one. Add Knowledge once; the Keeper gains 1 Fear for each Resolve actually spent, subject to the hard maximum of 12. All other Uncanny Power rules apply.


Precursor Touched (School of Ruins) (Knowledge), the patient reconstructionist. Other Mystics interpret revelations. You build a repeatable method from fragments, damaged machines, and the errors of the dead.

- Foundation, Persistent Inquiry (Passive). During every Long Rest, mark 1 segment on one active Domain Study Project without choosing Study the Archive as one of your Long Rest moves. You may still choose two other Long Rest moves normally.

- Specialization, Pattern Recognition (Passive). When you begin a Domain Study Project, reduce its clock by your Spellcast Trait modifier, to a minimum of 2 segments. Increasing the Trait later does not retroactively shorten an existing project.

- Mastery, Parallel Reconstruction (Passive). You may maintain two Domain Study Projects at the same time. Whenever you mark progress through Study the Archive, Persistent Inquiry, downtime, or a story reward, mark the same amount on both projects. While using Parallel Reconstruction, neither project benefits from Pattern Recognition; both use their normal clocks. You may instead maintain one reduced project normally.


### RESOLVE MOVES

**Class Moves**

- Calibrated Minor Ritual (spend and roll 1). Spend 10 uninterrupted minutes performing a documented group procedure. Roll the spent Resolve Die. Choose one Minor Ritual effect and a number of willing creatures up to your level + your Spellcast Trait modifier, minimum one. Every target must remain present throughout the procedure and receives the same chosen effect. The ritual lasts a number of hours equal to the Resolve Die result. It does not generate Fear and requires no Spellcast Roll. A creature can benefit from only one of your Calibrated Minor Rituals at a time; a new one replaces the old one.

 - **Group Calibration.** Choose Agility, Strength, Finesse, Knowledge, Instinct, or Presence. Every affected creature gains +1 to Rolls using that Trait. This does not modify damage, healing, Effort, Resolve, derived statistics, or the ritual's target limit.
 - **Group Adaptation.** Choose one specific environmental hazard examined or anticipated during the ritual, such as the radiation in this reactor, the pressure of this submerged facility, or the toxic spores of this organism. Every affected creature has Advantage on Rolls to resist, endure, or recover from that hazard. This does not grant immunity or prevent consequences that allow no resistance roll.
 - **Sustained Restoration.** At the end of every complete hour, every affected creature clears 1 marked HP. This cannot restore the dead, remove Scars, repair Armor Slots, or heal a creature while they are Dying. At any time while an affected creature is Dying, you may consume all remaining ritual duration and end the ritual for everyone to stabilize that creature. Stabilization clears all Dying and Final Progress but restores no HP.

- Uncanny Power (spend and roll 1+). Choose how many Resolve to spend, then roll one Resolve Die for each Resolve spent and add your Spellcast Trait once. The Keeper immediately gains 1 Fear for each Resolve spent, subject to the hard maximum of 12. The result is the maximum Domain level you can access, capped by your character level. After seeing the result, choose any Power from an unlocked Domain-level package whose level does not exceed that result.

 Invoking the Power takes a full Action and permits nothing else that turn. It cannot reproduce a Reaction or Passive Power. Ignore the Power's printed Hope cost and printed Spellcast Trait or DC, but pay any Stress, HP, material, frequency, or other printed cost. Make a Knowledge Spellcast Roll against **DC = 10 + the chosen Power's Level**, meaning the level of its unlocked Domain package. On success, resolve the Power normally. On failure, it does not manifest; the action and Resolve remain spent, and the Keeper retains all generated Fear.

 **Critical return.** On a Critical Success, the Power manifests and you immediately regain every Resolve spent on this use of Uncanny Power, up to your Resolve maximum. The Keeper retains the Fear already generated, and all non-Resolve costs remain paid.

### TECHNOLOGY ACCESS

Your class trains with the gear below; even at **Common (Tier 1)**, not every class is trained for every basic item (a Diplomat is not trained on rifles, and never becomes so). Using gear outside your access is at a penalty (Chapter 13), and Precursor (Tier 4) is story-gated.


| Access Tier | Level | Gear Categories |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Common (Tier 1) | 1 | Light Armor, Melee/Pistols, Neural/Physical Augments |
| Military (Tier 2) | 2 | Light Armor, Melee/Pistols, Neural/Physical Augments |
| Experimental (Tier 3) | 5 | Light Armor, Melee/Pistols, Neural/Physical Augments, now at Experimental grade |


:::class-emblem Pilot
:::

*Captain Vren Skykaja, twenty-year veteran of the Free Fleet*

### DESCRIPTION

The Sleeping Pilot is the version of the trade who does not lean on the Veil to read the lane. They lean on stick time. They lean on a panel they built or rebuilt themselves. They lean on the muscle memory of a thousand approach angles. They will out-fly an Awakened Pilot in clean conditions; they will lose, sometimes, in a Veil storm where the Awakened can *feel* the substrate's currents, but they will lose having read every gauge and called every adjustment, and they will come home anyway, because they trained for that storm too.

### CORE STATS

- **Domains:** Void & Tech

- **Spellcast Trait:** Instinct

- **Starting Evasion:** 11

- **Starting Hit Points:** 6

- **Class Items:** Personal Flight Chart Set · Worn Headset (the same one for fifteen years)


### EFFORT FEATURE: STICK TIME (2 EFFORT)

You can spend 2 Effort to choose one effect:

- **Hands on the Stick.** You have flown this lane, this approach, this maneuver before, and the ship is an extension of you. Choose one as you act: ignore one environmental penalty on your next piloting maneuver (a storm, a debris field, a failing instrument), **or** turn a Failure with Fear on a Finesse (Pilot/Navigate) Roll into an ordinary Failure, riding out the slip instead of crashing on it. Nobody flies this hull the way you do.

- **The Read.** Spend 1 minute studying a vessel, friendly or hostile, at standard Engagement range. The Keeper tells you its likely behavior over the next round, including any move it is about to make.

- **The Veteran's Burst.** During starship combat, declare that you and the ship execute a maneuver from your cumulative experience together. Gain **+2** on your next Pilot **Instinct** Roll this scene; after resolving it, clear **1 Heat**. This flat bonus does not create or stack with Advantage.

### CLASS FEATURE: THE SHIP KNOWS YOU

After you have flown the same vessel through one full mission arc, name **three** practiced maneuvers with the Keeper, such as threading debris, docking under pressure, holding a pursuit line, running silent, or emergency landing. When you make a **Finesse (Pilot/Navigate) Roll** for one of those maneuvers aboard that vessel, gain **+2**. During downtime after a mission, replace one named maneuver or add one until you know a maximum of **five**. This Feature never applies to weapon attacks, repairs, Presence Rolls made for social interaction, or Powers.

### BACKGROUND QUESTION

*What did the ship do, on the day you bonded with it, that nobody else has ever seen?*

### SUBCLASSES


Void Runner (Instinct), the smuggler with the cleaner record than the smugglers.

- Foundation, The Quiet Lane (Passive). In each reasonably familiar region, record one route that standard patrols do not watch. It remains unpatrolled until the crew uses it during a Failure with Fear or an established faction completes a surveillance clock covering that route; then cross it out and record a replacement only after a Long Rest spent surveying the region.

- Specialization, The Cold Run (Action). Spend 1 Effort. Your ship is, for the next hour, untraceable to standard scanning. (Specialized scanning still finds you; assume sensor parity with hostile capability.)

- Mastery, The Untouched Record (Passive). Your name does not appear in any standard Imperial or House record as a known smuggler. (The PEOPLE who know what you do, know. The systems do not.)


Combat Ace (Instinct), the dogfighter.

- Foundation, Wingman (Passive). When flying with at least one ally vessel, both vessels gain +1 to maneuver rolls.

- Specialization, The Tight Turn (Reaction). Spend 1 Effort when a hostile vessel places a pending Sensor Lock on your ship. The Lock ends immediately and the hostile vessel marks 1 Heat.

- Mastery, The Ace's Mark (Passive). You may claim, by named record, every kill you have made. The Sleeping Ace does not kill anonymously, the bodies are accounted for. You gain a fearsome reputation. NPC Pilots react to you accordingly; some flee, some seek you out.


System Jockey (Knowledge), the engineer-pilot. The Sleeping System Jockey knows the ship's wiring better than the engineer who installed it.

- Foundation, The Quick Repair (Action). Spend 1 Effort during starship combat. A damaged ship system goes from failed to limited functionality for the rest of the encounter.

- Specialization, The Modified Loadout (Passive). Your ship has one custom modification, declared at character creation, that no other ship has. The Keeper helps you decide what it is, and it is mechanically modest but narratively significant.

- Mastery, The Total Refit (Action). Once per story arc, after extensive downtime, you and your ship undergo a refit that grants permanent advancement: a new system, a doubled capacity, a hidden compartment. The refit is recorded as part of your ship's character.


### RESOLVE MOVES

**Class Moves**

- **Never Tell Me the Odds** *(spend 1)*. When a maneuver is called impossible or the odds are quoted, do it anyway: declare a quirk of this hull that makes it possible (a blind spot, a rattle before the stall, a tolerance the specs missed). The quirk is true and permanent. Roll with Advantage; on a Fear-dominant noncritical Roll, the ship pays, not the crew.

- **Hold Together** *(spend and roll 1+)*. Reduce the damage your ship takes this round by the rolled total, or keep a failing system online.

**Subclass Moves**

- **Void Runner, Lose the Tail** *(spend 1)*. When traffic, debris, terrain, or a previously established escape route is present, end one pending Sensor Lock on your ship or mark 1 segment on a visible escape clock. It cannot erase detection or end pursuit in open space without a viable route.

- **Combat Ace, Gun Run** *(spend and roll 1+)*. Add the rolled total to a ship-weapon attack; on a hit, it lands one threshold band higher.

- **System Jockey, Reroute Power** *(spend 1)*. This round, push one ship system (engines, weapons, or shields) past its rated limit.

### TECHNOLOGY ACCESS

Your class trains with the gear below; even at **Common (Tier 1)**, not every class is trained for every basic item (a Diplomat is not trained on rifles, and never becomes so). Using gear outside your access is at a penalty (Chapter 13), and Precursor (Tier 4) is story-gated.


| Access Tier | Level | Gear Categories |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Common (Tier 1) | 1 | Light/Medium Armor, Pistols/Rifles, All Augmentations |
| Military (Tier 2) | 2 | Light/Medium Armor, Pistols/Rifles/Heavy Weapons, All Augmentations |
| Experimental (Tier 3) | 5 | Light/Medium Armor, Pistols/Rifles/Heavy Weapons, All Augmentations, now at Experimental grade |


:::class-emblem Scholar
:::

*Archivist-Master Dorin Solari, on the occasion of his tenth Veritas Prize*

### DESCRIPTION

Sleeping Scholars are the Empire's institutional memory. Where Awakened Scholars sometimes have the eerie capacity to *feel* a fact's significance, a kind of substrate-aided intuition, the Sleeping kind work entirely from documents, citations, and patient cross-reference. They know more than the Awakened, on average, because they have read more. They cannot leap to conclusions; the leap is, for them, a methodological error.

### CORE STATS

- **Domains:** Tech & Social

- **Spellcast Trait:** Knowledge

- **Starting Evasion:** 10

- **Starting Hit Points:** 5

- **Class Items:** Citation Index *(your personal reference)* · Reading Glasses *(scratched, repaired, beloved)*


### EFFORT FEATURE: APPLIED SCIENCE (2 EFFORT)

You spend 2 Effort to choose one effect:

- **The Countdown.** When you study an ongoing poison, overload, collapse, pursuit, or similar process, the Keeper tells you how much time remains and one action that can slow it. If the process has no Clock, create a **four-segment Clock**; the Keeper states the consequence when it fills. This Feature reveals the process but does not remove segments itself.

- **The Improvised Reaction.** From materials in the scene, produce one immediate chemical effect: smoke, corrosion, adhesive, flash. One use, scene-length, never a weapon of war.

- **The Lost Source.** Declare one source relevant to the current investigation. It provides one partial answer, one named lead, or one complication that reframes known evidence. It cannot solve an active Clock, create equipment, or reveal an antagonist’s complete plan.

### CLASS FEATURE: THE OPEN QUESTION

Record one Question. During a Long Rest, you may work on it and make one Knowledge Roll using the normal Corebook difficulty procedure. After **three successful Knowledge Rolls** made during different Long Rests, the Question is answered. A Critical Success counts as one successful Roll for this Feature. When you record it, choose one reward: a named Contact, a verified lead, a Tier-appropriate schematic, or permission to attempt one project-related action without further research. It cannot grant a Domain, Power, Class Feature, permanent numeric bonus, or automatic success.

### BACKGROUND QUESTION

*What is your Question, and what do you fear you will find when you finally answer it?*

### SUBCLASSES


Xenobiologist (Knowledge), the documentarian of life.

- Foundation, The Catalog of Life (Passive). You have working classification competence with any biological organism you study for at least one minute. The Keeper provides phylum, hazard class, and one notable behavioral trait.

- Specialization, The Synthesis (Action). Spend 1 Effort with a sample or a minute of study of an organism: neutralize its toxin or spores for the crew this scene, or produce a lure that draws it where you choose, once.

- Mastery, The New Species (Passive). Once per story arc, you formally describe a new species. The description is published; future scenes acknowledge your authority on it; the Guild credits you. (This is the academic equivalent of slaying a dragon.)


Precursor Archaeologist (Knowledge), the dig-site discipline.

- Foundation, The Stratigraphic Eye (Passive). You can date Precursor structures by visual inspection alone, with at most a 200-year error.

- Specialization, As Built (Action). Spend 1 Effort studying a Precursor structure. The Keeper describes what it was built to do and how it worked; if it has a deactivation mechanism, you now know where it is. Reaching it is your problem.

- Mastery, The Site Report (Action). Once per story arc, you complete a definitive site report. The site is, from this point forward, understood; it does not stop being dangerous, but its history is no longer mysterious. Future scenes there resolve faster.


Information Theorist (Knowledge), the auditor of knowing.

- Foundation, The Source Critique (Passive). When presented with any document, recording, or testimony, you may, after one minute of inspection, ask the Keeper one question about its provenance: who made it, when, under what conditions, and with what likely biases.

- Specialization, The Model (Action). Spend 1 Effort modeling a system: a market, a patrol, a network, a crowd. Declare its behavior for the next hour absent intervention, and the Keeper adopts it; or inject one false datum the system treats as legitimate until audited.

- Mastery, The Settled Question (Action). Once per story arc, declare a contested historical question settled by your work. The settlement reverberates in the academic community; future scenes acknowledge the consensus you produced.


### RESOLVE MOVES

**Class Moves**

- **Analyze Weakness** *(spend 1)*. Study a foe or object and reveal a vulnerability that grants the crew Advantage against it for the scene.

- **I Have Read About This** *(spend and roll 1+)*. Add the rolled total to any Knowledge roll, and declare one true, useful fact into the scene.

**Subclass Moves**

- **Xenobiologist, Know the Beast** *(spend 1)*. Learn a creature's behavior, diet, threat pattern, and one weakness.

- **Precursor Archaeologist, Dig-Site Discipline** *(spend and roll 1+)*. Add the rolled total to a roll to safely excavate, date, or disarm a Vault feature. Your markers remain; the next team through follows them safely.

- **Information Theorist, Signal in the Noise** *(spend 1)*. Extract the true message from corrupted data, propaganda, or a flood of intel.

### TECHNOLOGY ACCESS

Your class trains with the gear below; even at **Common (Tier 1)**, not every class is trained for every basic item (a Diplomat is not trained on rifles, and never becomes so). Using gear outside your access is at a penalty (Chapter 13), and Precursor (Tier 4) is story-gated.


| Access Tier | Level | Gear Categories |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Common (Tier 1) | 1 | Light Armor, Pistols, Neural/Physical Augments, All Equipment |
| Military (Tier 2) | 2 | Light Armor, Pistols, Neural/Physical Augments, All Equipment |
| Experimental (Tier 3) | 5 | Light Armor, Pistols, Neural/Physical Augments, All Equipment, now at Experimental grade |


:::class-emblem Scoundrel
:::

Vex Tarrowmark, listed cause of death: unconfirmed

### DESCRIPTION

The Sleeping Scoundrel is the version of the trade who works on locks and ledgers and lies, not on the lucky cosmic shrug. They have not been blessed; they have been trained, often in places that no longer exist, by people who taught them to count exits. They are, on average, more careful than their Awakened counterparts. They tend to live longer.

### CORE STATS

- **Domains:** Social & Void

- **Spellcast Trait:** Finesse

- **Starting Evasion:** 12

- **Starting Hit Points:** 6

- **Class Items:** Lockpick Set · Several Identities (each with paperwork)


### EFFORT FEATURE: HANDS THAT KNOW (2 EFFORT)

You spend 2 Effort to choose one effect:

- **Cased the Joint.** Declare that you, or a previous version of yourself, has worked a job like *this* before. Name the target of a theft, a lock, or a mark; the Keeper tells you one concrete weakness, the guard's rhythm, the make of the lock, where the camera does not reach. You do not steal it for free, but you go in prepared: you have **Advantage** on the roll to pull the job, and the take is cleaner for knowing the way in.

- **The False Face.** Adopt one of your established alternate identities. NPCs who do not specifically know you under your true name accept the alternate identity for the duration of the scene.

- **The Backup Plan (once per scene).** After a plan fails or an obstacle is revealed, declare one prepared contingency: a common tool, a plausible exit or hiding place, a single useful fact, or one willing minor ally. The contingency gives **+2** to the crew’s next relevant Roll or permits one otherwise plausible approach. It cannot end a combat, erase a filled Clock, undo damage, produce Tiered gear, reveal a villain’s full plan, or force an NPC’s choice.

### CLASS FEATURE: THE QUIET NETWORK

**Sneak Attack.** When an Attack Roll with Advantage hits, add **1d6 damage** once to that attack. Add **2d6** at Tier 2 and **3d6** at Tier 3 instead. Any source of Advantage can arm Sneak Attack, but additional sources of Advantage do not increase its damage.

**The Quiet Network (once per session).** In a city, station, or region, declare one local contact. Choose one service: arrange a meeting, provide a safe place for one scene, identify a local opportunity or threat, or provide access to a routine local service. The contact may ask for payment or a future favor. They cannot provide Tiered gear, erase Heat, bypass major security, or solve an active Clock.

### BACKGROUND QUESTION

*What is the name on your real birth certificate, and who is still looking for you under that name?*

### SUBCLASSES


Assassin (Finesse), the closer.

- Foundation, The Quiet Approach (Passive). You can move silently in any environment that has reasonable cover. NPCs at standard alert do not notice your approach.

- Specialization, The Killing Stroke (Action). Spend 1 Effort. Your first attack of an encounter, against a target unaware of your presence, deals an additional 2d6 damage and ignores the first point of armor.

- Mastery, The Standing Contract (Passive). You hold a permanent contract that no living organization currently knows you hold. Its target is a specific named individual. The contract pays out, in full, on the day they die, by your hand or by another's, the contract does not specify. You may decide, at any point, to reveal your role.


Ghost (Finesse), the cipher.

- Foundation, Off the Record (Passive). You do not appear on any standard surveillance system. Specialized surveillance with proper procedure can find you; default systems cannot.

- Specialization, The Vanishing (Reaction). Spend 1 Effort. When you would be detected, captured, or photographed, you instead are not. The Keeper resolves how, narratively. Once per scene.

- Mastery, The Erased Record (Action). Once per story arc, declare that an existing piece of evidence about your activities, a security recording, a witness statement, a written note, has been erased. The Keeper helps you decide how it was done; it is now gone.


Contrabandist (Finesse), the courier of forbidden things.

- Foundation, The Hidden Compartment (Passive). Your kit, your ship, your room, wherever you live, has at least one compartment standard searches will miss.

- Specialization, The Established Route (Action). Spend 1 Effort. You move a piece of contraband through a checkpoint or border without being challenged. The route, once used, is logged by the relevant authority but may be reused with diminishing safety.

- Mastery, The Old Captain's Favor (Action). Once per story arc, call in a major favor from a senior Free Fleet, smuggler-cartel, or House-blacklist contact. The favor is significant, a ship, a passage, a name removed from a list, and is, after this use, repaid forever.


### RESOLVE MOVES

**Class Moves**

- **Vanish** *(spend 1)*. Break line of sight and leave a tense scene with no roll, to reappear where it will hurt them most.

- **The Long Con** *(spend 2)*. Plant a false belief or forged credential that holds up under one round of scrutiny.

**Subclass Moves**

- **Assassin, Killing Window** *(spend and roll 1+)*. Against an unaware or marked target, add the rolled total to the strike, and it lands one threshold band higher.

- **Ghost, Never Was Here** *(spend 1)*. Erase your presence from a scene after the fact: records, witnesses' certainty, sensor traces.

- **Contrabandist, False Bottom** *(spend 1)*. Produce a small forbidden item you "had stashed," or hide one from a search.

### TECHNOLOGY ACCESS

Your class trains with the gear below; even at **Common (Tier 1)**, not every class is trained for every basic item (a Diplomat is not trained on rifles, and never becomes so). Using gear outside your access is at a penalty (Chapter 13), and Precursor (Tier 4) is story-gated.


| Access Tier | Level | Gear Categories |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Common (Tier 1) | 1 | Light Armor, Melee/Pistols, Physical/Stealth Augments |
| Military (Tier 2) | 2 | Light Armor, Melee/Pistols/Rifles, Physical/Stealth Augments, Weapon Modifications |
| Experimental (Tier 3) | 5 | Light Armor, Melee/Pistols/Rifles, Physical/Stealth Augments, Weapon Modifications, now at Experimental grade |


:::class-emblem Soldier
:::

### DESCRIPTION

The Sleeping Soldier is, frankly, the version of the trade most veterans actually are. They don't believe the substrate has chosen them. They've been trained. They've drilled. They've lost people. They will lose more. The discipline is not glamorous; the discipline is what they have.

### CORE STATS

- **Domains:** Kinetic & Synthesis

- **Spellcast Trait:** Strength

- **Starting Evasion:** 9

- **Starting Hit Points:** 7

- **Class Items:** Dented Riot Shield · Fallen Comrade's Dog-tag

### EFFORT FEATURE: THE HELD LINE (1 EFFORT)

Spend 1 Effort after you successfully hit with an attack to deal an additional **1d6 damage**.

This is the smallest Effort cost among the Sleeping Class Features. The Soldier's discipline is meant to be used often rather than saved for a single decisive window: small, constant, and reliable.

### CLASS FEATURE: THE DRILL

Sleeping Soldiers turn repeated tactical procedures into reflex.

You automatically know all four **Common Drills**. Your subclass adds one Drill to your known repertoire at each subclass tier:

- **Foundation:** unlock its Foundation Drill.
- **Specialization:** unlock its Specialization Drill.
- **Mastery:** unlock its Mastery Drill.

At the beginning of each session, prepare **four Drills** from those you know.

**Using Drills.** An **Action** or **Reaction** Drill can be used once per scene while prepared. A **Passive** Drill is always active while prepared and does not track uses. Drills cost no resource unless their text says otherwise. Drills refresh when the scene ends. Unlocking more Drills does not increase the four prepared slots.

The subclass Drills are additional to the Soldier's existing subclass features.

#### COMMON DRILLS

**Covering Fire - Action.** Choose one ally within Close range and one visible enemy within Far range. The ally immediately moves one range band toward cover. Until the movement ends, the Keeper may still spend Fear to take the Spotlight and attack that ally, but the Attack Roll has Disadvantage. This Drill deals no damage.

**Breach and Clear - Action.** Open an ordinary door, hatch, window, or light barrier within Very Close range, then move through it. One willing ally within Very Close range may follow. You both gain Advantage on your next attack or Instinct Roll before your next Spotlight. A reinforced or secured barrier requires a Strength or Finesse Roll.

**Controlled Withdrawal - Action.** Choose one willing ally within Close range. You and that ally immediately move one range band away from the current threat. The ally does not use their Spotlight for this movement.

**Weapon Transition - Passive.** Switching to another equipped weapon does not use your Action. If your current action has not resolved, you may complete it with the new weapon.

### BACKGROUND QUESTION

*Whose name is on the dog-tag, and how did they die?*

### SUBCLASSES


Guardian (Strength), the wall between.

- Foundation, Bodyguard (Reaction). When an ally within Close range would take damage, you may step into the path. Take half the damage yourself; the ally takes none.

- Specialization, Hold Position (Action). Spend 1 Effort. Designate a position: a doorway, a corridor, or a wounded ally. Until you choose otherwise or you fall, no enemy may pass that position without succeeding on a Strength contest against you.

- Mastery, The Wall (Passive). Allies who fight within Close range of you have Advantage on resistance rolls and clear 1 Stress per scene. Your presence steadies people; this is observable training, not a cosmic effect.

**Guardian Drills**

- Foundation, Planted Stance (Reaction). When an effect would make you Prone or move you against your will, ignore that effect.

- Specialization, Casualty Extraction (Action). Choose one willing, Incapacitated, or Dying ally within Close range. Move to them, then move one range band with them. Until the movement ends, if the Keeper spends Fear to take the Spotlight and attack either of you, that attack has Disadvantage. This Drill does not heal, stabilize, or clear conditions.

- Mastery, Anchor the Line (Reaction). When an effect would make you or allies within Close range become Prone or move against their will, you and all affected allies within Close range ignore both effects.


Military Officer (Presence), the chain of command.

- Foundation, Rally (Action). Once per scene, allies within Close range each clear 1 Stress. You give an order; they remember why they are here.

- Specialization, Coordinated Strike (Action). Spend 1 Effort. You and one ally each take an action outside the ally's Spotlight. Both actions gain Advantage if they target the same enemy.

- Mastery, One Way Out (Action). Once per story arc, your voice organizes a group of non-combatant NPCs into coordinated action: an evacuation, a mutiny, or a work stoppage. They move as one while your voice holds.

**Military Officer Drills**

- Foundation, Tactical Reposition (Action). Choose up to two willing allies within Close range who can see or hear you. Each immediately moves one range band. This movement does not use their Spotlight.

- Specialization, Suppression Order (Action). Choose one visible enemy within Far range. Its next attack before your next Spotlight has Disadvantage.

- Mastery, Establish Fire Lane (Action). Designate a doorway, corridor, bridge, or clear line within Far range. Until your next Spotlight, each enemy crossing it becomes Vulnerable until the end of its next Spotlight.


Peacekeeper (Strength), the de-escalator.

- Foundation, Show of Force (Action). Display, without using, your weapon and authority. Hostile NPCs not specifically committed to violence retreat or stand down.

- Specialization, The Disarmament (Action). Spend 1 Effort during a tense scene. One armed NPC is convinced, through your demeanor, reputation, position, or all three, to lower their weapon for the duration of the scene. The standdown is real; betraying it has reputational cost.

- Mastery, The Cease-Fire (Action). Once per story arc, between two willing parties, you broker a cease-fire that the involved factions honor. The cease-fire's terms are negotiable; its existence is binding while you live.

**Peacekeeper Drills**

- Foundation, Safe Restraint (Passive). After succeeding on a Melee attack, you may deal no damage and apply Restrained instead, provided the target can be physically restrained.

- Specialization, Controlled Disarm (Passive). After succeeding on a Melee attack against a target holding a weapon, you may deal no damage and force it to drop one held weapon within Very Close range. Integrated or body-mounted weapons cannot be affected.

- Mastery, Evacuation Corridor (Action). Choose up to three willing non-combatants, or one Incapacitated or Dying ally, within Close range. They immediately move one range band toward an exit or cover. During this movement, selected characters have Advantage on rolls to cross, avoid, or resist hazardous terrain and environmental dangers, and any attack the Keeper makes against a selected character after spending Fear to take the Spotlight has Disadvantage. You may move with them, but you do not gain these benefits. This Drill does not remove hazards, heal, or stabilize.


### RESOLVE MOVES

**Class Moves**

- **Take the Hit** *(spend and roll 1+)*. When an ally within Close range is hit, intercept the attack. Reduce the damage by the rolled total and take any remaining damage yourself.

- **Disciplined Strike** *(spend and roll 1+)*. Add the rolled total to a damage roll. The target cannot spend Armor Slots against the added portion of this damage.

**Subclass Moves**

- **Guardian, Bulwark** *(spend and roll 1+)*. Grant one ally within Close range Armor Slots equal to the rolled total until the end of the scene. Unspent Armor Slots granted by this Move vanish when the scene ends.

- **Military Officer, Order the Line** *(spend 1)*. Choose one ally who can hear you. They immediately move one range band or make one attack outside their Spotlight. This does not consume their Reaction.

- **Peacekeeper, Stand Down** *(spend and roll 1+)*. Add the rolled total to a roll made to disarm, restrain, or de-escalate without killing. Word spreads that you ended it without blood.

### TECHNOLOGY ACCESS

Your class trains with the gear below; even at **Common (Tier 1)**, not every class is trained for every basic item (a Diplomat is not trained on rifles, and never becomes so). Using gear outside your access is at a penalty (Chapter 13), and Precursor (Tier 4) is story-gated.


| Access Tier | Level | Gear Categories |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Common (Tier 1) | 1 | All Armor, All Weapons, Physical Augments |
| Military (Tier 2) | 2 | All Armor, All Weapons, Physical Augments |
| Experimental (Tier 3) | 5 | All Armor, All Weapons, Physical Augments, now at Experimental grade |


:::class-emblem Vanguard
:::

*"The body is the strike. The mind is the line of the strike. There is no daylight between them. The Frequency does not enter into it. The Frequency entered into it, briefly, when I was nineteen, and I sent it away. I have my discipline."*

*Master Vanguard Tenshi-Ko, on the discipline of Refusal*

### DESCRIPTION

The Sleeping Vanguard is the version of the trade who has *deliberately closed* themselves to the substrate. Where the Awakened Vanguard fuses mind and body in the substrate's currents, the Sleeping Vanguard fuses them in *practice*, a discipline learned, drilled, and maintained without cosmic aid. Sleeping Vanguards are often *Refused*: characters who once heard the Frequency and chose, for personal or philosophical reasons, to stop listening. The discipline is more austere as a result. It is also more reliable.

**Core rules note - Refused histories.** *Refused* may be used as a background or identity for a character who begins play Sleeping. It is not a voluntary in-campaign Path transition: the Core provides no procedure for an Awakened character to choose Sleeping.

Watch one work and you will doubt the word *Sleeping*. They run up walls that should not be run up. They cross water that should not hold them. They fall five stories and land on one knee, in silence. None of it is the Veil. All of it has been rehearsed ten thousand times, and that is the point: the Awakened bend the world; the Sleeping Vanguard has rehearsed the world until they know its seams.

### CORE STATS

- **Domains:** Neural & branch *(Void / Kinetic / Lux, determined by Subclass)*
- **Spellcast Trait:** Presence
- **Starting Evasion:** 11
- **Starting Hit Points:** 6
- **Class Items:** Light Staff *(Melee)* · Meditation Orb *(unilluminated; the Sleeping Vanguard's orb does not glow)* · Spiced Tea Mix

### EFFORT FEATURE: THE REFUSED PATH (2 EFFORT)

Spend 2 Effort to enter the **Disciplined State**. As you enter, set your **Integrity Die** to its highest face by Tier: a **d4** at Tier 1, a **d6** at Tier 2, or a **d8** at Tier 3 or higher.

Choose **Agility, Instinct, or Strength** as you enter. For the duration:

- You have Advantage on rolls using the chosen Trait.
- Add the chosen Trait's modifier to your Melee and unarmed damage rolls.
- You are immune to Stunned and Dazed.
- Your first Melee attack against an enemy during the state deals an additional **2d6 damage** of your subclass branch type: Void, Kinetic, or Lux.
- After the first Melee attack made against you each round, subsequent Melee attacks against you that round have Disadvantage while at least two enemies are within Melee range of you.

Each time you roll with Fear during the state (including on a Reaction), reduce your Integrity Die by 1; it is never reduced on matching dice. The state ends when your Integrity Die reaches 0 or when the scene ends, whichever comes first.

**Breaking Point.** At any point during the state, you may end it as a free effect on your action to unleash a closing strike: that action deals an additional **(Proficiency)d6** damage of your subclass branch type (Void, Kinetic, or Lux). This bonus is added once, after any multipliers, and is never doubled on a Critical.

The discipline is a focus, not total superiority: you sharpen one line of your craft and hold it. The substrate does not become more cooperative; you become more present.

### CLASS FEATURES

**Trained Body.** Your unarmed strikes are Melee weapons using Strength or Agility, chosen at character creation, and deal **d6 physical damage**. They cannot be disarmed or confiscated. At the Tier 2 Achievement, Level 5, the damage die becomes **d8**. At the Tier 3 Achievement, Level 8, it becomes **d10**. Proficiency applies normally.

If your ancestry grants natural weapons or alters your unarmed damage type, retain that damage type and treat results of 1 or 2 on your unarmed damage dice as 3.

**Unbroken Focus.** Your mental discipline channels internal force into movement, combat, and refusal.

- While not wearing Heavy or Very Heavy armor, gain **+1 Evasion**.
- Once per scene, when you would mark Stress, spend 1 Effort and briefly meditate. The Stress is not marked. This does not use your Action.

**The Refusal - Reaction.** Once per scene, when you or an ally within Close range would be affected by a Domain Power or Veil phenomenon that calls for an attack or Spellcast Roll, or allows a Reaction Roll, spend 1 Effort. Apply Disadvantage to the attack or Spellcast Roll, or grant Advantage on the Reaction Roll.

### BACKGROUND QUESTION

*The substrate offered itself to you. You said no. Why?*

### SUBCLASSES


Ghost Blade (+Void) (Finesse), the discipline of stillness.

- Foundation, The Quiet Strike (Passive). Once per scene, when you make a Melee attack while Hidden, the attack ignores 1 Armor Slot.

- Specialization, The Folded Step (Action). Spend 1 Effort. Move to available cover within Close range and become Hidden. This is not phasing; you have rehearsed this movement for years.

- Mastery, The Folded Exit (Action). Once per scene, after a successful Melee attack, move from Very Close to Close range toward available cover. Until your next Spotlight, attacks against you have Disadvantage.


Kinetic Echo (+Kinetic) (Strength), the discipline of force.

- Foundation, Body Memory (Passive). Choose one kind of physical feat you have drilled to mastery, such as a specific climb, throw, or landing. You perform that feat without rolling in routine conditions only: no active opposition, no time pressure, and no real risk. When the feat is contested, rushed, or dangerous, roll normally.

- Specialization, The Channeled Blow (Action). Spend 1 Effort. Your next Melee attack deals an additional 1d8 Kinetic damage. On a success, move the target one range band directly away from you.

- Mastery, The Settled Ground (Passive). Once per scene, after a successful Melee attack, apply Dazed to the target.


Pure Conduit (+Lux) (Presence), the discipline of clarity. The Sleeping Pure Conduit's Lux is not divine reception; it is attention so total it produces light. The orb does not illuminate. The Vanguard does.

- Foundation, The Cleared Room (Action). Spend 1 Effort. For the next minute, you and allies within Close range have Advantage on rolls made to resist or clear Frightened, Confused, and Veil-induced deception.

- Specialization, The Held Truth (Action). Spend 1 Effort during a social or interrogation scene. NPCs who knowingly lie to you mark 1 Stress. NPCs who tell you a painful truth clear 1 Stress. Your presence does this without your speaking.

- Mastery, The Cleared Path (Passive). While you remain at a location affected by deception, illusion, or Veil-induced confusion, you and allies within Close range have Advantage on rolls made against those effects.


### RESOLVE MOVES

**Class Moves**

- **The Weightless Art** *(spend and roll 1)*. For the rolled total in rounds, your ki makes the world your floor: walls, water, cables, and the heads of a crowd. You fall without sound or harm, and your leaps cross one additional range band. This is motion, never flight: every step begins and ends on something.

- **Falling Star** *(spend and roll 1+)*. Close one range band, descending or leaping if the approach allows it, and attack. Add the rolled total to the damage. If you arrived from above, the strike deals your branch's damage type - Void, Kinetic, or Lux - instead of physical, and treats the target's Major and Severe Thresholds as 4 lower for this hit. This penetration replaces and never stacks with the damage type's own penetration effect.

**Subclass Moves**

- **Ghost Blade, Stillness** *(spend 1)*. Until your next Spotlight, you cannot be targeted by an attack that requires seeing you. You are simply not where the eye expects.

- **Kinetic Echo, Shockwave** *(spend and roll 1+)*. Your next Melee hit adds the rolled total to its damage. Then choose one: move the target one range band directly away from you, or apply Prone.

- **Pure Conduit, Burning Focus** *(spend 1)*. Until your next Spotlight, you shed light nothing can hide from. Enemies within Close range cannot benefit from Hidden against you.

> **GEAR, THE INNER NAME.** Vanguard traditions do not call it Resolve. They call it breath, ki, the coiled line, the weight that is not weight. The Corebook takes no position on whether internal energy exists. The Vanguard takes one. When a Sleeping Vanguard spends Resolve, ask the player what their tradition calls it, and use that word at the table.

### TECHNOLOGY ACCESS

Your class trains with the gear below; even at **Common (Tier 1)**, not every class is trained for every basic item (a Diplomat is not trained on rifles, and never becomes so). Using gear outside your access is at a penalty (Chapter 13), and Precursor (Tier 4) is story-gated.


| Access Tier | Level | Gear Categories |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Common (Tier 1) | 1 | Light/Medium Armor, Melee/Pistols, Neural Augments |
| Military (Tier 2) | 2 | Light/Medium Armor (excluding Heavy/Very Heavy features), Melee/Pistols/Rifles (excluding Massive feature), Neural Augments |
| Experimental (Tier 3) | 5 | Light/Medium Armor (excluding Heavy/Very Heavy features), Melee/Pistols/Rifles (excluding Massive feature), Neural Augments, now at Experimental grade |

## AWAKENING IN PLAY

Awakening is the only Path transition presented in the Core. A Sleeping character Awakens when a campaign event establishes that they can perceive and answer the Hope Frequency. This is a story event recognized by the Keeper and resolved during downtime; it is not an Advancement Slot option and cannot be selected solely for mechanical benefit.

When a Sleeping character Awakens:

- Replace the **Effort Track and Effort pool** with **Hope**. Their current Effort becomes their current Hope, up to the same maximum.
- Retire the **Resolve pool**, every Resolve Move, **Honed Edge**, and the Sleeping rule that invokes Experiences for free. Existing Experiences remain, but the character now spends Hope to invoke them under the normal Awakened procedure.
- Retire the **Recovery Anchor**.
- Replace the primary Class's **Effort Feature** and **Class Feature** with the corresponding **Hope Feature** and **Class Feature** from Chapter 6.
- Preserve the Class, Background answer, Subclass choice, and Subclass upgrade tier. Use the corresponding Awakened Subclass: **The Steward** becomes **The Icon**, and the other base Subclass names map directly.
- Open the Awakened **Vault and Loadout** and gain the normal starter pair of **two Level 1 Domain Powers** from the primary Class's accessible Domains.
- Refund every Advancement Slot previously spent on the Sleeping choices of Option 8 or on **Tempered Resolve**, then re-spend those Slots under the Awakened options in Chapter 12. All path-neutral advancement remains unchanged.

If the character multiclassed while Sleeping, their secondary Effort Feature becomes the corresponding Hope Feature, their one secondary Class Resolve Move is retired, and their recorded **Dormant Domain** becomes an active third Domain. This conversion costs no Slot and grants no starter Powers from the third Domain; its Powers must be acquired normally through advancement. The second Class still grants no separate Class Feature, Subclass, Class Items, or starter Loadout.

The Core provides no ordinary procedure for an Awakened character to become Sleeping. Exceptional reversals are Keeper-facing options, triggered only by specific campaign events.

# CHAPTER 8: FORGING A VOIDWALKER

*"You are not making a hero. You are making a person who will, sometimes, choose to do heroic things. Spend*

*the time on the person."*

*Old Keeper's note, Spire of Verita game library*

A Veilfarers character is a person with a job, a wound, a name, and a relationship to the Veil that is either *yes, I hear it* or *no, I do not*. The numbers describe that person; they do not invent them. This chapter is the procedure for building one. It takes most groups thirty to ninety minutes.

***At a glance. Six steps build the character: 1 Ancestry, 2 Community, 3 Path, Class & Subclass, 4 Traits,*** *5 Experiences, 6 Affiliation. Then a short set of finishing touches (Loadout or equipment, Connections, resource pools, name and look) makes them ready to play. Read this chapter once end to end, then work the steps with your sheet open. Fill the sheet in last; build the character in your head and notebook first.*

Each step below gives you the same three things: *what it decides*, *the action to take*, and *one tip*. The deep material for each choice lives in its own chapter; this chapter is the assembly line, not the encyclopedia.

## THE SIX STEPS

### STEP 1, ANCESTRY: THE BODY YOU WALK IN

**What it decides.** Your body type, one or more always-on **Ancestry Features**, the d6 complication table that shapes how you fail when Fear dominates, and the social texture the galaxy reads you through.

**The action.** Choose one of the nine ancestries in Chapter 3 (Ailuran, Bloomstrider, Celestiari, Ethereal, Human, Kryllian, Kryx, Rift Spinner, Synthetic) and note it at the top of your sheet. Ancestry does not lock your Class or Path: any ancestry can be any class on either path.

**Tip.** Pick the ancestry whose *complication table* you want to play. What your failures feel like defines a character more than what their successes do.

*Example. Maren wants a character whose feelings betray her at the worst moment, so she picks Celestiari: her Aural Light flares when she is afraid, and her complications are all things that happen when she lights up.*

### STEP 2, COMMUNITY: THE WORLD THAT SHAPED YOU

**What it decides.** A **Community Feature**, a default attitude toward galactic institutions, and your first social network.

**The action.** Choose one of the seven communities in Chapter 4 (Core World, Trade Hub, Frontier Colony, Void Station, Free Fleet, AgriSynth, Hidden Enclave) and note it under your ancestry. Community is your *origin*, not your current address; a Core World child can grow up to smuggle for the Free Fleet.

**Tip.** "Where did this character grow up?" is the same question as "what does this character think is normal?" Answer that and the rest of the build gets easier.

*Example. Maren chooses Free Fleet: she grew up aboard the freighter she now flies, which gives her Wayfinding and makes her loyal to crews and wary of Houses before she has said a word.*

### STEP 3, PATH, CLASS, AND SUBCLASS: THE RESPONSE, THE WORK, AND THE EDGE

The largest step, in three parts.

**3A, the Path.** Choose **Awakened** (you hear the Hope Frequency; your resource is **Hope**, spent on Domain Powers and your Class Feature, Chapter 6) or **Sleeping** (you are deaf to it, or refused it; your everyday resource is **Effort**, and you also draw on a scarce **Resolve** pool for signature Moves, Chapter 7). The full case for each path is in Chapter 2; do not re-decide it here, just record it. (Mystic is the one class where Path changes the Spellcast Trait: Knowledge for Sleeping, Instinct for Awakened, so plan your array accordingly.)

**3C, the Subclass.** Each class has three subclasses, each with a Foundation feature (level 1), a Specialization (Tier 2), and a Mastery (Tier 3). The subclass sets the texture of your abilities and, for some classes, locks a second Domain (most notably the Vanguard). Pick the future you want to play toward.

**Record:** Class, Path, Subclass.


**3B, the Class.** Choose one of the nine classes (full write-ups in Chapter 6 for Awakened, Chapter 7 for Sleeping). The class is the *work*: the role you cut when you walk into a scene. Each class has a Domain Pair and a Spellcast Trait, the Trait most of its signature actions use.

| CLASS | DOMAINS | SIGNATURE TRAIT |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Diplomat** | Social & Lux | Presence |
| **Engineer** | Tech & Synthesis | Knowledge |
| **Explorer** | Synthesis & Lux | Instinct |
| **Mystic** | Neural & Lux *or* Void | Instinct (Awakened) / Knowledge (Sleeping) |
| **Pilot** | Void & Tech | Instinct |
| **Scholar** | Tech & Social | Knowledge |
| **Scoundrel** | Social & Void | Finesse |
| **Soldier** | Kinetic & Synthesis | Strength |
| **Vanguard** | Neural & branch (Void / Kinetic / Lux) | Presence |

*Example. Maren is a Pilot, Awakened, Void Runner. She has felt the lanes hum since she was sixteen, so the Awakened path and the Void domain fit her; Void Runner is the smuggler-pilot she already is. Her Spellcast Trait is Instinct.*

### STEP 4, TRAITS: THE MEASURE OF YOUR POTENTIAL

The six Traits are **Agility, Strength, Finesse, Knowledge, Instinct, Presence**. Three canonical Subtraits name specialized applications without creating additional Traits: **Pilot/Navigate** is parented to **Finesse**, while **Tech** and **Medicine** are parented to **Knowledge**. A Subtrait always uses its parent Trait score unless a feature explicitly says otherwise. Every character assigns the same fixed array, one value per Trait:

**+2, +1, +1, +0, +0, -1**

**The action.** Put your **+2** on your **Signature Trait** (for the Awakened this is the Spellcast Trait; it powers your class engine), your **+1s** on your secondary class Trait and a Trait your Ancestry or Community uses, your **+0s** on utility, and your **-1** somewhere deliberate.

**Tip.** The -1 is a feature, not a flaw. The Diplomat with Strength -1 who cannot drag a wounded friend clear is *forged* by the moments they could not. Lean into it.

*Example. Maren puts +2 on Instinct (her Spellcast Trait), +1 on Finesse and Knowledge, +0 on Agility and Strength, and her -1 on Presence: she has never been the one who sweet-talks the customs desk.*

### STEP 5, EXPERIENCES: THE MEMORIES THAT DEFINE YOU

An **Experience** is a short, evocative phrase naming a defining moment, period, or skill from before play, *I held the line at Titan Station for 72 hours*, *Quantum Savant*, *I charted the Crimson Veil and lost a wingman doing it*.

**How they work.** A starting **Awakened** character has **two Experiences at +2** and invokes one by spending **1 Hope** to add its flat bonus to a relevant roll (a flat number, not advantage). A starting **Sleeping** character has **three Experiences at +2** and invokes them **free** (no resource), per the Sleeping engine in Chapter 7. Experiences rise with advancement (Chapter 12); new ones earned in play start at +1, and a character holds at most five.

**The action.** Choose your starting Experiences. Make each one **personal** (yours, not a generic skill), **applicable** (usable in more than one kind of scene), and **costly** (the best ones carry a wound or a debt the Keeper can pull on). Vary the Traits they apply to.

**Tip.** A good Experience gives the Keeper a hook. *I brokered the peace at Hydros* is fine; *I brokered the peace at Hydros, and it cost me my sister* is a campaign.

*Example. Maren takes "First to chart the Crimson Veil Storm, and I lost Iruvi doing it" (+2, the wound) and "Free Fleet Lifer, twenty years on one hull" (+2, the broad one). As an Awakened pilot she invokes either by spending 1 Hope.*

### STEP 6, AFFILIATION: THE INSTITUTION YOU ANSWER TO

**What it decides.** Your one **primary affiliation** sits on top of Community (where you came from) and defines who you answer to now. It grants three benefits and three obligations, all of which apply at the table.

- **Benefits:** equipment access within the affiliation's domain without a Wealth Check, up to one Tier above yours; starting **Affiliation Standing +1 (Good Standing)**; and **one Call per session**. A Call provides one Tier-appropriate fact, introduction, temporary safe place, or Common item. A Military item or direct intervention costs 1 Standing after it resolves. Anything larger requires a visible project and is not a Call.

- **Obligations:** periodic **dues**; occasional **calls** the institution makes on you; and **forbidden conflicts** that cost Standing if you commit them.

**Standing** runs +5 to -5 and starts at **+1 (Good Standing)**; the full Standing and recovery rules live in Chapter 16, and each affiliation's specific domain, dues, and conflicts are detailed in Chapter 5.

**The action.** Choose one: **House Amaranth, Joric, Kurogane, Solari, Valerius, or Volkov**; the **Free Fleet** or **Explorers' Guild**; or **Independent**. Two further affiliations, the **Solara Compact** and the **Stellar Commerce Guild**, are profiled in the Keeper's Companion and available as advanced options with the Keeper's approval. Independent is a real choice, not a fallback: it trades all three benefits for an **Independent Favor Pool** of 1 Favor token per session to call on improvised contacts, and carries no dues, conflicts, or Standing erosion.

**Tip.** Match your affiliation to your Community for a grounded professional; mismatch them deliberately for built-in tension.

*Example. Maren stays Free Fleet (Standing +1): ship parts and salvage without a Wealth Check, one Call to the Fleet each session, and the standing obligation never to leave another Fleet ship in distress.*

## FINISHING TOUCHES

The six steps make a character playable. These make them ready.

**Loadout and equipment.** Awakened characters take a **Starter Loadout** of **two Level 1 Domain Powers**, chosen from the **six** available to their class's two Domains, three per Domain (each class entry suggests a first pair; the catalog is Chapter 19). Every character takes their class's **Class Items**, plus one Tier 1 weapon and one armor piece (Chapter 13), a small kit of three to five personal objects that are *theirs*, and a starting **Wealth Tier of 0 or 1** (Chapter 15; the low tiers are deliberate).

**Resource pools.** Fill in **HP** and **Evasion** (class entry, plus Ancestry and Subclass modifiers), **6 Stress slots** (Synthetics 7), **Hope or Effort** (Awakened begin each session with 2 Hope; Sleeping begin play with 2 Effort and thereafter keep it between sessions; both cap at 6), **Resolve** for Sleeping characters (base 2, rising by 1 at levels 3, 5, 7 and 9; Chapter 7), and **Armor Slots** from your armor.

**Recovery Anchor (Sleeping only).** Define a **specific, lose-able, refusable** item, place, or ritual your character uses to recover, and name it here; everything about how Recovery works, including what the Anchor does and what losing it costs, lives in Chapter 7. Make it specific enough that the table can take it from you when the story needs the weight.

**Name, look, voice.** A name in two or three parts; three or four sentences of appearance; one or two sentences on how they speak. Voice is the fastest way to make a character distinct at the table; settle it before session one.

### CREW STEP: CONNECTIONS, TURNING CHARACTERS INTO A CREW

After everyone has built through Step 5, the table answers three questions together (fifteen to thirty minutes). Each names a *different* other PC, so in a four-person crew you have an explicit relationship to all three crewmates. Connections are dynamic and can change in play.

**First Bond, your closest crewmate.** Reciprocal. Both players gain **+1 Hope/Effort** at session start (on top of the standard reset, never above your normal maximum). For a Sleeping character, this is the named Connection exception to the ordinary Effort Track rule in Chapter 7. Once per scene, when both are present, one may spend 1 Hope/Effort to give the other +1 to a roll. And when your Bond is dying, you may move to their side with no roll, provided you are in the same scene and a path exists your character could take; it will not carry you through sealed bulkheads, hard vacuum, or impossible geography without the Keeper's blessing, the

one mechanic in the game that bypasses range bands. A Bond breaks only on real betrayal, not ordinary friction.

**Open Debt, someone you owe.** One-directional. Once per session the creditor may **call the Debt** to push the debtor toward an action within the obligation's scope; refusing marks 2 Stress and partially repays it. Significant service repays it too; two or three repayments clear it.

**Friction, someone who gets under your skin.** One-directional. When you act *despite* the Friction (defer, cooperate, hold your tongue), you gain **+1 Hope/Effort** at scene's end (capped at your maximum). For a Sleeping character, this is the named Connection exception to the ordinary Effort Track rule in Chapter 7. Once per session the Keeper may activate it for a short played-out clash, after which both characters gain +1 Hope/Effort. Frictions are meant to stay productive for most of a campaign, not resolve quickly.

## MAREN'S FINISHED SHEET

The running example, assembled: **Maren Solas**, Celestiari Pilot, Awakened, Void Runner, Free Fleet. Instinct +2, Finesse +1, Knowledge +1, Agility +0, Strength +0, Presence -1. Experiences: *First to chart the Crimson Veil Storm, and I lost Iruvi doing it* (+2), *Free Fleet Lifer* (+2). Starter Loadout of two Level 1 Void/Tech Powers; flight jacket and a photo of the lost crew in her kit; Wealth Tier 1; Standing +1 with the Fleet. First Bond: the *Vagrant Star*'s engineer. Friction: the new pilot the captain hired without asking her. One conversation, start to finish.

## TWO MORE, IN BRIEF

- **Doctor Skarrh's Apprentice (Sleeping Mystic).** Ethereal, Core World, Mystic / Sleeping / Veil Walker. Spellcast Trait Knowledge. Her starting Uncanny Archive contains Lux 1 and Neural 1, so she knows every Level 1 Power in both Paths. She supports the crew through Calibrated Minor Rituals and forces full Powers through Uncanny Power, generating Fear each time she opens the connection. Knowledge +2, Instinct +1, Finesse +1, Presence +0, Agility +0, Strength -1. Three Experiences (Sleeping) including *I catalogued a Class III Vault that killed the rest of my expedition*. Recovery Anchor: her late mentor's annotated field journal. Affiliation: House Amaranth.

- **The Quiet Mechanic of the Pelican (Sleeping** **Engineer).** Bloomstrider, AgriSynth, Engineer / Sleeping / Tech Specialist. Knowledge +2, Finesse +1, Instinct +1, Strength +0, Presence +0, Agility -1. Effort plus Resolve; the *Field Improvisation* and *Hot-Wire* Moves are their signature. Recovery Anchor: the specific socket wrench that came off their first ship. Affiliation: Free Fleet. Open Debt to the captain who pulled them out of indenture.

## QUICK-START ARCHETYPES

For one-shots and new players, the Veilfarers archetypes are complete pre-builds: **Void Runner** (Celestiari Pilot), **Corporate Enforcer** (Human Soldier), **Relic Seeker** (Ethereal Scholar), **Street Medic** (Kryllian Engineer), **Trade Ambassador** (Human Diplomat), **Veil Touched** (Celestiari Mystic), **Info Broker** (Synthetic Scoundrel), **The Whisper Broker** (Ailuran Explorer), **The Gray Bolt** (Ailuran Soldier). Each is built Awakened. To convert one to Sleeping, keep its ancestry, concept, Traits, Connections, and legal gear, then rebuild its Path package from the matching Sleeping class entry in Chapter 7: replace the Hope Feature with the Effort Feature, apply Honed Edge, take the Sleeping character's three Experiences, set Resolve and its Class Resolve Moves, and name a Recovery Anchor. Do not carry over a Vault, Loadout, or Domain Powers; the Sleeping Mystic uses its own Uncanny Archive procedure. This is a five-minute character-creation rebuild, performed before play with the Chapter 7 class entry open at the table; it is not an in-campaign Path transition.

## COMMON PITFALLS

- **The optimization puzzle.** The array is balanced; don't agonize. Put +2 on your Spellcast Trait and move on.

- **The encyclopedic backstory.** Two sharp Experiences beat ten pages of history. Leave room for play to write the rest.

- **The forgotten wound.** A character with nothing to lose is hard to move. Give at least one Experience a cost.

- **The lone wolf.** This is a crew game. Take your three Connections seriously; a character with no bonds starves the table.

- **The Sleeping character without an anchor.** Define a real Recovery Anchor, specific and lose-able. A vague one does nothing in play.

- **The unfocused Mystic.** Pick one Domain alignment and lean in. Trying to do everything does none of it well.

## BUILDING A CREW

A working crew mixes paths, roles, and origins, the Awakened reaching across, the Sleeping holding the line. Aim for coverage (someone who fights, someone who talks, someone who fixes, someone who reads the room) without forcing it; the gaps are where stories start. What a crew argues about is as defining as what it agrees on. Build the people, let the friction be real, and the crew assembles itself.

### THE FINAL CHECKLIST

Before the first session, run the sheet once more, top to bottom:

- **Path** chosen (Awakened or Sleeping), and you know what your path resource is.
- **Ancestry** and **Community** chosen, Gifts and Benefit noted.
- **Class** and **Subclass** chosen; Foundation feature written down.
- **Traits** assigned (+2 on your Signature Trait unless you had a strong reason not to).
- **Experiences** written as sentences with a voice, at +2: two if Awakened, three if Sleeping.
- **Affiliation** chosen (or Independent), Obligation and first Benefit noted.
- **Powers or Moves:** Awakened, your 2 Level 1 Domain Powers; Sleeping, your Resolve pool and Moves, and your **Recovery Anchor** named.
- **Resource pools** set: HP, Stress, Evasion, Armor, Hope cap or Effort Track, Proficiency.
- **Crew step:** three Connections answered, each naming a different crewmate.
- **Name, look,** and the small kit of objects that are *yours*.

# CHAPTER 9: HOW TO PLAY

*"I have taught five generations of Pearl Drive engineers. Every single one has wanted, at some point, a button that simply makes things go right. The system does not have one. The system has dice. The dice are not a*

*button. They are a question."*

*Master Engineer Jiro Kurogane Aimei, Hydros Yards, instruction manual preface*

This chapter teaches you how to play *Veilfarers* at a table.

**At a glance.** Every meaningful player action resolves with a **Duality Roll**: roll **2d12** (one Hope die, one Fear die), add one **Trait modifier** (-1 to +2), and compare the total with the **Difficulty Class** (DC). On a noncritical player Roll, Hope dominance grants the appropriate Path progress and Fear dominance gives the Keeper 1 Fear, subject to the hard maximum of 12. Matching dice always produce a Critical Success. Keeper-controlled combat attacks also use Duality Dice, but nonmatching dominance grants no resource. A noncritical Roll succeeds when its total meets or exceeds the DC and fails when it does not. Trivial, repeated, or consequence-free actions do not generate Hope, mark Effort, or generate Fear.

| PATH | RESOURCE | HOW IT IS GAINED | WHAT IT FUELS |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Awakened** | **Hope** (cap 6) | 1 per Hope-dominant meaningful roll | Experiences, class features, Domain Powers |
| **Sleeping** | **Effort** | The two-segment **Effort Track** (Chapter 7) | Effort Features; Experiences are free |


The previous chapters built the world. The chapters after this one will build your character. This chapter sits between them and explains the *interface*, the procedure by which the world and the character meet. When does your character roll dice? Which dice? How do you read the result? What happens after? These are the questions every working session at every *Veilfarers* table will need to answer, and they are the questions this chapter answers.

The system rests on a single resolution mechanic, the **Duality Roll** and a small number of resources that flow in and out of player and Keeper hands as the session progresses. Once you understand the Duality Roll and the resources, you understand how *Veilfarers* works. Combat, ship operations, character advancement, and Domain Powers are all extensions of the same simple procedure. You are about to learn the procedure.

Read this chapter all the way through on a first pass. Then refer back to specific sections as needed during play.

## FICTION FIRST

The most important rule in *Veilfarers* is the rule that comes before any of the dice rules.

You do not roll dice for things that do not matter.

A character who picks up a glass to drink from it does not roll a check. A character who walks across a room does not roll a check. A character who is alone in their cabin and decides to take a nap does not roll a check. The system has nothing to say about these moments, because the system is designed to handle moments where *something is at stake*.

A character who picks up a glass to drink from it *while suspecting it may be poisoned*, that is a moment where the system has something to say. A character who walks across a room *while a sniper is watching* is a moment for

the system. A character who tries to sleep *in a hostile environment* is a moment for the system.

The Keeper's first job, before any dice are picked up, is to recognize which moments are at stake and which are not. A common failure mode at new tables is to call for too many rolls, turning every minor action into a check, slowing the session down, and accidentally telling the players that the world is more dangerous and uncertain than the fiction warrants. Resist this. Most actions in *Veilfarers* resolve through narration alone. The dice exist for the moments where *the outcome is meaningfully uncertain* and *the consequences of failure or partial success would change the story*.

A useful test: if both success and failure would lead to a story you want to tell, call for the roll. If only one outcome is interesting, just narrate it. The roll is not a tax on action. The roll is a tool for handling moments where the table genuinely does not know what happens next.

This principle, *fiction first*, runs through every other rule in this book. Fiction determines whether a rule triggers, what it means, and how it looks. It does not silently alter the published procedure. A table may agree to a house rule, but it must name that change as a house rule; the system canon remains unchanged.

## THE DUALITY ROLL

When the Keeper calls for a check, the player rolls **two twelve-sided dice**.

One of these is the **Hope die**. The other is the **Fear die**. The dice are physically identical except for color or marking, many tables use a gold or white die for Hope and a red or black die for Fear. Some tables use any two d12s and just declare which is which before the roll. The dice do not need to be labeled by the manufacturer. They need to be distinguishable to the players.

The player rolls both dice at once. The procedure that follows is:

1. **Add the two dice together.** This is the **base total**.
2. **Add any relevant modifiers.** Most rolls add a Trait - Agility, Strength, Finesse, Knowledge, Instinct, or Presence - depending on what the action is. Other modifiers may apply: Experience bonuses (if invoked), situational adjustments, Advantage or Disadvantage dice (covered later in this chapter).
3. **Compare the final total to the Difficulty Class.** The Keeper fixes the DC before the dice come to rest. The Keeper may keep that DC hidden, but may not change it after seeing the roll.
4. **Look at which die is higher.** If the Hope die is higher than the Fear die, the result is **Hope-favored**. If the Fear die is higher, the result is **Fear-favored**. If both dice show the same number, the result is a **Critical Success**.

This produces five possible outcomes from a single roll, explained in detail in the next section.

> **QUICK PROCEDURE - THE DUALITY ROLL**
>
> | | HOPE > FEAR | FEAR > HOPE | HOPE = FEAR |
> | --- | --- | --- | --- |
> | **Total ≥ DC** | Success with Hope | Success with Fear | **Critical Success** |
> | **Total < DC** | Failure with Hope | Failure with Fear | **Critical Success** |
>
> Doubles are *always* a Critical Success, whatever the total, including 1+1 against DC 25. The worst nonmatching result is Failure with Fear.

The cosmology of the universe, the Hope Frequency hum that runs beneath everything, established in Chapter 1, sometimes simply *agrees with you*, and when it does, the agreement is total.

This is the entirety of the resolution mechanic. Every other rule in the system builds on this five-outcome structure.

## CHOOSING THE TRAIT

Most Duality Rolls add a Trait, one of the six character attributes that represent the broad arenas of human (and humanlike) capability. The six Traits are **Agility**, **Strength**, **Finesse**, **Knowledge**, **Instinct**, and **Presence**. Their numeric scores are set during character creation (Chapter 8) and shift over the arc of a campaign through advancement (Chapter 12).

**Canonical Subtraits.** Some specialized actions name a Subtrait in parentheses after its parent Trait. **Finesse (Pilot/Navigate)** covers piloting vehicles, plotting courses, docking, evasive maneuvers, and practical navigation. **Knowledge (Tech)** covers computers, engineering systems, electronics, hacking, repair theory, and technological analysis. **Knowledge (Medicine)** covers diagnosis, treatment, surgery, stabilization, and biological analysis. These are not seventh, eighth, or ninth Traits; they use the listed parent Trait score. Write the complete Roll as a **Finesse (Pilot/Navigate) Roll**, **Knowledge (Tech) Roll**, or **Knowledge (Medicine) Roll**. After a section establishes the parent Trait, the shorter forms Pilot/Navigate Roll, Knowledge (Tech) Roll, and Knowledge (Medicine) Roll are acceptable.

Choosing which Trait applies to a given roll is, in most cases, obvious from the fiction. Lifting a heavy object is Strength. Sneaking through a corridor is Agility. Picking a complex lock is Finesse. Piloting a skiff through a collapsing dock is Finesse (Pilot/Navigate). Recalling a fact about Precursor archaeology is Knowledge. Diagnosing an unfamiliar toxin is Knowledge (Medicine), while bypassing a security lattice is Knowledge (Tech). Reading another character's emotional state, or trusting your gut at the moment of a sudden decision,

is Instinct. Convincing, intimidating, or charming someone is Presence.

The cases where the Trait is genuinely ambiguous are the cases that matter, and the principle is this: **the player proposes, the Keeper confirms or adjusts**. A player who wants to use Knowledge to deceive a guard may have a perfectly good reason, perhaps their character has been studying Volkov security protocols and is leveraging that expertise rather than raw social skill. The Keeper, hearing the proposal, can accept it ("Yes, roll Knowledge, you're working from the protocols you memorized"), redirect ("That's actually closer to a Presence roll because you'll need to commit emotionally to the lie"), or split the difference ("Roll Presence, but spend a Hope to invoke your *Volkov Operations* Experience for the +3", for an Awakened character; the Sleeping invoke their Experiences free, Chapter 7).

The conversation matters more than the specific choice. A table that talks through the Trait selection together, even briefly, is a table that has shared agreement on what the roll means. A table where the Keeper silently picks the Trait and the player rolls without input loses some of that shared understanding. Both styles work, but the talking style produces tables where the dice carry more weight.

## READING THE OUTCOME

The five outcomes have specific narrative and mechanical meanings.

**Critical Success** means the action succeeds beyond what the character attempted. In addition to the fixed resource and combat payout, add one beneficial fictional detail consistent with established facts: a hidden compartment, useful information, or a charted Eddy. This detail grants no extra resource, numeric modifier, Condition, Action, item, or permanent change unless the feature being resolved explicitly states it.

Critical Successes also clear **1 Stress**, and then pay the character in the currency of their Path. This is the master statement of that payout; every other mention in this book defers to it.

> **QUICK PROCEDURE - WHAT A CRITICAL SUCCESS PAYS**
>
> | | CLEAR | THEN GAIN |
> | --- | --- | --- |
> | **Awakened** | 1 Stress | **1 Hope** |
> | **Sleeping** | 1 Stress | Mark **both** segments of the Effort Track at once, clearing it for **1 Effort**, then take **1 further point** into either Effort or Resolve - your choice. If Effort is already at maximum, the point becomes 1 Resolve. (Chapter 7) |
>
> The critical is the one moment the Sleeping bank a reserve from play rather than from rest. Wherever this book says a Critical Success grants "1 Hope", read it as shorthand for this table.

Many abilities and Domain Powers have additional triggers on Critical Successes. The dice favored you in the most absolute way the system permits, and the fiction, and the rules, both recognize this.

**Player Critical Damage.** When a player character scores a Critical Success on an attack roll, determine the attack's normal damage pool, including Proficiency, and roll twice that number of damage dice. Add flat modifiers once. Do not double Stress costs, Armor Piercing, conditions, blast radius, duration, or other secondary effects unless the effect explicitly says otherwise. A weapon that normally deals 4d8+2 on that attack deals 8d8+2 on a Critical Success.

**Keeper Critical Damage.** When a Keeper-controlled adversary scores a Critical Success on an attack roll, do not roll damage. Treat every damage die in the attack's normal damage pool as having rolled its maximum value, then add flat modifiers once. Resolve the result normally against Damage Thresholds. The target may spend Armor Slots to reduce the severity as normal unless the attack explicitly states that it ignores armor, cannot be shielded, or cannot be reduced with Armor Slots.

**No exceptional die faces.** A match of 1+1 and a match of 12+12 use the same Critical Success procedure as every other double. Neither result adds a penalty, a special mishap, an extra reward, or a separate table unless a feature explicitly modifies every Critical Success.


**Success with Hope** means the action succeeds cleanly, and the universe rewards you. The character does the thing, with no complication, and gains **1 Hope** for the player (Awakened only). This is the "clean win" outcome, the most common form of unambiguous success at the table. The Hope Frequency lifted you slightly, the way it does, and you carried the moment.

**Success with Fear** means the action succeeds, but at a cost. The character does the thing, but a complication arrives, the door opens *and* an alarm sounds, the negotiation works *and* the partner notes they will remember this favor, the jump completes *and* a Veil Eddy delays the arrival by six hours. The Keeper takes **1 Fear token**, subject to the hard maximum of 12 for their pool, to be spent later as the session demands. The success is real, but the universe registers a small cost, and the Keeper now has a pebble in hand, ready to drop.

**Failure with Hope** means the action fails without a complication. Resolve normal Path progress: an Awakened character gains 1 Hope and a Sleeping character marks one Effort Track segment, subject to the normal limits. The Roll creates no new route, clue, item, position, or numeric benefit unless its Feature explicitly prints one.

**Failure with Fear** means the action does not succeed, and a complication compounds the failure. The character does not do the thing, *and* something else goes wrong as a direct or indirect consequence. The lockpick fails *and* it breaks off in the lock. The negotiation breaks down *and* the partner is now actively hostile. The Keeper takes **1 Fear token**, subject to the hard maximum of 12 and the situation has measurably worsened. This is the worst single-roll outcome the system produces. It is not, however, "you die." Death,

covered in detail in Chapter 10, is a separate procedure that requires its own decisions.

Doubles are always a Critical Success. This is intentional. The cosmology of the post-Silence galaxy includes a Hope Frequency that, on average, lifts toward generosity rather than pulling toward catastrophe. A character can fail badly, but matched dice never create a negative critical result. The worst nonmatching result is **Failure with Fear**: failure plus a complication. The character's response to that failure is where the story goes next.

> **WORKED EXAMPLE - FAILURE WITH FEAR**
>
> Riven tries to slice the airlock override before the patrol rounds the corner. Duality Roll: 7 and 11, Fear die higher, total under the DC. **Failure with Fear** - the slice fails, and the Keeper takes 1 Fear, subject to the hard maximum of 12. Nothing happens to Riven this instant; the patrol is still thirty seconds out. The Keeper notes the Fear and says nothing yet, letting the scene continue. Two exchanges later, with four Fear now banked, the patrol's radio crackles early and the ambush the crew planned collapses before it starts.
>
