### LEVEL 4: TIER 2

**Cordon of Will** *Spell · 1 Stress · DC 15 (Knowledge) · RC 1*

Cost: 1 Stress. Knowledge Spellcast Roll (DC 15). You weave a zone of compelled stillness across a path, doorway, or threshold within Close range. A creature attempting to cross makes a Presence Reaction Roll, DC 20; on failure it cannot proceed and is Dazed. The Cordon has Major Threshold 5, Severe Threshold 10, and 10 HP against Neural damage; physical attacks pass through it. A determined hostile may bypass it by marking 1 Stress as a free effect. Reposition the Cordon one range band by spending an Action. This cannot compel a player character to cross, remain, or change allegiance.

**Neural Feedback** *Ability (Reaction) · 1 Stress · DC 15 (Presence) · RC 2*

*Trigger: An adversary within Close range deals HP damage to you.*

Reaction. When an adversary in Close range deals damage to you, Presence Spellcast Roll (DC 15). Success: They take (Proficiency)×d8 Void damage and must make a Instinct Reaction Roll, DC 15 or become Vulnerable until the end of their next Spotlight.

### LEVEL 5: TIER 2

**Mind Spike** *Spell · 2 Hope · DC 20 (Presence) · RC 2*

Presence Spellcast Roll (DC 20) against a creature in Far range. Success: Deal (Proficiency)×d12 Void damage ignoring armor. The target must make a Presence Reaction Roll, DC 15 or be Stunned until the end of its next Spotlight.

**Temporal Glimpse** *Spell · 2 Hope · DC 15 (Instinct) · RC 2*

Instinct Spellcast Roll (DC 15). Cost: 2 Hope. You gain a brief vision of one likely outcome. For your next Spotlight only, you may use this vision to either gain Advantage on one roll OR force an enemy to reroll an attack against you.

### LEVEL 6: TIER 2

**Collective Consciousness** *Spell · 2 Hope · DC 20 (Presence) · RC 3*

Presence Spellcast Roll (DC 20). Cost: 2 Hope. You link the minds of up to 6 willing creatures in Far range for one scene. You share thoughts, senses, and experiences instantly across any distance.

**Psychic Storm** *Spell · 2 Hope + 1 Stress · DC 20 (Presence) · RC 3*

Presence Spellcast Roll (DC 20) targeting all adversaries in Close range. Success: Assault them with psychic energy, dealing (Proficiency)×d10 Void damage. They must make a Presence Reaction Roll, DC 15 or Mark 1 Stress.

### LEVEL 7: TIER 3

**Mind Sanctuary** *Spell · 2 Hope + 1 Stress · DC 20 (Presence) · RC 3*

Cost: 2 Hope + 1 Stress. Presence Spellcast Roll (DC 20). You raise a lattice of disciplined thought around yourself and your allies, sealing every mind in the area against intrusion. For one scene, you and all allies in Close range are immune to mental, social, and emotional manipulation effects (charm, fear, deception, intimidation, psychic intrusion, compulsion). Once during the scene, when an enemy would target you or an ally with such an effect, you may reflect the attempt back at its caster: they make the contested roll against themselves at Disadvantage. Failure: The lattice forms inverted. You and all allies in Close range have Disadvantage on Presence and Instinct rolls until the end of the scene; the Keeper gains 2 Fear, subject to the hard maximum of 12.

**Veil Suppression** *Spell · 3 Hope + 1 Stress · DC 20 (Knowledge) · RC 3*

*Once per session*

Knowledge Spellcast Roll (DC 20). Cost: 3 Hope + 1 Stress. You stabilize physics in a Very Far range area for one scene. All Void, Ethereal, and Precursor effects have Disadvantage on rolls within the area. Failure: The sudden stabilization causes a shockwave, dealing 1 Stress to all allies.

### LEVEL 8: TIER 3

**Psychic Collapse** *Spell · 3 Hope + 1 Stress · DC 25 (Presence) · RC 3*

*Once per session*

Presence Spellcast Roll (DC 25). Target one creature in Very Far range. Deal 3d8 Void damage ignoring armor. The target suffers Disadvantage on all rolls for 1 round. Failure: The damage rebounds, dealing 1d8 Void damage to you.

**Temporal Maelstrom** *Spell · 2 Stress · DC 25 (Instinct) · RC 3*

Mark 2 Stress and Instinct Spellcast Roll (DC 25). Create a reality distortion in Close range for one scene. All creatures in the area (including you) have Disadvantage on all rolls. Failure: You are immediately subjected to the Veil Storm effects until you clear 2 Stress.

### LEVEL 9: TIER 3

**Destiny Weave** *Spell · 3 Stress · DC 25 (Instinct) · RC 3*

*Once per long rest*

Mark 3 Stress. Instinct Spellcast Roll (DC 25). Force a complete reroll on any one roll you witness. You may modify the result by +3 or -3. Failure: You must apply the worst possible result to the roll and take 2 Stress.

**Psychic Fallout** *Spell · 5 Hope + 2 Stress · DC 25 (Presence) · RC 3*

*Once per session*

Presence Spellcast Roll (DC 25). Affects all adversaries in Far range. Deal 3d6 Void damage. Targets make Instinct Reaction Rolls, DC 15 or become Stunned for 1 round and Vulnerable for the scene. Cost: 5 Hope + 2 Stress. Failure: You are overwhelmed (Disadvantage on all rolls) for 1d4 rounds.

### LEVEL 10: MYTHIC

**Consciousness Bridge** *Spell · 3 Hope + 2 Stress · DC 30 (Presence) · RC 3*

*Once per long rest [Mythic]*

Mythic. Once per long rest. Presence Spellcast Roll (DC 30). Share consciousness with a willing target across a planetary system for one scene. You can both use each other's Abilities, Domain powers, and Traits. Failure: Minds clash, reducing the Instinct or Presence Trait of both targets by 1 until the next long rest.

**Veil Mastery** *Spell · 3 Hope + 1 Stress · DC 30 (Instinct) · RC 3*

*Once per session [Mythic]*

Mythic. Once per session. Instinct Spellcast Roll (DC 30). Base cost: 3 Hope + 1 Stress. Choose one mode. **Rewind:** undo the Keeper's immediately preceding action block and restore 1 Hope and clear 1 Stress for each ally affected by it. **Accelerate:** before the end of the next round, each ally may take one additional Action during one of their Spotlights. **Restructure:** move each willing creature and unattended object within Far range up to one range band in any direction; an unwilling NPC may resist with a Presence Reaction Roll, DC 20, and a player character moves only with that player's consent. **Dream-Project:** instead pay 2 additional Hope and 1 additional Stress; up to 3 targets within Far range enter a shared illusion for one scene. At the start of each affected NPC's Spotlight it may make an Instinct Reaction Roll, DC 15, to perceive baseline reality; a player character participates only with that player's consent. At casting, +1 Hope adds one target, maximum 6, or raises the escape DC to 20; +1 Stress together with that Hope extends the duration until the next Long Rest. Maximum total cost is 6 Hope and 3 Stress. On failure to cast, adversaries receive the chosen foundational benefit and you mark 4 Stress; for Dream-Project, you are also Stunned for 1 round and have Disadvantage on Presence and Instinct Rolls for the scene.


## KINETIC DOMAIN

*Card label `KINETIC`. The crimson banner. Kinetic Powers are the control over kinetic force. This is the domain of unstoppable impacts and immovable objects. Practitioners create barriers of pure force, improve their own speed to impossible levels, strike with the concussive power of a meteor.*

### LEVEL 1: TIER 1

**Force Shield** *Ability (Reaction) · 1 Hope · - · RC 1*

*Trigger: You or an ally within Very Close range is hit by an attack.*

Reaction. When you or an ally in Very Close range is hit by an attack, you may Spend 1 Hope to create a kinetic barrier. You provide +3 Evasion against that attack. If the attack misses due to this bonus, the attacker takes (Proficiency)×d4 Physical damage with the Kinetic tag.

**Kinetic Blast** *Ability · 1 Hope · - · RC 0*

Spend 1 Hope when making a melee attack. Hit: Deal Weapon Damage + Strength + 1d8 Physical damage with the Kinetic tag. Empower: You may spend up to 2 additional Hope (3 Hope total) at the moment of the strike. For each additional Hope spent, add 1 die of (Proficiency)d6 Physical damage with the Kinetic tag. Ballistic Impact: If total damage triggers Overkill, move the target one range band directly away from the source. If it collides with a solid object, apply Prone.

**Tactical Overwatch** *Ability (Reaction) · 1 Hope · - · RC 0*

*Trigger: An ally within Close range is targeted by an attack.*

Reaction. When an ally in Close range is targeted by an attack, you may Spend 1 Hope. They gain Advantage on

their defense and 2 temporary Armor Slots until the start of your next Spotlight.

### LEVEL 2: TIER 1

**Impact Absorption** *Ability (Reaction) · 1 Stress · - · RC 2*

*Trigger: You take Physical damage.*

Reaction. When taking Physical damage, mark 1 Stress to reduce it by (Proficiency)×d6+2. On your next Spotlight, either add the absorbed amount to one attack's damage or move one additional range band.

**Kinetic Barrier** *Ability · 1 Stress · - · RC 1*

Mark 1 Stress. You create a protective force field around yourself for one scene. You gain +1 Evasion and Resistance to Physical damage. The barrier absorbs up to 10 damage before dissipating.

### LEVEL 3: TIER 1

**Protective Dome** *Spell · 1 Hope · DC 15 (Strength) · RC 1*

Strength Spellcast Roll (DC 15). You create a kinetic dome covering a Very Close zone for 10 minutes. It provides occupants with +2 Evasion and blocks area attacks from outside. An enemy entering makes a Strength Reaction Roll, DC 15. On failure it remains outside. On a Success with Hope, everyone inside clears 1 HP at the end of each round.

**Velocity Surge** *Spell · 1 Hope · DC 15 (Agility) · RC 1*

Agility Spellcast Roll (DC 15). You enhance your reflexes for one scene. You gain +2 on Agility Rolls, may move one additional range band during each of your Spotlights, and can move through enemy spaces without provoking attacks. On a Success with Hope, gain Advantage on the next Agility Reaction Roll you make this scene.

### LEVEL 4: TIER 2

**Guardian's Aegis** *Spell · 2 Hope · DC 15 (Presence) · RC 2*

Presence Spellcast Roll (DC 15). Designate up to 3 allies in Close range for one scene. When they would take damage, you may use your reaction to take half of it instead. You gain +1 Evasion for each protected ally. On a Success with Hope: You may redirect any damage you take this way as an immediate attack against a nearby enemy.

**Precision Strike** *Spell · 1 Hope · DC 15 (Finesse) · RC 2*

Finesse Spellcast Roll (DC 15). Choose one target within Far range. Make a ranged kinetic attack that deals (Proficiency)×d10 Physical damage with the Kinetic tag. This attack ignores ordinary cover but never Total Cover. On Success with Hope, the target cannot take Reactions until the end of its next Spotlight; this is an exact rider, not a separate Condition.

### LEVEL 5: TIER 2

**Kinetic Mastery** *Spell · 2 Hope · DC 15 (Strength) · RC 2*

Strength Spellcast Roll (DC 15). You gain perfect kinetic control for one scene. Choose one: walk on walls/ceilings OR gain immunity to forced movement and fall damage. On a Success with Hope: Extend the benefit to all allies in Close range.

**Shockwave Pulse** *Spell · 2 Hope + 1 Stress · DC 20 (Strength) · RC 3*

Strength Spellcast Roll (DC 20). You unleash a kinetic pulse throughout Close range. Choose one: Protective (all allies gain +2 Evasion for 1 round and clear 1d4 HP) or Offensive (all enemies take (Proficiency)×d12 Physical damage with the Kinetic tag and become Prone). On a Success with Hope, create both effects.

### LEVEL 6: TIER 2

**Energy Cascade** *Spell · 2 Hope + 1 Stress · DC 20 (Strength) · RC 3*

Strength Spellcast Roll (DC 20). A chain reaction affects all enemies within Far range for 1 minute. At the start of each round, every affected target makes an Agility Reaction Roll, DC 15; on failure it takes (Proficiency)×d8 Physical damage with the Kinetic tag and is pushed one range band away. The damage gains a cumulative +1 flat modifier each round. On failure to cast, the cascade affects you and your allies instead.

**Force Fortress** *Spell · 2 Hope + 1 Stress · DC 20 (Strength) · RC 3*

Strength Spellcast Roll (DC 20). You create a massive kinetic fortress with 50 HP, Evasion 18, that lasts 1 hour and provides total cover. Failure: The fortress collapses immediately, dealing 1d8 damage to occupants.

### LEVEL 7: TIER 3

**Orbital Lance** *Spell · 2 Hope + 2 Stress · DC 20 (Strength) · RC 3*

*Once per session*

Strength Spellcast Roll (DC 20). Cost: 2 Hope + 2 Stress. Call an orbital strike on a point in Very Far range; it cannot target a moving ship. It deals 4d10 Physical damage with the Kinetic tag throughout a Very Close zone and ignores ordinary cover. On failure, roll d8 for direction around the declared map orientation and 1d4 for distance in range bands; the strike lands there and cannot be redirected to a target that was not already in that zone. The discharge also makes your ship lose **1 Hull directly**; if no ship is present, the location suffers equivalent structural damage.

**Temporal Freeze** *Spell · 3 Hope + 1 Stress · DC 20 (Instinct) · RC 3*

*Once per session*

Instinct Spellcast Roll (DC 20). You control all momentum in Close range for one round. You may stop all moving objects or accelerate up to 3 objects/targets. Failure: Massive kinetic feedback leaves you Stunned for 1 round and you suffer 2 Stress.

### LEVEL 8: TIER 3

**Singularity Well** *Spell · 3 Hope + 1 Stress · DC 25 (Strength) · RC 3*

*Once per session*

Strength Spellcast Roll (DC 25). You manipulate gravity throughout Far range for 1 hour. You can create areas of high or low gravity (Disadvantage or Advantage on movement Rolls) or anti-gravity flight. On failure, you suffer Disadvantage on Agility Rolls for 1d6 days or until you complete a Long Rest devoted to recalibrating your kinetic attunement.

**Tactical Aegis** *Spell · 3 Hope + 3 Stress · DC 20 (Presence) · RC 3*

*Once per long rest*

Presence Spellcast Roll (DC 20). You create a kinetic barrier around a starship or settlement (Tier 5 Asset). The shield has 100 HP and protects against large-scale attacks for one scene/combat. Cost: 3 Hope + 3

Stress. Failure: The target location gains Vulnerable for 1 round.

### LEVEL 9: TIER 3

**Asteroid Redirect** *Spell · 3 Hope + 2 Stress · DC 25 (Knowledge) · RC 3*

*Once per long rest*

Knowledge Spellcast Roll (DC 25). You manipulate a small asteroid field to impact a target ship (Tier 3-4), dealing 3 Hull Damage. Failure: The impact is misdirected, dealing 3 Hull Damage to your own ship instead.

**Indomitable Bastion** *Spell · 3 Hope + 2 Stress · DC 25 (Strength) · RC 3*

*Once per long rest*

Strength Spellcast Roll (DC 25). You create a massive kinetic fortress with 150 HP, Evasion 18, that lasts 1 hour and provides total cover. Failure: The barrier collapses catastrophically, dealing 3d12 Physical damage with the Kinetic tag to all occupants.

### LEVEL 10: MYTHIC

**Absolute Command** *Spell · 5 Hope + 5 Stress · DC 30 (Strength) · RC 3*

*Once per campaign [Mythic]*

Mythic. Once per campaign. Strength Spellcast Roll (DC 30). For one week, you may apply the Massive or Stunning feature to any weapon damage roll. Cost: 5 Hope and 5 Stress. Failure: Disadvantage on all Agility and movement rolls until completing a mythic quest (approximately one story arc) to restore your kinetic connection.

**Force Incarnate** *Spell · 5 Hope + 5 Stress · DC 30 (Strength) · RC 3*

*Once per campaign [Mythic]*

Mythic. Once per campaign. Strength Spellcast Roll (DC 30). Cost: 5 Hope + 5 Stress. Until your next Long Rest, you exist as pure kinetic energy: gain Immunity to Physical damage and, once during each of your Spotlights, Teleport up to Far range as a free effect. You cannot use equipment that requires hands. At the start of each later Long Rest, before other benefits resolve, you may pay 3 Hope + 1 Stress to extend the state through the next rest cycle. Once it ends, Force Incarnate cannot be used again in this campaign. On failure to cast, take 4d12 Physical damage through normal Thresholds, the Keeper gains 4 Fear subject to the hard maximum of 12, and Force Incarnate becomes unavailable for the campaign.


## VOID DOMAIN

*Card label `VOID`. The deep-black banner. Void Powers are the subtle manipulation of space, shadow, and luck. The Void is the quietest but perhaps strangest of the Domains, those who touch it can step through shadows, bend probability to their favor, find paths where none should exist. They are the galaxy's ghosts, spies, and masters of the impossible escape.*

### LEVEL 1: TIER 1

**Slipstream Jolt** *Ability · 1 Stress · - · RC 1*

Mark 1 Stress. Choose one electronic system or creature in Close range. They suffer a momentary temporal/spatial misalignment, gaining Disadvantage on their next Agility or Finesse roll.

**Temporal Cloak** *Ability · 1 Hope · - · RC 0*

Spend 1 Hope. Choose one mode: Vehicle (the ship is nearly invisible for 10 minutes and attacks against it have Disadvantage) or Personal (you are nearly invisible for 10 minutes and gain Advantage on Agility Rolls to avoid detection). The effect ends if the protected subject attacks or uses another Void Power.

**Vector Calculus** *Ability · 1 Hope · - · RC 1*

Spend 1 Hope when making an Agility or Finesse (Pilot/Navigate) Roll. You may add your Level to the roll and treat a 10 or lower as an 11 on the Hope die.

### LEVEL 2: TIER 1

**Lucky Break** *Ability (Reaction) · 1 Stress · - · RC 2*

Reaction. Mark 1 Stress. Choose one mode: Vehicle (reroll one die you rolled for a spacecraft Action and use the new result) or Personal (reroll one die you rolled and use the new result). Once per scene, also choose one coincidence: a loose unsecured object is within reach, an ordinary unlocked exit is unobstructed, or a non-hostile bystander notices you. The coincidence creates no item, credential, damage, resource, or automatic success.

**Spatial Shift** *Ability · 1 Stress · - · RC 2*

Mark 1 Stress. Choose one mode: Vehicle (instantly teleport your spacecraft to any location up to Far range, arriving silently in shadow/cover) or Personal (teleport to any location in Close range, arriving silently in shadow/cover with no trace). No roll required --- the Void does not fail to move you. It only asks the price.

### LEVEL 3: TIER 1

**Flux Field** *Spell · 1 Hope + 1 Stress · DC 15 (Instinct) · RC 3*

Instinct Spellcast Roll (DC 15). Cost: 1 Hope + 1 Stress. For 10 minutes, choose one mode. **Lucky Streak:** once per round, grant one ally Advantage on one Roll before it is made. **Unlucky Enemies:** once per round, impose Disadvantage on one enemy attack before it is made. On a Success with Hope, gain both modes. Matching Duality Dice always remain a Critical Success.

**Temporal Muffle** *Spell · 1 Hope · DC 15 (Finesse) · RC 1*

Finesse Spellcast Roll (DC 15). Choose a mode: Vehicle (a Very Far field centered on the vehicle for 1 hour; sensor-based detection has Disadvantage) or Personal (a Far field centered on you for 1 hour; sounds are muffled and allies gain Advantage on Agility Rolls to avoid auditory detection).

### LEVEL 4: TIER 2

**Danger Sense** *Spell · 1 Hope · DC 15 (Instinct) · RC 2*

Instinct Spellcast Roll (DC 15). For one scene, you have supernatural threat awareness. You automatically detect

traps, ambushes, and hostile intent in Far range. You gain you may take the first player Spotlight when combat begins and cannot be surprised. On a Success with Hope: Share this benefit with all allies in Close range.

**Spatial Cache** *Spell · 1 Stress · DC 15 (Finesse) · RC 2*

Cost: 1 Stress. Finesse Spellcast Roll (DC 15). You create a pocket dimension for 8 hours, completely undetectable. Choose a mode: Vehicle (store cargo/small craft or hide the entire ship) or Personal (store equipment/allies).

### LEVEL 5: TIER 2

**Fate's Hand** *Spell · 2 Hope + 1 Stress · DC 20 (Instinct) · RC 3*

Instinct Spellcast Roll (DC 20). Cost: 2 Hope + 1 Stress. Dramatically alter probability for one outcome within the next hour. Choose one: ensure one future Roll is a Critical Success; cause one enemy weapon to suffer a catastrophic malfunction until an Action repairs it; or establish one improbable but fictionally possible coincidence. On failure, suffer Disadvantage on all Rolls for 1d4 hours.

**Phase Walk** *Spell · 2 Hope · DC 15 (Finesse) · RC 2*

Finesse Spellcast Roll (DC 15). For one scene, you can move without trace, passing through solid objects as if they were difficult terrain. Choose a mode: Vehicle or Personal.

### LEVEL 6: TIER 2

**Spatial Link** *Spell · 2 Hope · DC 20 (Instinct) · RC 3*

Instinct Spellcast Roll (DC 20). Create a quantum link with up to 3 willing allies for 24 hours. You share a sense of luck and spatial awareness. On a Success with Hope: As a reaction, you can instantly swap positions with any linked ally.

**Void Sanctuary** *Long-Term Project (10 segments) · 2 Hope to begin · - · RC 3*

Create a permanent sanctuary hidden within a pocket dimension. Spend 2 Hope to begin the project and define its nature with the Keeper.

**Progress:** During each active Downtime phase, make a Finesse roll against DC 15. On a success, advance 1 segment. On a Success with Hope, advance 2 segments.

**Completion:** The sanctuary permanently exists. Choose one form:

- **Fleet Mode:** A hidden base for up to 12 ships, completely undetectable by standard methods.
- **Personal Mode:** A safehouse accessible only to people you have explicitly authorized.

Once established, the sanctuary requires no maintenance.

### LEVEL 7: TIER 3

**Chrono Stasis** *Spell · 2 Hope + 2 Stress · DC 20 (Instinct) · RC 0*

Instinct Spellcast Roll (DC 20). Cost: 2 Hope + 2 Stress. Freeze time for all other creatures and objects within Far range for up to 1 subjective minute. You may move and act normally, but frozen targets are invulnerable and cannot be moved or altered until time resumes.

**Phase Jump** *Spell · 2 Hope + 2 Stress · DC 20 (Finesse) · RC 3*

*Once per session*

Finesse Spellcast Roll (DC 20). Warp space around yourself/ship/allies for one scene, gaining the ability to phase through matter and become invisible. Cost: 2 Hope + 2 Stress. Failure: You are temporarily displaced (Stunned) until the end of your next Spotlight and suffer 2 Stress.

### LEVEL 8: TIER 3

**Phantom Ship** *Spell · 3 Hope + 1 Stress · DC 20 (Instinct) · RC 3*

*Once per long rest*

Instinct Spellcast Roll (DC 20). You phase your entire ship and crew into a parallel dimension for one scene/combat. The ship is undetectable and intangible. Failure: The ship phases back immediately and loses **2 Hull directly** from turbulence.

**Temporal Disarray** *Spell · 3 Hope + 1 Stress · DC 25 (Instinct) · RC 3*

*Once per long rest*

Instinct Spellcast Roll (DC 25). Create a probability storm throughout a Very Far area for one scene. For Rolls made inside it, a physical Duality die face of 1 counts as 12 and a face of 12 counts as 1 before checking for a match; this can create or remove a Critical Success but never create a negative critical result. On failure, you suffer Disadvantage on all Rolls for 1d6 hours.

### LEVEL 9: TIER 3

**Cosmic Luck** *Spell · 4 Hope + 2 Stress · DC 25 (Instinct) · RC 3*

*Once per long rest*

Instinct Spellcast Roll (DC 25). You may apply the effects of a Critical Success to any single roll you witness during the next session. Cost: 4 Hope + 2 Stress. Failure: Your next nonmatching Duality Roll resolves as a **Failure with Fear**, regardless of its total. If that roll is doubles, it remains a Critical Success and this consequence waits for the next nonmatching roll.

**The Navigator's Truth** *Spell · 3 Hope + 2 Stress · DC 25 (Knowledge) · RC 3*

*Once per story arc*

Knowledge Spellcast Roll (DC 25). Gain a permanent, unique Stellar Chart (Tier 5 Asset) for the sector. This allows your vessel to make one Instantaneous Jump within the sector per session. Failure: The jump leads the ship directly into a Veil Storm and it loses **3 Hull directly**.

### LEVEL 10: MYTHIC

**Master of Fate** *Spell · 5 Hope + 3 Stress · DC 30 (Instinct) · RC 3*

*Once per campaign [Mythic]*

Mythic. Once per campaign. Instinct Spellcast Roll (DC 30). Cost: 5 Hope + 3 Stress. You weave a single perfect knot in the threads of probability. For one scene: All allies have Advantage on every roll they make. All enemies have Disadvantage on every roll they make. Once during the scene, you may declare a single roll (yours or an ally's) to be treated as a Critical Success without rolling. This declaration cannot be made on damage rolls or on rolls that have already resolved. Failure: For the rest of the scene, Advantage and Disadvantage are inverted, your enemies receive the boon, and your allies suffer the penalty. The threads tighten the wrong way.

**Master of Space** *Spell · 5 Hope + 5 Stress · DC 30 (Instinct) · RC 3*

*Once per campaign [Mythic]*

Mythic. Once per campaign. Instinct Spellcast Roll (DC 30). Your vessel gains the ability to use Instantaneous Jump once per session. Cost: 5 Hope and 5 Stress. Failure: You are temporally lost and cannot make a jump for 1d4 sessions, and your ship loses **3 Hull directly**.


## LUX DOMAIN

*Card label `LIGHT`. The gold banner. Lux is the science of hope made manifest. Lux is not mystical magic, it is the manipulation of measurable wavelengths, stellar radiation, and a quantum phenomenon called the Hope Frequency. Its wielders channel photonic energy to shield allies, burn away the Veil's corruption, reveal hidden paths, and guide the lost through the dark. Lux is the cosmological opposite of Void: where Void unravels, Lux restores; where Void conceals, Lux reveals.*

### LEVEL 1: TIER 1

**Blinding Flash** *Ability (Reaction) · 1 Hope · - · RC 0*

*Trigger: An enemy within Close range makes an attack.*

Spend 1 Hope. All enemies within Close range must make an Instinct Reaction Roll (DC 10). On failure, they suffer Disadvantage on their next attack. On a Failure with Fear, they are Dazed until the end of their next Spotlight.

**Spark of Hope** *Ability · 1 Hope · - · RC 0*

Spend 1 Hope. Touch an ally within Close range. They clear 1 Stress. You cannot target yourself.

**Wayfinder's Pulse** *Ability · 1 Hope · - · RC 1*

Spend 1 Hope. You emit a pulse of light visible only to you. The pulse reveals the following within Far range: the direction and approximate distance of the nearest significant threat (hostile creature, trap, ambush), the nearest exit or navigable path, and any hidden or concealed objects of value or importance. The information is directional, not precise --- you know where, not what. The pulse does not penetrate solid walls thicker than 1 meter.

### LEVEL 2: TIER 1

**Eyes of Truth** *Ability · 1 Stress · - · RC 1*

Mark 1 Stress. For the remainder of the scene, you see through illusions, invisibility, and mundane disguise. You ignore all visibility penalties from darkness, smoke, or Veil distortion. You gain Advantage on Instinct Rolls to Perceive or Investigate. Additionally, you can read emotional intent --- you know when someone within Close range is lying, afraid, or hostile, though not the specific content of their thoughts (that is Neural territory).

**Photon Shield** *Ability (Reaction) · 1 Stress · - · RC 1*

*Trigger: An ally within Close range takes HP damage from an attack.*

Reaction. Mark 1 Stress. When an ally within Close range takes HP damage from an attack, reduce the damage by your Tier + 2 before it is compared to Damage Thresholds. Against creatures with the Veil-Touched tag, the reduction is doubled.

### LEVEL 3: TIER 1

**Aura of Clarity** *Spell · 1 Hope · DC 15 (Presence) · RC 2*

Cost: 1 Hope. Presence Spellcast Roll (DC 15). Cost: 1 Hope. Concentration. You and all allies within Close range are immune to the Frightened and Dazed conditions. While sustained, all allied Damage Thresholds within the aura increase by +1 (both Major and Severe). Concentration ends if you take Stress or are incapacitated.

**Stellar Lance** *Spell · 1 Hope · DC 15 (Presence) · RC 1*

Presence Spellcast Roll (DC 15). Ranged attack at Far range. Deal (Proficiency)×d8 Energy damage with the Radiant tag. Against targets wearing Heavy or Very Heavy armor, this attack gains the Devastating keyword. At Tier 2+, the target is marked as Illuminated until the end of your next Spotlight: they cannot benefit from cover or stealth, and the next attack against them has Advantage.

### LEVEL 4: TIER 2

**Deflection Prism** *Ability (Reaction) · 2 Hope · - · RC 2*

*Trigger: An enemy makes a ranged attack against you or an adjacent ally.*

Spend 2 Hope as a Reaction. Redirect the attack to any other valid target within the original weapon's range. Resolve the original attack roll against the new target's Evasion.

*Limitation: You cannot redirect the attack back at the original attacker. This power works only against ranged attacks, not melee attacks.*

**Solar Judgment** *Spell · 1 Hope · DC 15 (Presence) · RC 2*

Cost: 1 Hope. Presence Spellcast Roll (DC 15). Choose a point within Close range; every enemy in a Very Close zone around it takes (Proficiency)×d6 Energy damage with the Radiant tag. A creature with the Veil-Touched or Void tag then makes an Instinct Reaction Roll, DC 15; on failure it is Dazed and cannot use Void Powers until the end of its next Spotlight.

### LEVEL 5: TIER 2

**Beacon of Resurrection** *Spell · 3 Hope + 3 Stress · DC 20 (Presence) · RC 3*

Presence Spellcast Roll (DC 20). Cost: 3 Hope + 3 Stress. You restore a fallen ally (who has reached 0 HP within the last round) to 1 HP. The revived ally acts at Disadvantage until the end of their next Spotlight. After using this power, you cannot use any Lux power until you complete a Long Rest.

**Cartographer of the Unseen** *Spell · 1 Hope · DC 15 (Instinct) · RC 2*

Instinct Spellcast Roll (DC 15). Cost: 1 Hope. For the remainder of the scene, you perceive the complete layout of the structure, installation, or natural environment within a 500-meter radius. You know every room, corridor, door, shaft, and hidden passage. You know where every creature larger than a rat is located and whether they are moving. You cannot determine identity or intent --- only position, count, and approximate size. This information updates in real time for the duration.

### LEVEL 6: TIER 2

**Lightbridge** *Spell · 2 Hope · DC 20 (Presence) · RC 3*

Presence Spellcast Roll (DC 20). Cost: 2 Hope. Teleport up to 3 willing creatures within Far range to a visible point within Far range. On arrival, each clears 1 Stress. If the destination is beyond sight or actively contested, the Keeper must set DC 25 before the Roll instead of adding an intermediate modifier.

Presence Spellcast Roll (DC 20). Fill a Close-range cone and deal (Proficiency)×d10 Energy damage with the Radiant tag. This attack ignores ordinary physical cover and barricades. Each affected target makes an Agility Reaction Roll, DC 15; on failure it is Blinded for 1 round.

### LEVEL 7: TIER 3

**Corona Beam** *Spell · 2 Hope · DC 20 (Presence) · RC 3*

*Once per session*

Presence Spellcast Roll (DC 20). Cost: 2 Hope. Draw a piercing line through Far range and deal (Proficiency × 2)×d8 Energy damage with the Radiant tag to every target in it. Against a target of lower Tier, add +10 to the damage total before comparing with Damage Thresholds; normal Overkill still applies.

**Inviolable Sanctum** *Spell · 2 Hope + 1 Stress · DC 20 (Presence) · RC 3*

*Once per session*

Presence Spellcast Roll (DC 20). Concentration. Create a Close-range dome of hardened light. Nothing crosses its boundary in either direction without your explicit permission: not weapons fire, Void Powers, or sound. Allies inside clear 1 Stress at the end of each round. The dome persists for up to 1 minute or until your concentration is broken.

### LEVEL 8: TIER 3

**Omniscient Eye** *Spell · 2 Hope + 1 Stress · DC 25 (Instinct) · RC 3*

*Once per long rest*

Instinct Spellcast Roll (DC 25). Cost: 2 Hope + 1 Stress. For 1 hour, perceive every creature, vehicle, energy signature, and hidden space throughout the same local district, treated as Very Far range for this Power. Focus on any point there and observe it as though present, including hearing conversations. Veil-distorted areas and psionic shielding appear as blank spots. While using this Power, your body is immobile and Vulnerable.

**Solar Avatar** *Spell · 4 Hope · DC 25 (Presence) · RC 3*

*Once per long rest*

Presence Spellcast Roll (DC 25). Cost: 4 Hope. Personal transformation lasting 3 rounds. While transformed, you gain flight and immunity to Physical damage. After a Lux attack determines its normal HP loss, increase that loss by 1, to a maximum of 4 HP from severity and Overkill before other explicit modifiers. You emit bright light to Far range; a creature attempting a Void Power there first makes a Presence Reaction Roll, DC 20, and on failure the paid Power has no effect. When the transformation ends, mark 2 Stress.

### LEVEL 9: TIER 3

**Pulse of Genesis** *Spell · All remaining Hope (minimum 5) · DC 25 (Presence) · RC 3*

*Once per story arc*

Presence Spellcast Roll (DC 25). Cost: All remaining Hope (minimum 5). You release a wave of purifying light across the entire sector. All Veil corruption, Void anomalies, and temporal distortions within the area are suppressed for 24 hours. Veil-Touched NPCs of Tier 3 or lower are removed from the scene; a player character instead takes 4d10 Energy damage with the Radiant tag and uses the normal Dying procedure. Tier 4+ creatures take the same 4d10 Energy damage.

**Stellar Chorus** *Spell · 3 Hope + 2 Stress · DC 25 (Presence) · RC 3*

*Once per story arc*

Presence Spellcast Roll (DC 25). Cost: 3 Hope + 2 Stress. For the remainder of the scene, all allies within Far range add your Presence modifier to their attack rolls, Reaction Rolls, and Damage Thresholds. This does not stack with Aura of Clarity. When the effect ends, you fall unconscious for 1 hour.

### LEVEL 10: MYTHIC

**Apotheosis** *Spell · 5 Hope + 3 Stress · DC 30 (Presence) · RC 3*

*Once per campaign [Mythic]*

Mythic. Once per campaign. Presence Spellcast Roll (DC 30). Cost: 5 Hope + 3 Stress. You collapse the boundary between yourself and the Hope Frequency itself, becoming, for one perfect moment, a fragment of stellar light made flesh. On activation: All allies within Far range heal HP equal to their current Severe Threshold and clear 1 Stress. All enemies within Far range take 6d10 Energy damage with the Radiant tag (no Thresholds, direct HP, ignores armor). Veil-Touched enemies take double damage from this effect. Vessel of Light: Until the end of the current scene, you cannot fall below 1 HP and your unarmed strikes deal 1d6 Energy damage with the Radiant tag in addition to their normal damage. When the scene ends, your body discorporates. You reform 24 hours later at the nearest star system, with 1 HP and 0 Stress. You cannot be resurrected by any other means during this 24-hour period. Failure: The light tears through you instead of through your enemies. You take 4d10 damage (Threshold-applied), the Keeper gains 4 Fear, subject to the hard maximum of 12, and Apotheosis is unavailable for the remainder of the campaign.

**Eternal Beacon** *Spell · 5 Hope + 5 Stress · DC 30 (Presence) · RC 3*

*Once per campaign [Mythic]*

Mythic. Once per campaign. Presence Spellcast Roll (DC 30). Cost: 5 Hope + 5 Stress. Create a permanent source of Lux energy at your current location: a miniature star, lighthouse, or monument of living light. The Beacon suppresses Void influence across the established planetary region. Ships within sensor range navigate Veil storms without risk, and Pilot Instinct Rolls there automatically succeed. Veil-Touched creatures cannot approach within Far range of the Beacon. The Beacon cannot be destroyed by any force below Tier 5.

## HOW TO BUILD A LOADOUT

A practical note for players: by the end of Tier 3, an Awakened character may have access to 15+ Powers in their Vault. The **Loadout cap** (Chapter 18) determines how many they can carry into a session: 5 cards at Tier 1, 6 at Tier 2, and 7 at Tier 3, regardless of class.

The art of Loadout-building is **scene-anticipation**: thinking about what kind of work this session is likely to demand, and equipping accordingly. A combat-heavy session deserves combat-aligned Powers; a negotiation deserves Social and Lux. Most experienced players carry a mix, two combat-utility, two scene-shaping, one signature, and revise per session as the campaign clarifies.

Some Powers are good for almost every session and tend to live permanently in the Loadout (the Engineer's *Quantum Firewall*, the Mystic's *Mind Shield*, the Diplomat's *Silver Tongue*). Others are situational and earn their slot when the situation arrives.

**Recall Costs** (RC) matter. Powers with RC 0-1 swap freely mid-scene; RC 2-3 Powers commit you to that loadout for the encounter. Build with that in mind: keep your high-RC powers as known commitments, your low-RC powers as flexible response.

The *catalog* in this chapter is the resource. The *Loadout* is the choice. Build deliberately. The campaign will reward foresight; it will not reward over-preparation. Bring what you can use; leave what you cannot.

## CLOSING: THE CATALOG IS NOT THE PRACTICE

The Powers here are the system's content, not the practice of being Awakened; that practice is in the choosing, the cost, and what each Power says about who your character is becoming. The catalog is the starting place. The character is what you build from it. Welcome to the practice.

# THE GALAXY IN DEPTH

*"If the Veil is a medium for reaching across distance, and I am no longer prepared to argue otherwise, then what we call faster-than-light travel is not movement at all. It is conversation. We are making the universe small enough to fit inside a single voice. The voice answers if it likes us."*

*Mystic Iolanthe Vesh, Spire of Verita, lecture transcribed in the seventy-ninth post-Silence year*

This chapter is the deep end of the pool. You do not need any of it to play.

Everything required to build a character and run a session lives in the earlier chapters: the rules in Chapters 9 through 12, the world in Chapters 13 through 16, the cosmology in plain summary back in Chapter 1. What follows here is the *why* underneath all of that, the metaphysics of the Veil, the meaning of the Hope Frequency, the nature of the Awakened, the mystery of the Precursors, and the quiet question the whole setting is built around. Read it when you are curious. Skip it and you lose nothing at the table.

A note for Keepers: the texture lives here, but the genuine secrets do not. The deepest answers are held for the *Keeper's Companion* and the expansions. What you read below is what any educated person in the post-Silence galaxy could, in principle, know.

## THE VEIL: WHAT IT IS, AND WHAT IT IS NOT

The Veil is a region of physics. That sentence is wrong on at least three counts, but it is the closest the post-Silence sciences have come to a working definition.

It is wrong, first, because the Veil is not strictly *physics*. The Veil is the substrate from which physics emerges. To say physics describes the Veil is about as accurate as saying grammar describes the human voice. The grammar is real and useful and arrives at consistent rules. The voice is something else, of which the grammar is a partial and somewhat embarrassed catalog.

It is wrong, second, because the Veil is not strictly a *region*. There is no place a navigator can point to and say "the Veil is here." The Veil is everywhere, beneath everything, the underneath of normal space. A ship enters the Veil not by traveling somewhere but by *changing modes*, slipping from the surface into the deep, the way a thought slips from speech into silence.

It is wrong, third, because the Veil is not *one thing*. The pre-Silence sciences treated it as a uniform medium beneath which spacetime could be folded. The post-Silence sciences have learned, painfully, that the Veil is layered: regions that behave one way, regions that behave very differently, zones where it is calm and zones where it is something close to alive. The Q-Net's collapse did not merely make Veil travel difficult. It revealed that

the Veil had always been more complicated than anyone realized, and that the Q-Net had been smoothing over the difficulty.

What can be said with confidence: the Veil exists. It is the medium of faster-than-light travel. Time inside it does not flow at the same rate or direction as time outside, which is the source of the Chronal Shear that made travel lethal between the Silence and the Pearl. It responds, measurably, to the emotional state of the conscious beings interacting with it, which is the Hope Frequency. And it is old, older, by the indirect evidence, than the universe in which we are speaking this sentence. Beyond that, almost everything is contested.

## HOW VEIL TRAVEL WORKS

**In play:** a Veil jump costs one Quantum Pearl and takes anywhere from hours to weeks of outside time, while the crew inside ages only seconds. The starship rules in Chapter 17 cover the mechanics. What follows is what a jump actually *is*.

The technology has three components, two that can be manufactured and one that cannot.

The first is the **Pearl Drive**, the propulsion and resonance assembly mounted on a ship's keel. Heavy, expensive, precisely calibrated, it is built around a central **resonance lattice** that suspends a Quantum Pearl at the moment of jump in perfect mechanical isolation while coupling it to drive, navigation, and life support. It is the most precise engineering in the post-Silence galaxy, the product of two centuries of inherited tradition, repairable by good mechanics, buildable from scratch only by the Hydros consortia and a handful of independent yards.

The second is the **navigational array**, the sensors and predictive systems that compute the route before the Pearl is spent. A jump is not a straight line. It is a path through a layered medium, planned against known Veil currents, recent storms, and the gravitational topology of the destination. The array integrates what no mind can integrate at speed and encodes the result into the lattice as a sequence of phase modulations, instructions for the Pearl to follow as it dies.

The third is the **Quantum Pearl** itself, and it cannot be made. Pearls are the biological product of the Chrono-Oysters of Hydros Prime, and a century of research has produced no synthetic equivalent. A successful jump destroys the Pearl in a flash of liberated temporal entropy.

The jump, as the crew lives it: the lattice charges off the main reactor. The Pearl is loaded by a trained engineer's hand, about ninety seconds of careful work. A low subsonic hum builds. The captain gives the order. For the next subjective ninety seconds the bridge lights flicker, the viewscreen shows a featureless white that is really the absence of any photons reaching the optics, the temperature drops three or four degrees for reasons nobody has explained, and there is no sense of motion at all. Most crews have a private word or gesture for this moment, the way old sailors touched the figurehead before a long voyage. Then the white breaks, the destination star is in the field, the drive disengages, and the Pearl is gone. Outside, hours or days or weeks have passed. The crew has aged ninety seconds.

There are no shortcuts. There is no alternative drive. Every Pearl burned came from a Chrono-Oyster, was harvested at a cost paid down the whole supply chain, and was consumed so the crew could be somewhere else. The Pearl Era runs on this, and the price is felt.

> **GEAR 1, NAMING THE PEARL** *(OPTIONAL ATMOSPHERIC RULE).* SOME CREWS NAME THEIR PEARLS BEFORE BURNING THEM. THIS SERVES NO MECHANICAL FUNCTION. IT IS A WAY OF ACKNOWLEDGING WHAT IS BEING PAID: A SINGLE USE, A SINGLE DEATH, A SINGLE UNIT OF THE THING THAT LETS THE CREW EXIST AS A CREW. THE NAMED PEARL IS MENTIONED AT THE START OF THE JOURNEY AND AGAIN AT THE END ("THERESA CARRIED US THROUGH. REST WELL, THERESA."). TABLES THAT PREFER FASTER PACING SIMPLY BURN THE PEARL AND CONTINUE.

## THE HOPE FREQUENCY

**In play:** this is the reason you roll a Hope die and a Fear die for nearly every meaningful action. The rules are in Chapter 9. What follows is what those dice *mean*.

The most striking discovery of the post-Silence century was not the Pearl. It was the slow, uncomfortable realization that the Veil *responds to the people inside it*.

The first observations were anecdotal. Veil-runners had said for decades that some routes "felt" different, that some lucky crews got through worse storms with less damage, that the same route flown twice could take wildly different durations. It was chalked up to imagination and confirmation bias. Most navigators learned to stop bringing it up.

The Solari Mystics took it seriously first. In the third decade after the Silence, a Mystic named Tova Marek began collecting crew reports systematically and correlating them against journey logs: recorded transit times, weather, route, ship status. After three years she presented a paper, *On the Possible Influence of Crew Affect on Veil Transit Duration*. It was politely received and quietly buried; the methodology was sound and the conclusion unbelievable. A decade later the Kurogane Research Division, funded in part to *disprove* the claim, replicated her results with greater rigor. The replication was devastating. The correlation was real, small (a few percent of journey duration on average), statistically robust, and explicable by no known mechanism.

Crews that flew in *hope*, confident, focused, bonded, had measurably shorter and smoother journeys than crews that flew in *fear*, anxious, divided, demoralized. The effect held across ship classes, routes, crews, and Pearl quality. Something about the emotional state of the beings inside the Stasis Bubble was reaching out, through the bubble, into the Veil, and changing its behavior. The phenomenon was named the **Hope Frequency**, in deference to the Spire's framing.

The picture that has emerged since is not one a pre-Silence physicist would have accepted. The Veil contains, somewhere in its substrate, a register that responds to coherent emotional states. Hope and fear are the clearest; love, grief, faith, and despair correlate at lower confidence. The register is *small*, the Veil does not bend to a single hopeful thought, but it is *cumulative*. A crew that spent three days knitting itself into a stable, hopeful unit travels better than one that spent three days fighting. A region where mass casualties recently occurred carries crueler currents than one at peace for decades. The Hope Frequency is, at the limit, the way the Veil *remembers what people have been doing*.

This is the cosmological foundation of *Veilfarers*. The Hope and Fear dice are not abstractions invented for the game. They are the dice the universe rolls in its own register. When your character spends Hope to do the impossible, they spend the same currency the Veil responds to. When a player's Fear-dominant noncritical Roll gives the Keeper Fear, that pressure ripples, very slightly but really, through the substrate.

The implications are large. A ship leaving a port where the crew was loved travels better than one leaving a port where the crew was hated. Crews that bond accumulate a real cosmic advantage; crews that fight each other do worse. A ship that has done genuine evil, slavery, mass killing, the breaking of meaningful promises, flies under a measurable burden. Many of the safest smuggling routes are simply the routes that have carried good people long enough that the Veil has grown used to them. A campaign whose moral choices matter is not only narratively satisfying. The mathematics of the Veil make it cosmically satisfying as well. The galaxy itself is a stakeholder in what the players choose.

> **GEAR 1, THE CREW'S RESONANCE** *(OPTIONAL ATMOSPHERIC RULE).* TABLES THAT WANT THE HOPE FREQUENCY PRESENT IN THE FICTION CAN TRACK A LOOSE "CREW WEATHER" BETWEEN JUMPS: AFTER A SESSION OF GENUINE BONDING, THE NEXT JUMP IS DESCRIBED AS SMOOTH AND QUICK; AFTER A SESSION OF FRACTURE AND CRUELTY, THE NEXT IS DESCRIBED AS LONG AND GRINDING. THIS IS COLOUR, NOT A MECHANICAL MODIFIER (THE DICE ALREADY CARRY THE WEIGHT). IT SIMPLY LETS THE TABLE FEEL THE VEIL NOTICING.

## THE LIVING VEIL: STORMS AND ANOMALIES

**In play:** these entries are descriptive travel phenomena and have no inherent mechanical effect. To use one as a hazard, select a complete printed environment feature or write its trigger, telegraph, targets, Roll, damage or Stress, duration, and end condition before the crew can be affected. Never add a retroactive effect merely because an anomaly appears.

**Veil Storms** are the most dangerous. A Storm is a region where the substrate has turned turbulent on a scale large enough to disrupt Pearl-driven transit. A ship caught in one during a jump can lose temporal coherence: the Stasis Bubble destabilizes, time begins to flow unevenly inside it, and the crew may live minutes that take hours, hours that take seconds, or worse. A ship that survives is changed by it. Crews often report vivid dreams of times and places they have never been, lingering echoes from the period when their Bubble was being beaten by the substrate. Some of those echoes turn out to be premonitions. Some are memories of futures that never came. Some are memories of futures that *did* come, for the crews who lived to see them.

**Chronal Eddies** are smaller and local, regions where time runs at an irregular rate, often spiralling, pulling a ship slightly out of synchronization with its expected arrival. A ship that hits one may arrive with its chronometer off by hours or days. Most are harmless once the crew adjusts. A few are inhabited, in some sense, by patterns nobody has identified.

**Memory Wakes** are the most philosophically unsettling, regions where the substrate appears to *retain* the emotional patterns of past travelers. A ship crossing one may find its crew flooded with feelings that are not their own: the grief of a refugee fleet that fled a century ago, the joy of a wedding party from the last decade, the rage of a battle that ended here in slaughter. The feelings are real, and they are not the crew's. Trained navigators usually recognize a Wake for what it is. Untrained crews sometimes mistake the borrowed emotion for their own and act on it, with consequences that can be tragic.

**Ghost Echoes** are the rarest of the routine phenomena and the strangest: encounters with what appear to be other ships, vessels matching the descriptions of ships lost in earlier eras, ships that flicker on the sensors and vanish, ships that broadcast distress calls on frequencies abandoned decades ago. Whether they are genuine remnants somehow preserved, or hallucinations born of the substrate's response to consciousness, or something else, nobody knows. The Free Fleet has a tradition: when a Ghost Echo is sighted, the crew salutes and continues on. It costs nothing to be polite, and the dead may be paying attention.

**Apex Threats** are the rarest of all and are not, properly, Veil phenomena. They are entities, beings, systems, or whatever the right word is, that appear to *live* in the Veil, observed rarely and briefly across the post-Silence century, never on demand. They are not understood. They do not seem to communicate, and they are rarely aggressive; most recorded encounters end with the Apex simply moving on, leaving the witnesses shaken and unharmed. But their existence is real and the implications are enormous, and they are the subject of ongoing intelligence work by every major power. The *Keeper's Companion* explores what is known and what is suspected.

## THE AWAKENED AND THE SLEEPING IN THE VEIL

**In play:** the choice between an Awakened (Threadbender) and a Sleeping (Threadwalker) character is made in Chapter 2; Awakened mechanics and Domain Powers live in Chapters 6, 7, 17, and 18. What follows is what the distinction means at the level of the substrate.

At its core, the distinction is about the Veil. A Threadwalker's relationship with it is the standard one: they exist in normal space, enter the Veil only via Pearl-driven ships, and cannot directly perceive or manipulate the substrate. A Threadbender's relationship is non-standard: with training, they can *perceive the substrate as it is*, and with greater training, *act on it directly*.

For Threadwalkers, the vast majority of every species, House, and culture, the Veil is something entered by technology and exited by technology, and that is the whole of it. They feel the Hope Frequency as everyone does, a faint background tone affecting their luck in ways too small to use. They live in the surface layer of reality. The Veil hums beneath them. They do not bend.

For Threadbenders, the rare individuals who can spend Hope to act on the substrate, the Veil is *available* in a way it is not to anyone else. A trained Mystic can feel the currents of the substrate the way a fish feels a river. An Awakened Pilot can sense the eddies and storms before the navigation computer flags them. A Vanguard who knows what they are doing can step partially out of normal space for fractions of a second, briefly inaccessible to ordinary harm. A Scholar who has trained their perception can read a region's local register, can tell at a glance whether a place has been the site of recent good or recent evil.

The crucial point: Threadbenders are not magical. Their abilities do not violate physics. They are physically real practitioners of a real but rare interface with the substrate, the same kind of thing as a Pearl Drive, scaled down to the individual. They are, in a sense, living Pearl Drives, beings whose biology has somehow been calibrated to exchange directly with the Veil.

Why some are born this way, nobody knows. The Mystics have one theory, the Kurogane researchers another, the Amaranth scholars a third, and the Volkov

clans a fourth that mostly involves not asking. The working consensus is only this: Threadbenders appear in every species at roughly one in forty thousand, the trait is not consistently heritable, and it cannot be reliably induced by any known training, technology, or intervention. They are born, and the universe does not explain why.

> **GEAR 2, THE THREADBENDER'S BURDEN** *(RECOMMENDED OPTIONAL).* Once per session, AT A TENSE MOMENT, THE KEEPER MAY ASK AN AWAKENED PLAYER WHAT THEIR CHARACTER SENSES IN THE SUBSTRATE THAT NO ONE ELSE CAN. THE PLAYER NARRATES A BRIEF IMPRESSION, AN EMOTION NOT THEIR OWN, A FLICKER IN THE DEEP, A SENSE OF BEING NOTICED, AND THE KEEPER FOLDS IT INTO THE NEXT SCENE. THE RULE REWARDS THE AWAKENED FOR AN INTERFACE THE REST OF THE CREW LACKS AND GIVES THE PLAYER A HAND IN THE CAMPAIGN'S METAPHYSICAL FABRIC. TABLES THAT PREFER CLEANER MECHANICS CAN SKIP IT; THE AWAKENED CLASSES WORK FULLY WITHOUT IT.

## THE PRECURSORS, AND WHY THE GALAXY FEELS LONELY

Underneath everything, the mechanics of Veil travel, the Hope Frequency, the existence of the Threadbenders, sits one question the post-Silence century has not been able to stop asking.

Why does the Veil exist?

The Veil is not just a feature of the universe. It is the substrate from which the rest seems to emerge, and it has at least one observable property, the Hope Frequency, that strongly implies it was *configured*. Configured for what? By whom? When? Almost everyone who studies the question seriously ends up looking back to the **Precursors**, the long-vanished prior civilization whose works predate biological life as we know it. The reasoning is plausible: the Veil is configured, the Veil is old, and the only thing in the record older than the Veil is the Precursors. If anyone configured it, they did. But this is correlation, not proof. The post-Silence sciences have no instrument that can read the Veil's authorship, if it has one.

What can be said with confidence is brief. **Precursor Vaults exist**, sealed structures of unfathomable age across hundreds of systems, holding artifacts that resist most analysis. **The Precursors themselves are missing**, no remains, no decipherable language, no historical record. **The Veil is real and the Hope Frequency is measurable**, and both feel, to anyone who has spent time inside them, like things someone arranged. Beyond that, the post-Silence understanding is competing theory.

The mainstream archaeological reading: the Precursors were a vanished prior species, perhaps several in succession, who built the Vaults and possibly built or modified the Veil before disappearing for reasons unknown. House Amaranth's archives hold this, arguing the details. House Kurogane's researchers hold a related, blunter view: they built things, we are learning how, the cosmology is a distraction. House Joric has no official view; the question is not operationally relevant. House Valerius regards Precursor sites as significant only insofar as their contents can be brokered.

There are religious readings too. Several Mystic traditions, most prominently the Spire of Verita on Solari Prime, hold that the Precursors were not a civilization at all but **a single distributed consciousness** that, having achieved cosmic-scale unity, found that unity unbearable and chose to engineer the conditions for other minds to exist. In this reading the Veil and the Hope Frequency are not infrastructure but *gestures*, the lingering trace of an ancient act of will. Some Solari Mystics speak of the Precursors with reverence approaching worship; most do not, and even within the Spire the reading is disputed by senior teachers who consider it elegant philosophy rather than testable cosmology. Other readings circulate: Kryllian engineers who insist the Precursors were simply a prior civilization with extraordinary materials science whose strangeness will yield to better tools; Ethereal scholars who suggest the Precursors are *not yet over*, that their vanishing is an artifact of temporal perception; Bloomstrider Groves who teach that the Precursors were the original gardeners and the post-Silence species are their crop, ripening for a purpose nobody has been told. Every Vault recovered produces new variations. None has produced an answer.

What you should take away as a player: the Precursor question is a real, open mystery in the setting. Different campaigns reach different conclusions. Some discover one of the existing theories is correct. Some find none are. Some leave it open, and that openness becomes part of the texture. The system supports all of these.

And here is the one thing the system commits to, independent of any cosmology. By every available proxy, the Veil and the Hope Frequency **reward beings who reach toward each other**. The Frequency rises in the presence of company. It thins in grief and isolation. The Veil is calmer in trafficked lanes and crueler in abandoned ones. Whether this is the trace of an ancient deliberate act, an emergent property of the substrate, or a

coincidence the eye is biased toward seeing, the system does not say. It simply notes, and asks the table to notice with it, that the universe of the Pearl Era behaves like a galaxy that prefers connection over solitude.

That, more than any theory, is the soul of *Veilfarers*. The Awakened can spend Hope to bend the universe because the universe, as observed, yields slightly to that spending. The Sleeping live without that lever, but their hopes still register, still ripple, still matter. Every campaign asks, in its own vocabulary, the same question all the cultures of the galaxy are asking in theirs: *can we be less alone in this?* The answer, in nearly every story worth telling, is yes, but not without cost, and not without choice, and not without the courage to keep reaching even when the dark does not always answer.

## WHAT THE GALAXY HAS INHERITED: THE VAULTS

**In play:** the five Vault classes below are a reference for exploration play. The deep mechanics of Vault delving live in the exploration material (*Stellar Frontier*) and the *Keeper's Companion*. Here they are setting, the thing your characters go *into*.

Across human-settled space, in patterns no cartographer has explained, stand structures nobody built and nobody now understands: the **Precursor Vaults**, remains of a civilization (or entity, or process) gone long before the first human-equivalent intelligence rose anywhere in the record. They predate the Silence by an order of magnitude no one has measured precisely. Some are weather-worn ruins half-buried in sediment. Some are sealed structures whose entry points remain, after a century of effort, perfectly inviolate. The rarest are *active*, performing functions older than the Silence and continuing, slowly, into the present.

The Vaults are the closest thing the post-Silence galaxy has to a frontier, and the closest thing it has to a *source*: most high-Tier equipment, most contested Precursor data, most artifacts in any House museum came, in some sense, out of a Vault. To manage the flood of independent expeditions and their contradictory reports, the **Imperial Vault Registry** was established in PE 17, classifying every catalogued Vault into one of five ascending classes:

- **Class I, Open Ruins.** Surface-accessible, partially mapped, regularly visited. The introductory class, the Vault every Voidwalker has heard of.

- **Class II, Standing Architecture.** Structurally intact, deep sectors unbreached, ongoing exploration. Where most working expeditions operate.

- **Class III, Active Anomalies.** Maintaining live Precursor functions whose purpose is not understood. Restricted access. Transformational rewards. Real lethality.

- **Class IV, Living Vaults.** Vaults that respond *intentionally* to the presence of visitors. Severely restricted. Once-in-a-career.

- **Class V, Sealed (Unbreachable).** Historically impossible to enter. Forty-seven catalogued; in the past eighteen months, nine have unsealed themselves without external action.

The Registry is taught at the Spire of Verita as standard introductory material. Most Voidwalkers will see no higher than Class II in a normal career. The career-changing finds, the ones that fund a fleet or write a name into the Imperial record, come from Class III and above. What is currently happening to the Class V catalogue, and what it might mean, is a question this book deliberately leaves for the table to discover in play.

## WHAT THIS BOOK HAS NOT TOLD YOU

There are deeper layers that this material has deliberately not addressed.

Where the Veil really comes from. What the Apex Threats really are, and what they want, if they want anything. Why some Vaults are sealed, and what is in the ones that have opened. Whether the Hope Frequency is *reading* consciousness or *constituting* it. Whether the Precursors still exist in some form, somewhere, in the substrate or beyond it. Whether the post-Silence species have a cosmic role they have not yet figured out, and if so, who is keeping the score.

These are the genuine mysteries of the *Veilfarers* setting. The Keeper's material addresses them the way mysteries should be addressed: with hints, with partial answers, with directions a campaign can take rather than verdicts it must accept. No published *Veilfarers* material gives a complete answer to any of them. That openness is deliberate. The mysteries are meant to stay mysteries until your table decides, through play, what they will mean for your campaign. Players who read the Keeper's material without permission will not find the truth. They will find a richer set of hints, and they will spoil the texture of their own discovery. Don't.

What you have read here is what every educated person in the post-Silence galaxy could, in principle, know, the surface that the texture rests on. Your campaign builds on this surface. What lies beneath is at your Keeper's table, where it belongs.

# APPENDIX A: QUICK START: A SPARK IN THE DARK

*"Out here, you're not defined by the world you came from, but by the promises you keep. And in the silence between stars, a promise is the only thing that's real. Break one, and you become a ghost long before you're*

*dead."*

Captain Eva Rostova, of the wandering ship The Stubborn Echo

## WELCOME TO THE VOID

This is *Veilfarers*. It is a galaxy of patched-up ships and patched-up souls, a century after a cataclysm called *the Great Silence* shattered civilization. The instantaneous communication network that bound the stars together went dark. Travel became unreliable. The very laws of physics began to fray at the edges.

You are not a chosen one or a god. You are a survivor, a pilot who sees paths in the chaos, an engineer who can breathe life into dead tech, an explorer who ventures where others fear to tread, a scoundrel who trades secrets in shadowed alleys, a vanguard who is a weapon of perfect discipline, or a mystic who feels the strange whispers of the Stellar Veil.

This appendix contains everything you need to play your first session of *Veilfarers*. It is a guide to the core rules, an introduction to the desperate, hopeful tone of the universe, and a complete starter adventure for a Keeper and 2-5 players. **You do not need to read the rest of this book to use it.** When you finish your first session and want more, more powers, more ancestries, more depth, that is when the rest of the chapters become useful.

For now: pick a character. Roll some dice. Walk into the dark with a crew.

## THE CORE MECHANIC: THE DANCE OF HOPE AND FEAR

*Veilfarers* is a story about the tension between hope and fear. This is represented by its core dice mechanic: the **Duality Dice**.

Whenever you attempt an action where the outcome is uncertain, you roll two twelve-sided dice (2d12) of different colors. One is your **Hope Die**. The other is your **Fear Die**.

### THE PROCESS OF A ROLL

1. **Roll both dice simultaneously.** 2. **Add the results together.** This sum is your base roll. 3. **Add your Trait Modifier** from one of your six core Traits (Agility, Strength, Finesse, Knowledge, Instinct, Presence), from -1 to +2. 4. **Compare to the Difficulty Class (DC).** The Keeper gives you a target number. If your final result is equal to or greater than the DC, you succeed. If less, you fail. 5. **Check which die was higher.** This is the most important step. It determines the *narrative consequences*.

### THE FIVE OUTCOMES

Every Roll produces one of five results; matching dice use Critical Success instead of either row or column below.

| RESULT | MEANING |
| --- | --- |
| **Success with Hope (Met DC, Hope > Fear)** | The goal succeeds. An Awakened character gains 1 Hope; a Sleeping character marks one Effort Track segment. No extra mechanical benefit appears unless a rule prints it. |
| **Success with Fear (Met DC, Fear > Hope)** | You achieve your goal, but with a cost or complication. The Keeper gains 1 Fear token, subject to the hard maximum of 12. |
| **Failure with Hope (Missed DC, Hope > Fear)** | The goal fails with a useful opening. An Awakened character gains 1 Hope; a Sleeping character marks one Effort Track segment. |
| **Failure with Fear (Missed DC, Fear > Hope)** | You fail, and the situation gets worse. The Keeper gains 1 Fear token, subject to the hard maximum of 12. |

**Critical Success.** If the physical Hope and Fear d12 faces match, including 1+1, the Roll is an automatic Critical Success. Clear 1 Stress. Awakened gain 1 Hope. Sleeping complete the Effort Track for 1 Effort and gain one further point in Effort or Resolve. Add at most one beneficial fictional detail consistent with established facts; it grants no extra resource, modifier, Action, item, or permanent benefit unless a feature prints one.

### HOPE AND FEAR TOKENS

**Hope** is the Awakened path resource. It can be spent to invoke an Experience (add a flat bonus to a roll), activate certain class features, or fuel Domain Powers. Sleeping characters run on **Effort** instead (Chapter 7); these pregenerated characters are all Awakened.

**Fear tokens** are the Keeper's resource. They are spent to trigger antagonist abilities, escalate scenes, and put pressure on the crew.

At session start, each Awakened player begins with **2 Hope**. The Keeper rolls **1d4+2** for starting Fear. Fear does not carry between sessions, has a hard maximum of **12**, and loses all excess.

## FORGING A QUICK SOUL: PRE-FORGED LEGENDS

For this Quick Start, you will use one of seven pre-generated character archetypes. Choose the one that speaks to you. Each is a complete character ready to play.

These characters are defined by six **Traits**, providing the modifiers for your rolls:

- **Agility** speed, reflexes, dexterity (combat dodging, piloting, athletic action)

- **Strength** raw physical power (lifting, melee force, endurance)

- **Finesse** precision, fine motor skill (ranged accuracy, stealth, tinkering)

- **Knowledge** learned skill (technology, science, lore, languages)

- **Instinct** intuition, perception, survival (noticing things, gut-feel decisions)

- **Presence** social weight, charisma (persuasion, deception, commanding attention)

Each character also has: - **HP** (Hit Points), physical resilience. When HP reaches 0, you are Dying. - **Stress** mental and emotional resilience. When Stress reaches its

cap, you become Overwhelmed: you cannot mark or spend more Stress, cannot pay Stress costs, and have Disadvantage on all Rolls until at least 1 Stress clears. - **Evasion** your defensive number. Enemies must meet or exceed it with an attack roll to strike you. - **Gear** what you carry. Armor reduces incoming damage. - **Starting Powers** special abilities you can use, fueled by Hope or Stress.

## THE SEVEN ARCHETYPES

> **Armor note.** Each archetype names an armor item. Use that item's current Armor Slots and damage thresholds from Chapter 13.

### ARCHETYPE 1: THE VOID RUNNER (CELESTIARI PILOT)

**Experience.** *"I was the first to chart a stable route through the treacherous Crimson Veil Storm."*

**Traits.** Agility +0, Strength +0, Finesse +2, Knowledge +1, Instinct +1, Presence -1

**HP** 6 | **Stress** 6 | **Evasion** 11

> **GEAR.** LIGHT FLIGHT SUIT, SLUG PISTOL, FRAYED STAR CHART, VEIL-ENERGY CONTROL CRYSTAL.

**Starting Powers.** - **Zero-G Drift** *(Void).* Spend 1 Hope. For 1 hour, ignore gravity/vacuum and gain Advantage on Agility Rolls for movement or avoiding detection. - **System Jackknife** *(Tech).* Spend 1 Hope. Make a Knowledge roll to control a nearby electronic system for 10 minutes.

**Playing Notes.** You are the ship's hands at the helm. Your Celestiari heritage gives you a deep relationship with the Veil, you *feel* its currents even when others cannot. You are also a survivor of the Veil Rip; you have seen too much to trust easily. Lead with action; the Voidrunner does, the Voidrunner does not explain.

### ARCHETYPE 2: THE CORPORATE ENFORCER (HUMAN SOLDIER)

**Experience.** *"I held the line during the Titan Station riots for 72 hours straight, with no backup."*

**Traits.** Agility +1, Strength +2, Finesse +0, Knowledge -1, Instinct +1, Presence +0

**HP** 7 | **Stress** 6 | **Evasion** 9

> **GEAR.** COMBAT ARMOR, ASSAULT RIFLE, DENTED RIOT SHIELD, FALLEN COMRADE'S DOG-TAG.

**Starting Powers.** - **Kinetic Strike** *(Kinetic).* Spend 1 Hope on a melee attack. Deals +1d4 damage and gains the Energy tag. - **Rapid Regeneration** *(Synthesis).* Spend 1 Hope when you or a nearby ally takes damage. The target heals 1d4+2 HP immediately.

**Playing Notes.** You served. You bled. You lost people you cared about. Now you carry their dog-tag and you bring discipline to every situation. You are not cynical, but you are *careful*. You expect betrayal because betrayal is what your old employers gave you. Lean into the Soldier's protectiveness, the crew is your responsibility now.

### ARCHETYPE 3: THE RELIC SEEKER (ETHEREAL SCHOLAR)

**Experience.** *"I activated a dormant Precursor beacon on a dead world and lived to tell the tale."*

**Traits.** Agility +0, Strength -1, Finesse +1, Knowledge +2, Instinct +1, Presence +0

**HP** 5 | **Stress** 6 | **Evasion** 10

> **GEAR.** ENVIRONMENTAL SUIT, HOLDOUT BLASTER, CRACKED DATA-SLATE, VIAL OF ALIEN SAMPLE.

**Starting Powers.** - **Environmental Adaptation** *(Synthesis).* Spend 1 Hope. For one hour, adapt your body to survive a hostile environment: vacuum, extreme temperature, toxicity, or radiation. - **Wayfinder's Pulse** *(Lux).* Spend 1 Hope. Emit a pulse, seen only by you, that reveals within Far range the nearest threat, the nearest exit or path, and any hidden objects of value. Direction, not detail.

**Playing Notes.** Your Ethereal body lets you slip through walls thinner than yourself; your scholar's training lets you read the world like a text. You came looking for Precursor knowledge and you stay because you found a crew that lets you keep looking. Curiosity is your strongest pull, sometimes stronger than your sense of self-preservation.

### ARCHETYPE 4: THE STREET MEDIC (KRYLLIAN ENGINEER)

**Experience.** *"I saved a dying colony with only spare parts, a roll of duct tape, and sheer determination."*

**Traits.** Agility -1, Strength +1, Finesse +1, Knowledge +2, Instinct +0, Presence +0

**HP** 7 | **Stress** 6 | **Evasion** 9

> **GEAR.** MESH ARMOR, PLASMA PISTOL, ALIEN-ETCHED MULTI- TOOL, UNIVERSAL LUBRICANT.

**Starting Powers.** - **Emergency Repair** *(Tech).* Mark 1 Stress. Touch damaged tech and make a Knowledge roll (DC 10). Success restores 2d6 HP and removes a malfunction. - **Biological Scan** *(Synthesis).* Spend 1 Hope. Touch a living creature. Learn its HP and health status. Knowledge roll (DC 10) reveals diseases or cybernetics.

**Playing Notes.** Four arms. Compound eyes. A mind that sees the universe as a beautiful, malfunctioning machine and a heart that refuses to let people die from broken parts. The Kryllian engineering tradition treats fixing as worship, and you have made the crew your temple. You will weld a hull breach and stitch a wound with the same focused calm.

### ARCHETYPE 5: THE TRADE AMBASSADOR (HUMAN DIPLOMAT)

**Experience.** *"I personally brokered the peace treaty that ended the bloody Outer Rim Trade War."*

**Traits.** Agility +0, Strength -1, Finesse +0, Knowledge +1, Instinct +1, Presence +2

**HP** 6 | **Stress** 6 | **Evasion** 10

> **GEAR.** FINE CLOTHES (ARMOR 1), NEEDLE GUN, ENCRYPTED DATAPAD, TREASURED TOKEN (A MEMENTO FROM A LONG-DEAD MENTOR).

**Starting Powers.** - **Silver Tongue** *(Social).* Spend 1 Hope, make the Presence Spellcast Roll, and resolve the current card text in Chapter 19. Do not add character Level unless the card itself directs it. - **Spark of Hope** *(Lux).* Spend 1 Hope. Touch an ally within Close range; they clear 1 Stress. You cannot target yourself.

**Playing Notes.** You believe in *words* the way Soldiers believe in *bullets*. You think every fight is a fight someone failed to *prevent*. Your Token reminds you that someone, somewhere, believed enough in you to teach you this, and that loss never quite stopped echoing. You speak with weight because you remember what was lost when the speaking failed.

### ARCHETYPE 6: THE VEIL TOUCHED (CELESTIARI MYSTIC)

**Experience.** *"I once walked through a Veil storm unprotected and emerged with visions of the future."*

**Traits.** Agility +0, Strength +0, Finesse -1, Knowledge +1, Instinct +2, Presence +1

**HP** 6 | **Stress** 6 | **Evasion** 10

> **GEAR.** LIGHT ARMOR, HOLDOUT BLASTER, WHISPERING VEIL-CRYSTAL, STARLIGHT BLINDFOLD.

**Starting Powers.** - **Veil Sensitivity** *(Neural).* Spend 1 Hope. For 10 minutes, sense emotions and surface thoughts of creatures in Close range. - **Telekinetic Grasp** *(Neural).* Presence Spellcast Roll (DC 10). For 1 minute, move a single object within Far range (up to 50 lbs) with the precision of your own hands, or hurl it at a target for (Proficiency)xd6 Void damage.

**Playing Notes.** The Veil has *spoken* to you, and you have not entirely come back from that conversation. Other Celestiari treat you with respect tinged with worry. You sometimes know things you should not know. You have learned to keep the blindfold on when you do not want to *see*, because Veil sight is not always a gift. Lean into the strangeness; let it make the crew uncomfortable, and let them love you anyway.

### ARCHETYPE 7: THE INFO BROKER (SYNTHETIC SCOUNDREL)

**Experience.** *"I sold the secret location of a lost treasure fleet to three different buyers and escaped before they realized."*

**Traits.** Agility +0, Strength -1, Finesse +2, Knowledge +1, Instinct +1, Presence +0

**HP** 6 | **Stress** 6 | **Evasion** 12

> **GEAR.** STEALTH ARMOR, GAUSS PISTOL, MORPHIC SKELETON KEY, INFLUENTIAL HOLO-MASK.

**Starting Powers.** - **Data Ghost** *(Tech).* Mark 1 Stress. Choose a security system you interacted with. Knowledge roll (DC 15). Success erases all records of your presence. - **Perfect Facade** *(Social).* Spend 1 Hope. Create a perfect disguise for 1 hour. Advantage on Presence rolls to maintain the deception.

**Playing Notes.** You are a Synthetic, a forged person, and your relationship with your manufactured origin is complicated. You learned early that *information* travels further than bullets and pays better than honest work. You sell secrets, you keep secrets, and somewhere in the middle of all that you are slowly discovering which secrets are *yours*. The Skeleton Key opens locks; the Mask hides faces. You decide which to use.

## THE RULES OF SURVIVAL: THINGS YOU WILL NEED

### ADVANTAGE AND DISADVANTAGE

When a roll has special favorable conditions, you have **Advantage**: roll an additional d6 and add it to your total. When circumstances are working against you, you have **Disadvantage**: roll an additional d6 and *subtract* it. Only one such die ever applies. They do not stack from multiple sources, and if both Advantage and Disadvantage are in play they **cancel out** - you roll neither.

### ECHOES OF THE VEIL: POWERS

Each archetype has Starting Powers from one or two of the seven Domains (Tech, Synthesis, Social, Neural, Kinetic, Void, Lux). To use a Power, spend the indicated cost (Hope, Stress, or both) and follow the Power's effect. Every Power uses its printed trigger, target, range, cost, Roll, effect, duration, and end condition. If an entry omits one of these, the effect is incomplete and cannot create an additional mechanical consequence by implication.

The full Catalog of Powers is in Chapter 19 of this book. For your first session, the two Powers on your archetype card are all you need.

### CONFLICT AND HARM

When attacked, the attacker rolls 2d12 + their attack Trait. If they meet or exceed your **Evasion**, the attack hits. They then roll damage and compare the total to your two **Damage Thresholds** (Major and Severe, listed on your sheet): below Major marks **1 HP**, at or above Major marks **2 HP**, at or above Severe marks **3 HP**. You may spend one **Armor Slot** to drop a hit one step (Severe to Major, Major to Minor, Minor to no HP at all). Mark the resulting HP.

When all your HP are marked, you are **Dying**. You cannot take Actions or Maneuvers. At the beginning of each of your Spotlights while Dying, roll 1d12; on an 8 or higher, mark 1 Dying Progress. At 2 Dying Progress, enter Final. While Final, roll the same way and mark Final Progress; at 2 Final Progress, you die.
