# APPENDIX C: VERSION CONTROL

## 11.1-RC2 DRAFT 3 - EQUIPMENT BENCHMARK

The Core equipment catalog is explicitly canonical and Rust & Steel additive. Phase Blade and Phase Pistol prices were corrected to WT3. Riot Armor was reclassified as Military TT2, reduced to 5 Armor Slots, and repriced to WT2. The Suppressor modification now matches the expansion's standard model. Equipment data gained Burden, family, weight-class, and benchmark metadata. PDFs were not regenerated in this pass.


**11.1-RC2-draft2** - Complete Sleeping Mystic redesign. The class now uses the Uncanny Archive, Domain Study Projects, Calibrated Minor Rituals, and Uncanny Power. Starting characters unlock every Level 1 Power in two chosen Domains; higher Domain levels require breadth at the preceding level. Uncanny Power spends Resolve, generates Fear per die, uses Knowledge for both access and control, and resolves against DC 10 + Domain level. A Critical Success refunds all Resolve spent on that invocation while retaining generated Fear and other costs. The Veil Walker now specializes in layered group rituals, the Mind-Touched in direct and over-level manifestations, and the Precursor Touched in accelerated and parallel research. The Awakened Mystic is unchanged.

**11.0.1** - Two-column readability pass. Compact page-spanning tables now sit at explicit flow breaks, extensive catalogs move to dedicated full-width pages, and text after every wide table restarts unambiguously in the left column. Short H3 modules such as Hope Features, Class Features, and Background Questions are kept intact within a single column when they fit. Table type was enlarged for print legibility. No rules or setting content changed.


**11.0** - Release and pagination pass. The 147-power catalog and B1 canon corrections were retained; playtest writing fields now render as ruled lines, Contents page references were regenerated from the final PDF, orphaned end-of-section fragments were repaired, blank augmentation Stress cells were normalized, and final copyediting removed residual untranslated metadata.


**11.0-B2** - Domain catalog normalization. All 147 powers now use the canonical metadata line with Type, Cost, DC and explicit Trait, and Recall Cost. Twelve mechanically incomplete powers were fully rewritten from the approved systemic review; reaction triggers and usage frequencies are explicit. Bare Core Trait Rolls and untyped Spellcast Rolls in the catalog were normalized, consent language was added where powers can affect another PC, and residual Armor Score terminology in power effects was converted to temporary Armor Slots. A matching canonical powers JSON was generated for the Character Creator.


**11.0-B1** - Canon correction pass. Product-name residues were normalized to VeilFarers. Starting Hope and Rest/Recovery are now defined in Chapter 9; the Quick Start matches the 2-Hope session reset. Sleeping-compatible ancestry resource wording was applied to Irrepressible Curiosity, Stellar Meditation, and Chrono-Gift. Multiclass Mastery now clearly remains available for the original Class. Active Armor Score references were retired in favor of Armor Slots, and Emergency Repair now uses Knowledge rather than the nonexistent Tech Trait.

## VERSION CONTROL

**12.06 (editorial corrections pass)** - Applied reserved 12.06 errata and one Path redesign. Errata: the Vanguard's Kinetic Echo Mastery (Echoing Strike) now deals Kinetic damage to match its branch element, not Void; the Pilot's Veil Surge drops a redundant "minimum 0" clause its own trigger already guarantees; the Ethereal ability is named Phase Shift throughout prose (its former name Liminal Presence remains only as a glossary deprecation pointer). Typography aligned to house standard. Path redesign - Path to Nirvana and the Disciplined State (mirrored): both now run on an Integrity Die instead of a flat "Spotlights equal to Proficiency" timer, superseding the note in the entry below. Why (documented because this is a mechanical redesign, not an errata, in an already-published edition): a flat timer scales duration by level but never makes the state feel different across Tiers and gives the player no in-state decision. The Integrity Die - a Tier-sized step-track (d4/d6/d8 at Tier 1/2/3, counting down from its highest face; the inverse of the Soldier's Focus Die) - turns duration into a resource: rolling with Fear erodes it, so the state rewards deciding when to act, and it models mastery as resilience under fear rather than as a longer buff. The new Breaking Point option ends the state for a closing strike of (Proficiency)d6, spendable at a chosen moment; that bonus is added once after multipliers and never doubles on a Critical, keeping it devastating at high Tier but bounded. The Hearts in the Void pregen was synchronized to the same model.

**12.06** - Release consistency and source-cleanup pass. Corrected the Guardian's Unbreakable threshold names; unified Maren's Presence, Experiences, and worked rolls with her finished sheet; advanced the line authority markers to 12.06; and removed internal review scaffolding. The underlying Duality, Path, advancement, combat, economy, and ship procedures are unchanged.

**12.05** - Personal-scale defenses and cross-scale damage.

- Added **Natural Thresholds (no armor)** in Chapter 10: a character wearing no armor uses base Damage Thresholds of Major 2 / Severe 4. This was previously undefined.
- Added an ancestry-scale gift for **Kryllian** (Chitin Plating), **Rift Spinner** (Crystalline Carapace) and **Synthetic** (Alloy Chassis): while unarmored, their base Damage Thresholds are Major 4 / Severe 6. Wearing armor overrides these values in the usual way.
- Reworked **Ship Weapons Against Personnel** in Chapter 17 and the Sacred System Bible entry: naval damage is now resolved in full including Critical effects, multiplied by ×5 after Mount Rating, and applied through halved Major and Severe Thresholds (rounding up) rather than through Direct HP Damage. HP loss continues past 0: exactly 0 HP is Dying with the Death Move available; -1 HP or lower is killed outright and cannot make a Death Move. The previous ×2 / Direct HP procedure is retired.
- Glossary entry for Ship-scale harm updated to match.
- Chapter 17 counterplay list: the entry for disabling the targeting system was rewritten. It previously said the shot went to "double Disadvantage," a stack that the core rule (Chapter 1, Chapter 21) does not allow; it now reads as the shot cannot resolve until targeting is restored, matching the other three options in that list.

**12.04** - Naval scale clarification pass. Naval mount Proficiency was renamed and redefined as **Mount Rating (MR)**, a hull-scale statistic rather than character Proficiency. Base Ship Evasion is now standardized by scale at 16 / 12 / 8 and MR at ×1 / ×2 / ×3. Naval weapon tables no longer carry a PROF field. Ship weapons against personal-scale targets now use naval damage ×2, allowing explicit personal shields and damage-reduction effects to function before remaining damage becomes Direct HP Damage; one Armor Slot may reduce that Direct HP Damage by 1. Sensor Lock is restricted to vehicle- and starship-scale targets; personal Guided and tracking mechanics remain separate. No printed naval weapon damage expressions, Hull values, Armor Slots, Heat Caps, or personal Proficiency rules changed.

**12.03** - Surgical canon correction pass. The 12.02 Wealth ladder of DC 10 / 15 / 20 / 25 / 30 is ratified as the current economic tone. Criminal Heat remains one crew-wide 0-10 score by default, with Rust & Steel Chapter 2.3 as its only procedure; Individual and Factional Heat remain explicitly adopted, mutually exclusive options, and Keeper’s Companion now expands management rather than creating a competing track. The Sacred System Bible, glossary, and Publication Gate now state that Spotlight is dynamic and cannot be determined by a contest, Roll, initiative, modifier, Advantage, Disadvantage, or speed; active Spotlight contest text was retired from Corebook, Keeper’s Companion, and Rust & Steel. Silent Alarm now creates a prepared ambush through the ordinary Fear procedure. Rust & Steel’s five personal Disruptor entries now use the central additional-damage-die procedure rather than double damage, and Smart Rifle and Seeker Sniper retain normal attacks against Evasion. No PDF was regenerated in this source pass.

**12.02** - Canon lock and line-wide stability pass. Fear has a hard maximum of 12 at every gain; matching Duality Dice, including 1+1, have one Critical Success procedure and every retired negative-critical trigger now uses Failure with Fear. Sensor Lock, Path rules, rest, damage, ship Heat, criminal Heat separation, mount Proficiency, naval tags, damage tags, action timing, Power activation, drone installation, Domain Study Projects, Hivemind Convergence, Universal Life Force, and worked examples were synchronized. Arbitrary and duplicate procedures were replaced with declared triggers and complete outcomes, and an obsolete Chapter 20 glossary reference was repaired. Development-only notes were removed. The final Sacred System Bible defines the non-negotiable rules and publication gate for every book.

**12.01** - Sensor Lock definition pass, superseded where noted by 12.02. Added Sensor Lock as a Sensors-station Knowledge Roll using Adjacent 5, Engagement 10, Standard 15, Long 20, and Extreme 25, granting Advantage on the next Gunner attack and then being spent, with its break procedure. Added the Death Move and corrected glossary references. The former ship-scale exclusion was retired in 12.02: ship-scale harm now preserves Dying, Final, and the voluntary Death Move. Also corrected Quick Start Power access, Saber's thresholds, Resistance Rolls, and Pushed.

**12.00** - Unified editorial release. Integrated the approved Core revisions over the complete 11.35 canonical base, including the Chapter 6 feature replacements, the two-Slot multiclass model for both Paths, the Sleeping multiclass Dormant Domain and Resolve Move, and the event-driven Sleeping-to-Awakened procedure. The Core provides no ordinary Awakened-to-Sleeping transition; Refused remains available as a pre-play history or identity, while exceptional reverse conversion belongs to Keeper-facing events. Restored and verified The Galaxy in Depth and every untouched lore section, rebuilt navigation and final PDF pagination, and synchronized the complete editorial package.

**11.35** - Process transparency pass. The legal page now states how the line is made: AI-assisted throughout production, with all game design, worldbuilding, and editorial judgment the author's. A closing colophon, How This Book Was Made, pairs that statement with an open invitation to artists, proofreaders, and playtesters through the VeilFarers portal. No rules changed.

**11.34** - Artwork note. The legal page now carries the generative-art disclosure, framed as an open invitation: the generated interior artwork stands as a placeholder for real art and is in no way meant to replace human artists, and artists who wish to collaborate are invited to reach out through the feedback section of the VeilFarers portal. Cover version line corrected. No rules changed.

**11.33** - Heraldry integration. The Chapter 5 affiliation entries now open with their faction crests set in the text flow: the seven Great Houses, the Free Fleet, the Explorers' Guild, the Solara Compact and the Stellar Commerce Guild, plus the independents' seal (broken chains) on Choosing Your Affiliation - twelve tagged figures, each with alt text. House signature marks are packaged as brand assets and are not used in the interior. No rules changed.

**11.32** - Front matter pass. Added product front matter: a typographic cover and a legal and credits page carrying the copyright notice, the Darrington Press Community Gaming License attribution for the Daggerheart System Reference Document 1.0, the trademark and non-affiliation statement, and typeface and accessibility credits. Front matter pages are unnumbered; Contents repaginated. No rules changed.

**11.31** - Bookmark titles pass. The eighteen class-opening bookmarks in the PDF navigation tree, generated from the banner headings, now carry their class names instead of empty labels. No content, rules, or layout changed.

**11.3** - Human ancestry expansion. Humans gain a fourth Ancestry Gift, **Inheritance of the Builders (Choose One at Character Creation)**: a free augmentation of Common (TT1) or Military (TT2) with no drawbacks, where Common (TT1) does not consume an Augment Slot and Military (TT2) occupies one, its expression (genetic modification, mutation, or chrome) chosen by the player; or one item of equipment of Experimental (TT3) access and 9 Cr (WT3) value from any catalog in play. A starting-ship option was evaluated and rejected as a group-composition incentive problem; its salvage, "The Claim", is set aside as a Keeper campaign-opening hook. Data packs and the Character Creator must be updated to include the new gift.

**11.2** - Accessible re-layout and art integration pass. The whole book was rebuilt paragraph by paragraph for tagged PDF output under ISO 14289-1 (PDF/UA-1), ISO 32000 and WCAG 2.2 (1.3.2 Meaningful Sequence, 2.4.3 Focus Order): true heading, list and table structure with header cells, logical reading order, decorative page backgrounds as artifacts, and alt text on every figure. Typography moved to the embedded Aller family (Display for chapter and ancestry titles, Light for headings, 8 pt body), with chapter and ancestry titles enlarged and centered as section presentations. Catalog groups (weapons, armor, augmentations, drones) are re-laid as full-width self-contained boxes with the table first and item descriptions below, applied identically to every group so the visual order always matches the reading order. The class banner block was restored on all eighteen class openings. Nine ancestry portraits and seven community scenes were integrated with alt text. Editorial purity: Unicode arrows are written as "->", decorative emoji were removed, and gear complexity is standardized as gear icons (Gear N shows N gears) applied at layout. Source corrections in this pass: the all-caps Concealed gear passage was restored to sentence case, unbalanced emphasis asterisks were normalized across the manuscript, and the Pulse of Genesis stat line, accidentally left in Spanish, was restored to English ("All remaining Hope (minimum 5)"). Contents regenerated against the final pagination. No rules changed.

**11.1-RC3** - Canon integration pass. Added the prepared Drill system for the Sleeping Soldier, revised Soldier Resolve Moves and Effort economy, rebuilt the Sleeping Vanguard, expanded the canonical Conditions list, and established the unarmed-strike baseline. Regenerated the Corebook PDF and synchronized portal downloads and rules data.

**11.1-RC2-draft6** - Manuscript and data synchronization pass. Rebuilt page-neutral Contents, repaired and alphabetized the Core glossary, added the Sleeping Mystic ritual/research terminology and House Kaelen, inserted class and subclass bookmark markers for the next PDF render, removed a stale Sleeping Mystic Stress example, and synchronized all four consolidated sources and canonical metadata. Final page numbers remain deferred to the PDF candidate render.

**This copy: VeilFarers Corebook 12.06 canonical editorial release. Rules canon: 12.06.**

Project rules in force across all versions: no em dashes; single-Trait Rolls; matching Duality Dice always resolve as Critical Success; the worst nonmatching result is Failure with Fear; the present day is about 103 years after the Great Silence.

Versioning note: the whole line shares a unified decimal version. Increments of 0.01 mark minor revisions; increments of 0.1 mark major ones.

**10.95** - Armor tables brought onto the Tech Tier standard set in 10.94. The three armor tables (Light, Medium, Heavy) now carry a **TECH TIER** column and their rows are ordered by Tech Tier within each weight class. Following the project-wide convention, every Tech Tier is written as the tier name with its code in parentheses: **Common (TT1)**, **Military (TT2)**, **Experimental (TT3)**, **Precursor (TT4)**; this format was applied to every equipment table in the chapter, weapons included, and to the inline gear notes. The legacy **A.S.** (Armor Score) column, already flagged as removed in the armor rules, was deleted from all three tables, and the **SHIELDS** column was renamed **ARMOR SLOTS** to match the unified term used everywhere else; the values are unchanged, so no character's soak pool changes. Tier assignments follow each armor's own description: civilian and frontier gear at Common (TT1), House-regular and professional gear at Military (TT2), and post-Silence, prototype, and top-line gear at Experimental (TT3); no armor is Precursor (TT4). Two stat adjustments were made in the same pass: **Power Armor** moves to **25 Cr (WT5)**, matching Siege Armor at the top of the price ladder, and both Power Armor and Siege Armor are fixed at **Experimental (TT3)** access (they are House-manufactured, not found Precursor artifacts). The **Railgun** was corrected to **d8+3** damage. A Common-tier medium armor, the **Homestead Rig** (6 / 13, Armor Slots 3, *Flexible*, 4 Cr), was added so the Medium table has an entry at Common (TT1) access; it fills the gap between the light frontier gear and the professional Military medium armors. Three NPC example loadouts that still used the old "Tier N, A.S. N" notation were updated to the tier name with Armor Slots. The armor rules note that referenced the retired A.S. column was rewritten to describe the clean state.

**10.94** - Equipment tables: notation standard and a fixed table. Two axes that were blurred are now shown separately in every Chapter 13 table. Access is the **Tech Tier**, printed in a **TECH TIER** column as **TT1** (Common), **TT2** (Military), **TT3** (Experimental), **TT4** (Precursor). Price is the **Wealth Tier**, printed in the Cost column as **N Cr (WTx)** on the ladder 1 Cr (WT1), 4 Cr (WT2), 9 Cr (WT3), 16 Cr (WT4), 25 Cr (WT5); non-consumable gear sits on these values, while consumables may fall between them and show the fraction, for example 2 Cr (1/2 WT2). The chapter's tier and cost prose was rewritten to teach this. **This TT and WT notation is now the project-wide standard** and will be carried into the remaining line, Rust and Steel especially, as each book is next revised. Separately, the **Neural Augmentations** table was corrected: it had been a duplicate of the Stealth table (which also printed the same rows one page later), so the four neural augments the section describes in prose (Memory Chip, Pain Suppressor, Combat Reflexes, Combat Precognition) had no stats. The real table was written from those descriptions and inserted; the Stealth table now appears once, under its own heading.

**10.93** - Presentation. The Sleeping chapter (Chapter 7) now prints on a light silver page background (RGB 250, 250, 245), a subtle tint that sets the path apart from the Awakened chapter without affecting legibility; applied via a full-page field behind the text on that chapter's pages only, so no other chapter is touched. No text or rules changed.

**10.92** - Index integrity pass and license attribution. Stale glossary and page references were corrected, obsolete entries removed, and the formal Attribution section was added.

**10.91** - Structural pass on Chapter 7. The chapter-end "Sleeping Resolve Moves (Complete Menu)" section was dissolved: each class's Class Moves and Subclass Moves now live inside that class's entry, in a Resolve Moves section placed after Subclasses, so a class reads as one self-contained unit. The universal Bear Down and the Move economy explanation moved up into the Resolve rules section at the head of the chapter. The entry-anatomy reading guide was updated to match. Contents and the Appendix B index were repaginated against the rebuilt PDF (chapters 8 through 19 and the appendices shifted by one page). No rules text changed; this aligns the chapter layout with the guide's own promise that Moves are part of each entry.

**10.9** - Feature flavor pass on the Sleeping classes (Chapter 7), with two mirrored Diplomat changes in Chapter 6. Triggered by review finding that the Sleeping catalog leaned on two repeated mechanical verbs, "pay Effort and the Keeper reveals information" and "declare retroactive preparation", so several classes played identically at the table even where they read differently. Two design rules were adopted for the pass: every class carries at least one mechanical verb no other class has, and features should change the fiction, not only the roll. All new text is written short, rule first, for direct use on the sheet.

**New and rebuilt features.** The Scholar was rebuilt around the applied-scientist fantasy: The Cited Authority became **Applied Science**, dropping the two pure information options (The Fact, The Connection) for **The Countdown** (state how long a process in motion truly has; the table now plays against that clock) and **The Improvised Reaction** (one immediate chemical effect from scene materials), keeping The Lost Source. Its three Specializations were rebuilt to match: the Xenobiologist's The Field Sample became **The Synthesis** (neutralize an organism's toxin or lure it, from a sample or a minute of study), the Precursor Archaeologist's The Recovered Document became **As Built** (learn what a Precursor structure was built to do and where its deactivation mechanism is; reaching it is your problem), and the Information Theorist's The Triangulation became **The Model** (declare a system's behavior for the next hour, or inject one false datum it treats as legitimate). The Engineer's The Workaround, a retro-preparation duplicate, became **Never Rated For This** (push a machine one tier above grade for the scene, then it breaks, you describe how). The Explorer's The Survey became **The Margin Note** (declare one recorded physical feature of the surroundings; it is there, one Keeper complication allowed, no note rewrites a premise), and the Wilderness Specialization Make Camp grew into **The Old Craft** (We Camp Here, The Weather Turns, or Live Off This), absorbing Make Camp's Stress bonus. The Soldier's Military Officer Mastery The Standing Force became **One Way Out** (once per arc, organize non-combatant NPCs into coordinated action while your voice holds). The Vanguard's Disciplined State gained two lines: reading the room on entry (who is dangerous, who is bluffing, who breaks first) and Disadvantage on melee attackers beyond the first each round while outnumbered. The Diplomat gained **Protocol** inside its Class Feature (always know the correct form for cultures in common knowledge; roll Knowledge to read unknown ones from behavior; once known, offense is a choice, never an accident).

**Influence now scales with the roll.** A boxed rule in both Diplomat entries: Success reaches those present for the scene, with Hope it holds after you leave, a Critical spreads beyond the room, and with Fear it turns on you. Two Masteries were rebuilt on it: the Awakened Icon's Defining Moment became **The Address** (speak to a crowd, DC by size and hostility, themes preserved on a critical) and the Sleeping Cultural Attache's The Translator's Authority became **The Reconciliation** (mediate between willing parties, DC by depth of grievance; a critical buries the grievance itself).

**Moves pass.** Every class Move that only added the rolled total gained a one-line narrative rider so it leaves a mark beyond the roll: Force of Presence (what they yield, they yield before witnesses), The Ledger Remembers (the obligation becomes established fact), Ghost in the Logs (the intrusion is attributed to whoever you choose), Run It Down (the quarry knows it is hunted), Decipher (what you decipher stays deciphered), Dig-Site Discipline (your markers remain for the next team), Stand Down (word spreads you ended it without blood). The Pilot Move Thread the Needle became **Never Tell Me the Odds** (attempt the impossible maneuver with Advantage by declaring a true, permanent quirk of this hull; on a Fear-dominant noncritical Roll the ship pays, not the crew), which also resolves its name collision with the Chapter 17 ship maneuver of the same name.

**Renames for collisions.** The Mind-Touched Resolve Move Cold Read is now **The Clinical Eye** (its Effort Foundation keeps The Cold Read); the Vanguard Ghost Blade Mastery The Vanishing is now **The Folded Exit** (the Scoundrel Ghost keeps The Vanishing). Separately, the Chapter 12 advancement example (Maren) was found to be written against an older Power catalog: eight of its named Powers (Lane Reading, Veil Sense, The Steady Hand, Void Currents, Cold Read, Reading the Substrate, Folded Step, Diagnostic Pulse) no longer exist in Chapter 19, and its Vault listed a Power the example never acquired, and her Foundation cited the Sleeping Void Runner's The Quiet Lane instead of the Awakened Pathfinder's Sense. All were repointed to current material (Vector Calculus, Temporal Muffle, Emergency Repair, Slipstream Jolt, Veil Sensitivity, Temporal Glimpse, Phase Walk, Pathfinder's Sense), which also retires the Cold Read name-share outright: the Mind-Touched Foundation The Cold Read now owns the name alone. The duplicated 10.71 block in this appendix was removed.

**10.8** - Structural and navigational pass. Four changes. A **Contents** page was added at the front, listing every chapter and appendix with the page it begins on. **Appendix B was rebuilt from a clogged glossary into a proper glossary-and-index**: the entries had been mashed several to a paragraph and partly out of alphabetical order; each term is now its own entry, correctly alphabetized, carrying its category, a working definition, the chapter or chapters where it lives, and the page where it is explained (selective by design, the page points to where a term is defined or substantially treated, not to every passing mention). The **class entries (Awakened and Sleeping) now open with their visual class emblems** (the banner-and-flag treatment), each starting on a fresh page. And the **Quick Start's simplified Starter Adventure was removed from the Corebook**; the full version of that adventure already lives in the Keeper's Companion (Chapter 17), so the Corebook no longer carries a lesser duplicate. Page references throughout the new Contents and index were generated against the final paginated PDF in a two-pass build.

**10.71** - Two layout and cleanup fixes. Twenty stray page numbers had been left embedded at the ends of paragraphs (mostly Mastery features and equipment entries), debris from an old copy-paste out of a PDF, for example a "55" trailing the Scoundrel's The Long Con; all twenty were removed without touching the surrounding text. And the page breaks added in 10.7 were landing class and Domain openings in the right-hand column rather than on a clean new page, because a plain page break only breaks to the next column inside a two-column layout; the break now uses a new-page section break (re-applying the two-column format), so every class and Domain starts genuinely at the top of a fresh page.

**10.7** - Two changes: per-class Common access, and layout.

The Technology Access tables gained a **Common (Tier 1) row** for every class, on both paths. Previously Common was treated as universal (anyone could use any basic gear); now a class is trained only in some Common categories, so a Diplomat is not trained on rifles even at Common, and never becomes so. The Chapter 13 definition of the Common tier was corrected to match (Common gear needs no access *level*, but still falls into gear *categories* your class may or may not be trained in), and a "Weapons and gear outside your access" rule was added beside the armor rule: using a weapon family your class is not trained on imposes **Disadvantage on attacks made with it** regardless of the weapon's tier, while augments and equipment outside your access cannot be operated until trained. Each class's Common row was derived as the core of its profile (its basic weapons, its light armor, and its characteristic augments), with Military adding new categories as real progression.

**Layout:** every class entry (Awakened and Sleeping) and every Domain in the Catalog of Powers now begins on a fresh page, for cleaner reading and reference. The table of contents was regenerated to match the new pagination.

**10.6** - Restored the per-class Technology Access tables, which had been lost. The Proficiency Tier system (Common, Military, Experimental, Precursor) survived in Chapter 13, and the advancement option to raise Technology Access survived in Chapter 12, but the class-specific tables that say which gear each class trains into had gone missing, leaving a broken cross-reference: Chapter 13 stated the tables "are listed in each Class entry (Chapters 6 and 7)" while no such tables were there. Each of the nine classes now carries its Technology Access table in its Core Stats, on both paths (a class trains into the same gear regardless of path). The categories were reconciled to the current Chapter 13 catalog: the retired "Sensory Augments" category folded into Physical Augments (the Sensory Package now lives under Physical), while weapon, armor, equipment, and modification categories mapped directly. Each table shows the class's Military (Tier 2, level 2) and Experimental (Tier 3, level 5) access; Common (Tier 1) is universal and Precursor (Tier 4) is story-gated.

The access summary: the Soldier trains the broadest combat access (all armor, all weapons); the Engineer the broadest technical access (all augments, modifications, and equipment); the Pilot mid-weight armor and the full weapon range; and the Mystic, Scholar, and Diplomat the lightest (Light Armor, sidearms, Neural and Physical augments), with the Scoundrel, Explorer, and Vanguard in specialized middle bands.

The armor restriction was made mechanical instead of a soft note. Where Chapter 13 previously said class armor limits were "narrative, not absolute," it now states that wearing armor above your class's access imposes **Disadvantage on everything involving movement** (Agility, maneuvers, evasion, climbing, piloting while worn): a Mystic can put on Heavy plate, but moves as if underwater in it until the access is trained.

**10.5** - Deep balance and consistency pass on the nine Sleeping classes (Chapter 7), with the mirrored Vanguard and Scoundrel features in Chapter 6 where the two paths had to stay matched. Triggered by finding the Scoundrel could resolve a difficult theft with no roll at all.

**Auto-successes removed.** Four features let a Sleeping character succeed at a difficult action without rolling, which switches off the Duality Roll and its risk of Fear exactly where the game should tense. Each was rebuilt to buy information, position, or mitigation instead: the Scoundrel's "The Practiced Theft" became "Cased the Joint" (the Keeper names a concrete weakness and you gain Advantage on the job); the Pilot's "The Approach Memorized" became "Hands on the Stick" (ignore an environmental penalty, or turn a piloting Failure with Fear into an ordinary Failure); the Diplomat's "Anticipated Move" now takes its Reaction with Advantage rather than auto-succeeding; and the Vanguard's "Body Memory" was narrowed to one chosen feat in routine conditions only. The Soldier's "The Drill" (already well bounded) gained a line clarifying it covers routine actions, not decisive blows. The Explorer's "The Marked Route" (following a trail you left) was left as low-impact.

**Pilot and Explorer differentiated.** The auto-success was the Pilot's; the Explorer's Methodical Reconnaissance was already information, not a free success, and was left alone, so the two no longer overlap.

**Effort economy retuned.** Effort is earned at half the rate Hope is (two Hope-favored rolls fill the two-segment Effort Track for 1 Effort), so every class Effort Feature was lowered from 3 Effort to 2 to bring its everyday frequency back in line; Masters that cost Effort keep their listed cost. A critical success now also grants 1 point to place in Effort or Resolve (or 1 Resolve if Effort is already full), the one moment the Sleeping bank a reserve from play rather than rest. A new universal menu, "Bearing Down: Common Efforts," gives every Sleeping shared ways to spend Effort (gain Advantage, reroll one Duality die, brace off a severity band, lend an ally +2, and more), none of them an auto-success; subclasses add their own on top.

**Resolve rescaled.** From a flat 2/4/6 by Tier to a smoother climb: base 2, rising by 1 at levels 3, 5, 7, and 9 (2/3/4/5/6, reaching 6 at level 9).

**The Refused Path / Path to Nirvana redesigned (both paths).** The Vanguard's signature state granted Advantage on three Traits plus two immunities plus 2d6 for a whole scene, far too much, and was identical on both paths. It now grants Advantage on one chosen Trait (Agility, Instinct, or Strength), keeps the immunities and the 2d6 opening strike, and lasts a number of rounds equal to Proficiency rather than the whole scene. The Awakened Path to Nirvana was changed in step so the two stay mirror-identical except for the resource.

**Scoundrel Sneak Attack added to the Sleeping path.** The Awakened Scoundrel had a Sneak Attack (extra damage when you have Advantage on an attack, scaling by Tier); the Sleeping Scoundrel did not, an asymmetry between paths. The Sleeping now has the same Sneak Attack, folded into The Quiet Network, and the new "The Opening" Common Effort (2 Effort for Advantage) doubles as a way to arm it.

A consistency check of all 27 subclasses confirmed the Effort-versus-Resolve split was already clean (Specializations cost Effort, Moves cost Resolve, no subclass spends Resolve); no reassignments were needed.

**10.4** - Unified the Diplomat's social currency into a single resource across the whole game. The line had grown three overlapping social currencies that were basically the same thing: the Awakened Diplomat's Favor Tokens (Cultural Lens), the Sleeping Diplomat's separate Reputation Tokens (Standing Reputation), and the Core World community's own Favor Tokens. These are now one resource, the **Favor Token**, with one set of rules.

Generation is identical on both paths (deliberately, so a player who Awakens or who came up Sleeping never relearns it): begin each session with 2, gain 1 the first time each scene they succeed on a meaningful Presence Roll to persuade or deceive, and gain 1 per Long Rest. The Sleeping's "Reputation Token" name and its roll-based, once-per-scene earning method were retired; "Standing Reputation" is kept as the feature's name but now describes the Sleeping reading of the same shared resource. Spending is unified: subclass abilities, House and Free Fleet contacts (the stale "Chapter 9" cross-reference corrected to Chapter 5), automatic success on an institutional task (1 Favor), and a new use replacing the old "permanent standing": spend 5 Favor Tokens to raise your Reputation with one faction by 1 RP (Chapter 16), bought standing that can be lost again by how you act.

The cap is now base 4, raised cumulatively: a Core World Diplomat holds up to 6 (the Core World community feeds the same pool rather than a separate currency, and still grants non-Diplomats up to 2 Tokens of their own), and the Political Operative's Call in a Debt and the Icon subclass each add +1 on top of the current cap rather than setting a flat 5. The Political Operative's Web of Favors lost its now-redundant "start each session with 2" line (every Diplomat does) and gained a once-per-session free contact Favor in its place.

**10.33** - Rules gap filled: the Sleeping Diplomat's Standing Reputation (Chapter 7). The feature said how Reputation Tokens are spent but never how they are earned, leaving a resource with a ceiling and no climb. An "Earning Reputation Tokens" paragraph was added. (Superseded in 10.4, which folded this resource into the unified Favor Token.)

**10.32** - Rules fix: the Sleeping Recovery procedure was aligned with the standard rest moves, removing an unnecessary recovery roll and preserving the Recovery Anchor as a fictional requirement.

**10.31** - Internal consistency audit. The Quick Start harm procedure was aligned with Damage Thresholds and Armor Slot soak, and the core resolution, Reaction Roll, Spotlight, Loadout, Hope, and Proficiency terminology was standardized across the book.

**10.3** - Deep chapter-by-chapter rules review, with the design rule that every section must carry useful mechanics and nothing may be cosmetic.

**Starship combat (Chapter 17) reworked so class identity is mechanical, not decorative.** The old "Class Coordination" table told you a Soldier brings "highest damage on the gun" and a Pilot "owns the helm," abstract role labels with no rule attached. It was replaced with **Class Actions in Ship Combat**: each of the nine classes now has a concrete ship action it spends its Spotlight and path resource on, modeled on the drone rules (reach through a machine and change the battle's state), for example the Soldier's Fire Discipline (coordinate the whole gunline against one arc), the Engineer's Overclock a System (push one subsystem past spec for the round at a cost in Heat and Integrity), the Scholar's Read the Enemy (extract a true weakness and grant the crew Advantage on acting on it), the Scoundrel's Cut the Cord (jam an enemy system), and the Mystic's Veil-Sight (act through the substrate for effects no station can produce). None is "you shoot better."

The two structural premises were made explicit in the text: the crew's ship is a **shared scene in which each player spends their own Spotlight** at a station (not one entity the table puppets in turn), while the Keeper runs **each enemy ship as a single entity** with one block of actions, keeping the action economy tilted toward the crew. The Two Scales table and the Round Structure section were rewritten to state this directly.

Two cosmetic rules found in the same review were made concrete: the **Captain** station, previously granting "a small efficiency that scales with the Captain's standing," now grants a **Command Dice** pool (Presence modifier in d6s that crew members add to station rolls); and the **Ship Quirks** intro, which claimed the Quirks were "mostly invitations to story rather than stat modifiers" while every entry in its own tables carried a concrete effect, was reworded so the text matches its tables (each Quirk is a small concrete effect plus a story hook).

The review of Chapters 1 to 16 and 18 to 23 retained their load-bearing communities, affiliations, classes, multiclassing, and reputation rules. The former Veil-pursuit gap now has a complete DC, Wake, tie, Failure with Fear, ejection, and end-state procedure; only Veil-Aligned weapons and Mystic Veil-Sight may deal damage in transit. Naming a Pearl before burning it remains explicitly optional flavor and grants no mechanical benefit.

**10.21** - Rebrand cleanup. Residual former-product-name references were normalized while preserving in-world Void terminology.

**10.2** - Added the **Human Complications: Silver Linings** rule to the Human ancestry (Chapter 3), a short evocative subrule beneath the existing Complications table: resolve the Complication's cost first, then let the fallout reveal a small, immediate, actionable opening, a way to use the damage rather than erase it, with a "cost first, opening second" control box so it is never used as plot armor. The expanded version (a four-column d6 table and table-craft guidance) lives in the Humans: The Catalyst mini-expansion; the Core carries the short form.

**10.1** - Final product-name normalization to **VeilFarers**, the line's final published name. Every in-text reference to the game as a product (60 instances) was renamed; the world and system vocabulary built on the word "void" (void damage, the Void Domain, Voidwalker, the Void between hulls, void powers, the Veil, the Stellar Veil as a setting element) is unchanged, as it is fiction and mechanics, not the title. Running headers and the cover tagline updated to "Veilfarers: A Game of Distant Stars Across a Broken Universe" (the former "Chronicles of the Stellar Veil" is retired as a tagline; the Stellar Veil remains the in-world phenomenon). No mechanical content changed in this pass.

**10.01** - Errata pass surfaced while rebuilding Rust and Steel and the Keeper's Companion against this book. Chapter 18 (Domain Mechanics) corrected: the Starter Loadout is **2 Level 1 Powers** (it had read "usually three Powers", contradicting the V9 class entries), and Power acquisition now points to **Chapter 12, Option 8, New Power** as one advancement option rather than an automatic per-level grant. Chapter 10 (The Weight of Steel): the **Area Effects** block rewritten from the residual d20 save language (Reflex / Fortitude / Will Saves against a Save DC) to canon **Reaction Rolls** (Agility, Strength, or Instinct against a DC fixed before the roll). Twelve stray en dashes normalized to hyphens (numeric ranges and one compound modifier, heritage of the V8 extraction). The V9 changelog entry below was also corrected where it referenced the advancement menu by its pre-renumbering labels.

**V9** - The June 2026 editorial pass. Path-resource engine: Hope for Awakened, Effort for Sleeping, with the two-segment Effort Track as the sole Effort source; Recovery no longer grants Effort. Character creation reordered (Step 3 is Path, then Class, then Subclass); Awakened Starter Loadout is 2 Level 1 Powers (from the 6 of your Domains), with a Starter Loadout block in every class entry. Chapter 5 renamed Affiliations; House Reputation optional track removed in favor of Standing; Church of the Eternal Veil removed as a playable affiliation; Independent Favor Pool. Combat: attack procedure clarified (attack vs Evasion, then damage with Proficiency scaling vs thresholds); Overkill is +1 HP per 10 over Severe (optional Deadly: per 5); Direct Damage defined; range bands unified to Melee / Very Close / Close / Far / Very Far; armor terminology unified to Armor Score and Armor Slots for characters, drones, vehicles, and starships; the magic damage type is now void. Awakening rewritten as a transformational arc and moved to the end of Chapter 7. New **Chapter 14: Drones and Remote Tools**; chapters after 13 renumbered (+1). Stale page lists removed from the Glossary pending index regeneration. Recommended-tier pass: choice tables for Affiliations and Awakened Classes; the final creation checklist and the Crew Step heading; Community Benefits restructured to Trigger/Roll/Effect lines; the Displaced Enclave universalized as the Hidden Enclave (Ailuran archetype kept); brief in-Core profiles for the Solara Compact and Stellar Commerce Guild as advanced options; explicit Sleeping lines in every affiliation attitude; How to Read a Sleeping Class Entry, the Effort-vs-Resolve box, and the broken-scene refresh rule; the path-resource table; group rolls in path-resource language; the shared-scene spotlight question; the attack-procedure and defenses tables; Surprise as attacker Advantage; Surrender highlighted. Chapter 12 advancement unified: one menu for both paths (Option 8, New Power, with Awakened and Sleeping mirrors; Tempered Resolve as Option 11), merged resource caps, Changing Paths in Play with the path-specific refund, a Sleeping reading of the worked example, and the appended Sleeping section dissolved into the main flow; the chapter at-a-glance corrected to the real two-slot economy. New advancement Option 4, +1 to a Trait (one slot; the same Trait only once per Tier, resetting at Levels 5 and 8, for a +3 campaign ceiling per Trait); menu renumbered to eleven options and references updated.

**V8** - Added Repair Nanites (Synthetic healing consumables) to the gear table; a healing-by-repair note in the combat chapter; an emergency nanite ship-patch note in The Void Between Hulls.

**V7** - Appendices relabeled correctly: Appendix A (Quick Start) and Appendix B (Glossary), previously shown as Chapter 20 and 21.

# THE SACRED SYSTEM BIBLE: NON-NEGOTIABLE CANON

**Authority: Rules canon 12.06.** This appendix is the line-wide mechanical contract for *VeilFarers*. It is deliberately placed at the end of the Corebook so future work has one final reference. If another passage in this Corebook conflicts with this appendix, this appendix controls. If a supplement, adventure, quick reference, character sheet, example, or older release conflicts with the current Corebook, the current Corebook controls. A supplement may add content or a clearly labelled optional module; it may not silently replace a Core procedure.

A specific feature may override a general rule only when it states the exception, its trigger, cost, target, duration, and end condition. An unnamed implication is not an exception. A table may knowingly adopt a house rule, but that choice does not alter published canon.

## 1. THE RESOLUTION CONTRACT

| ELEMENT | CANON |
| --- | --- |
| **Dice** | Roll one Hope d12 and one Fear d12 together. They must remain distinguishable. |
| **Total** | Add both d12 results, one relevant Trait, and any explicit modifiers. Compare the final total with the DC. |
| **Traits** | The only Traits are Agility, Strength, Finesse, Knowledge, Instinct, and Presence. Pilot/Navigate, Tech, and Medicine are Subtraits of Finesse or Knowledge, never separate Traits or skills. |
| **DC timing** | Fix the DC before the dice come to rest. It may be hidden, never changed after seeing the roll. |
| **DC ladder** | Use 5 Routine, 10 Easy, 15 Challenging, 20 Difficult, 25 Extreme, or 30 Nearly Impossible. An opposed roll or a rule explicitly identified as a formula exception, such as Sleeping Mystic Uncanny Power, may depart from the fixed ladder. Nothing else may. |
| **Success** | Final total equal to or above the DC. |
| **Failure** | Final total below the DC. |
| **Dominance** | The higher individual d12 determines Hope or Fear. Modifiers and Resolve never change dominance. |
| **Critical** | If the physical Hope and Fear d12 faces match, the result is always a Critical Success, regardless of total or face. This includes 1+1. There is one critical procedure and no negative critical result. Player Rolls receive the Path payout; Keeper attack Critical Successes use the Keeper damage procedure and grant no path resource or Fear. A feature changes whether the dice match only if it expressly changes a die face. |

The five results are Critical Success, Success with Hope, Success with Fear, Failure with Hope, and Failure with Fear. **Failure with Fear is the worst normal roll result.** Matching dice can never trigger a jam, friendly-fire accident, suit breach, item destruction, death, or other negative result merely because of the faces shown. A rule triggered by Failure with Fear never triggers on matching dice, even if the Fear die shows a low number.

| RESULT | INVIOLABLE OUTCOME |
| --- | --- |
| **Critical Success** | Automatic success, fixed Path payout, and critical attack damage when applicable. A generic critical grants no extra Action, resource, item, Condition, damage, or permanent statistic. |
| **Success with Hope** | The Action succeeds and normal Path progress resolves. No complication applies. |
| **Success with Fear** | The Action succeeds, the Keeper gains 1 Fear subject to the hard maximum of 12, and exactly one consequence stated before the Roll or printed by the Feature applies. If none was eligible, no consequence is invented. |
| **Failure with Hope** | The Action fails and normal Path progress resolves. No complication, new clue, route, item, position, or numeric benefit appears unless the Feature prints one. |
| **Failure with Fear** | The Action fails, the Keeper gains 1 Fear subject to the hard maximum of 12, and exactly one consequence stated before the Roll or printed by the Feature applies. It never means automatic death. |

Consequences are declared before dice settle or referenced from a complete printed rule. They are resolved at that Roll and cannot be banked, chosen retroactively, or supplemented later. Fear generated by the Roll is a separate resource and may later buy only a printed Keeper Move or ability.

**Advantage and Disadvantage.** Roll one d6 and add it for Advantage or subtract it for Disadvantage. Multiple sources do not stack. One of each cancels; after cancellation, the roll is normal. An explicit flat modifier is not Advantage and applies only as its rule states.

**Experiences.** Invoke at most one relevant Experience per roll. An Awakened character spends 1 Hope and adds its flat value. A Sleeping character invokes it free and adds the same flat value. Experiences never change dominance and never create a critical.

**Reaction Rolls.** Defensive responses use the named Trait as a Reaction Roll against a fixed DC. The system does not use saving throws, Reflex, Fortitude, Will, or a separate save statistic.

## 2. HOPE, EFFORT, RESOLVE, FEAR, AND STRESS

### Hope

Awakened characters begin each normal session with 2 Hope and hold at most 6. Hope does not carry between sessions unless play resumes the same unresolved scene. A Hope-dominant Success or Failure grants 1 Hope. A Critical Success clears 1 Stress and grants 1 Hope. Hope beyond the cap is lost.

### Effort and the Effort Track

Sleeping characters begin play with 2 Effort and hold at most 6. Effort and its two-segment Track persist between sessions. On a meaningful Hope-dominant roll, mark one segment whether the roll succeeds or fails. When both segments are marked, clear them and gain 1 Effort. Trivial, repeated, or consequence-free rolls never mark the Track. Rest and Recovery never generate Effort. Only a rule that explicitly names an exception may grant it directly.

On a Critical Success, a Sleeping character clears 1 Stress, marks both Effort Track segments and resolves the completed Track for 1 Effort, then gains one further point placed in Effort or Resolve. If Effort is full, that further point becomes Resolve. This is the complete Sleeping critical payout.

### Resolve

Resolve Dice are d4 unless the Tier 3 Tempered Resolve option upgrades the whole pool to d6. Maximum Resolve is 2 at level 1, 3 at level 3, 4 at level 5, 5 at level 7, and 6 at level 9. A Sleeping character begins play with the pool full; it otherwise persists between sessions. Resolve is recovered by choosing Prepare during rest, by the Sleeping critical payout, or by a feature that explicitly grants it. Resolve added to a roll changes only the total.

### Fear

The Keeper begins each session with 1d4+2 Fear. Fear resets every session and never carries over. The hard maximum is **12**. The pool can never exceed 12; excess Fear is lost.

Fear is gained only from a **player-rolled** Success with Fear or Failure with Fear, or a printed environment, antagonist, adventure, clock, or feature with an explicit trigger and amount. Keeper-controlled attack Rolls never generate Fear merely from dominance; their noncritical dominance matters only when the printed action has a complete rider. An action being dangerous, aggressive, or surprising is not by itself a Fear trigger. Fear may buy only stated Keeper Moves and abilities. A Fear spend cannot bypass the Dying, Final, consent, or Death Move procedures and cannot declare a player character dead by fiat.

### Stress

Default Stress maximum is 6; Synthetics have 7. At maximum, a character is Overwhelmed: they cannot mark or spend more Stress, cannot pay Stress costs, and have Disadvantage on all rolls until at least 1 Stress is cleared. No character becomes unconscious merely from being Overwhelmed unless an explicit effect says so.

## 3. REST AND RECOVERY

During a **Short Rest**, choose two different moves: Tend Wounds clears `1d4 + Tier` HP; Clear Stress clears `1d4 + Tier` Stress; Repair Armor restores `1d4 + Tier` Armor Slots with suitable tools; Prepare grants 1 Hope if Awakened or 1 Resolve if Sleeping. During a **Long Rest**, choose two different moves: Recover clears all HP; Decompress clears all Stress, including Long Bruise; Repair All Armor restores all Armor Slots; Prepare restores Hope to its normal session-start value or Resolve to maximum. A move cannot be chosen twice unless a feature explicitly allows it.

A Sleeping character needs their named Recovery Anchor to choose Clear Stress during a Short Rest or Decompress during a Long Rest. The Anchor is not a roll and does not affect Prepare, wound care, or armor repair. If it is unavailable, establish a new Anchor over a Long Rest. Downtime restores HP, Stress, Armor Slots, and renewable resources to maximum. Neither rest nor Recovery generates Effort.

## 4. PATHS, CREATION, POWERS, AND ADVANCEMENT

Awakened and Sleeping are complete, equal Paths. A starting Awakened character has two Experiences at +2, 2 Hope, and a Starter Loadout of exactly two Level 1 Powers from accessible Domains. A starting Sleeping character has three Experiences at +2, 2 Effort, a two-segment Effort Track, full Resolve, the class Moves, Honed Edge, and a Recovery Anchor. Ancestry never determines Path.

**Ancestry Complications.** At most once per character per session, after a player-rolled Fear-dominant noncritical Roll materially uses an Ancestry Gift, the Keeper may spend 1 Fear and roll 1d6 on that ancestry's table. The result is rolled, never chosen. Matching dice never trigger it and it never selects a player Action. Apply only a complete printed effect; if a row lacks one, its full mechanical effect is to mark 1 Stress and use the row only as narration.

An Awakened Loadout holds 5 Powers at Tier 1, 6 at Tier 2, and 7 at Tier 3. The Vault has no cap. A Power acquired through Chapter 12 Option 8 enters the Vault. Recall is free during a Long Rest; during a Short Rest it costs the Power's printed Recall Cost in Stress; during an active scene it uses an Action, costs the printed Recall Cost, and costs 1 Hope. Self-Recalling Powers use their own printed procedure. There is no automatic Power every level and no extra Mystic Loadout slot.

**Formal DC exception, Sleeping Mystic.** Uncanny Power first rolls spent Resolve Dice plus Knowledge to set the highest accessible Domain level, capped by character level. After choosing an unlocked Power at or below that result, make Knowledge Spellcast against `DC = 10 + the chosen Power's Domain-package level`. This formula is the only standard player-facing exception to the fixed DC ladder; it is not rounded to a rung. The Keeper gains 1 Fear per Resolve spent, subject to the hard maximum of 12. A Critical Success refunds the spent Resolve after the Power manifests; the Fear remains.

**Multiclass.** Available at level 5 or later, once per character, and costs both Advancement Slots for that level on either Path. It grants the secondary Hope Feature or Effort Feature and a new Background Question, never the second Class Feature, Subclass, starter Loadout, Class Items, resource pool, Tier Achievement, or Loadout capacity. An Awakened multiclass activates one genuinely new Domain at half level, rounded up. A Sleeping multiclass gains one eligible Class Resolve Move and records one genuinely new Dormant Domain; that Domain grants nothing while Sleeping.

**Path change.** Core play permits only Sleeping to Awakened, and only when a qualifying event in the fiction explicitly triggers the option. It is never an ordinary advancement choice, level reward, group vote, or compulsory upgrade. Convert Effort to Hope up to 6; retire Effort, Track, Resolve, Honed Edge, free Experience use, Recovery Anchor, Sleeping Features and Moves; activate the corresponding Awakened package and two legal Level 1 Powers. For a Sleeping multiclass, convert the secondary Effort Feature, retire its secondary Resolve Move, and activate its Dormant Domain without new Slots or starter Powers. The Core contains no ordinary reverse procedure. Keeper-only reversal rules are exceptional, event-triggered, consent-based options and never become a player-selectable Core procedure.

## 5. PERSONAL COMBAT

Combat uses the Spotlight, not rolled initiative. Spotlight is dynamic: it is never gained, lost, compared, or resolved through a contest, Roll, initiative value, bonus, penalty, Advantage, Disadvantage, or speed. The players choose among eligible PCs as the fiction permits; the Keeper chooses eligible NPCs or Threat Groups and may spend Fear to Spotlight one eligible NPC under the Fear procedure. A printed rule may require a character to yield Spotlight, but no rule may create a Spotlight contest. One significant action normally spends the Spotlight; Reactions and explicit free effects work only as printed. Attacks are Duality Rolls using the named Trait against Evasion. Area effects use Reaction Rolls, not saves.

Where legacy card text says a character's **turn**, read it as that character's current Spotlight. “Until the end of the next Spotlight” means until the end of that character's next Spotlight. A **round** ends after every eligible participant has taken exactly one Spotlight, unless a printed feature explicitly grants an additional Action without another Spotlight; end-of-round effects then resolve once.

Personal ranges are Melee, Very Close, Close, Far, and Very Far. Movement and features use bands, not feet, meters of Speed, Short, or Medium range. Exact measurements may describe fiction but do not create extra mechanical bands.

**Personal weapon Proficiency.** Identify one Proficiency Die in the printed damage expression, normally the first listed die. Roll that die once per Proficiency rank, every other printed die once, and the flat modifier once. Thus `2d8+2` at Proficiency 3 is `4d8+2`. Never add the attack Trait to damage unless a feature says so.

Compare damage with Major and Severe Thresholds: below Major marks 1 HP; Major to below Severe marks 2; Severe or above marks 3; every full 10 above Severe marks 1 additional HP. One Armor Slot lowers the hit one severity step. Direct HP damage bypasses Thresholds and Armor Slots only when the rule explicitly says direct.

On a player attack Critical Success, double the complete normal damage-dice pool and add flat modifiers once. On a Keeper attack Critical Success, maximize every die in the normal pool and add flat modifiers once. Then resolve thresholds and Armor Slots normally.

**Resistance and immunity.** Resistance to a named canonical damage type or printed damage tag halves that incoming damage before comparison with Thresholds, rounding down. Multiple applicable Resistances do not stack. Immunity to a named damage type or tag reduces that damage to 0 and prevents a secondary Condition delivered only by that damage; it does not cancel an unrelated effect unless the rule says so. “Resistant” used only as ordinary description grants no mechanical benefit. Vulnerable is the Core Condition: attacks against the target have Advantage; it never doubles damage by implication.

**Damage types and tags.** The four universal damage types are **Physical, Energy, Void, and Neural**. Kinetic, Ballistic, Blunt, and Impact are Physical tags. Plasma, Laser, Arc, Thermal, Fire, Cold, Sonic, Radiant, Radiation, Lightning, Corrosive, and Acid are Energy tags. Toxic, Chemical, and Poison use the type printed by the item; Psionic uses Neural. A tag describes delivery and interaction but has no inherent rider, Condition, ongoing damage, armor loss, or penetration unless its complete rule states one. Matching dice remain a Critical Success even when a feature explicitly changes only critical damage; the Path payout is never removed.

At 0 HP a character becomes Dying. At the start of each Dying Spotlight, 1d12 result 8+ marks Dying Progress; the second mark enters Final. At the start of each Final Spotlight, 8+ marks Final Progress; the second mark means death. Stabilize adjacent with Knowledge (Medicine) or Finesse at DC 15 while Dying or DC 20 while Final; stabilization clears progress and restores no HP. A Dying or Final player may voluntarily replace a progress roll with the Death Move, Blaze of Glory. It is always the player's choice and death after it is irrevocable. Ordinary death can be reversed only by a feature that explicitly says it revives a dead character and states its window and cost; no feature can reverse a completed Death Move. Nothing triggers a Death Move merely because a hit lands or Fear is spent.

Only the Core condition registry is universal. A bespoke condition is valid only if its rule defines exact effect, duration, stacking, and how it ends. Flavor words are not conditions.

## 6. TECHNOLOGY, WEALTH, AND ACCESS

Technology Tier and Wealth Tier are separate scales. Technology Tier governs sophistication and access; Wealth Tier governs affordability and social reach. Standard Credit values by Wealth Tier are 1, 4, 9, 16, and 25 unless an item prints a specific exception. Class Technology Access controls training. Using an untrained weapon family imposes Disadvantage; other inaccessible equipment cannot be operated until access is gained. Equipment properties must use the Core or Rust & Steel registry, or define a new property completely where introduced.

**Burden.** Capacity equals `6 + Strength modifier`. At 1-2 above capacity, movement is limited to one band per Spotlight and Agility or Strength Rolls to run, climb, jump, swim, or resist forced movement have Disadvantage. At 3 or more above capacity, the character cannot move or take a physical Action while carrying the excess; they may drop non-secured carried items as a free effect at the start of their Spotlight. No book may substitute a discretionary encumbrance penalty.

## 7. STARSHIP COMBAT

The player ship is a shared scene: each player spends their own Spotlight at a station. Each enemy ship is one Keeper-controlled entity with one action block. Ordinary navigation and vehicle control use Finesse (Pilot/Navigate); **Pilot maneuvers and Veil pursuit during starship combat use Instinct**. Gunner attacks use Finesse or Knowledge as the weapon and fiction require. Engineer uses Knowledge. Captain uses Presence and the Core Command Dice procedure.

Ship scale has Hull, Armor Slots in Fore/Aft/Port/Starboard arcs, Heat, Ship Evasion, and named Systems with Integrity, normally 3. No secondary structural-stress track exists. Direct Hull loss bypasses Armor Slots and the severity table. Otherwise, damage depletes the targeted arc point for point, then converts the remainder: 1-5 = 1 Hull; 6-12 = 2; 13-20 = 3; 21-30 = 4; 31+ = 5, plus 1 per full 10 beyond 30. Each arc regenerates 2 Armor Slots at end of round.

**Ship states.** An **Exposed arc** gives Advantage only to attacks that target that named arc; it does not stack and ends at the start of the affected ship's next Pilot Spotlight. A **Visible ship** grants +2 on attacks against it; Visible does not stack and ends when its rule states. Neither state changes damage.

Before every ship attack Roll, name the targeted arc and at most one target System. The target crew confirms that System is reachable through the arc or names one reachable alternative before dice are rolled. If a ship-scale Critical Success causes Hull loss, that declared System loses 1 Integrity once. If no System was declared, no System Integrity is lost. A noncritical hit causes no System Integrity loss unless its printed weapon property says so.

| TIER | CANONICAL SCALE | HULL RANGE | BASE EVASION | MR |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| **1** | Small craft: fighters, shuttles, couriers | 6-12 | **16** | **×1** |
| **2** | Light vessels: freighters, transports, corvettes | 12-22 | **12** | **×2** |
| **3** | Medium vessels: frigates, destroyers, institutional ships | 22-30 | **12** | **×2** |
| **4** | Capital vessels: cruisers, carriers, dreadnoughts | 34-52 | **8** | **×3** |
| **5** | Legendary vessel or megastructure | Set-piece | **8 default** | **×3 default** |

Rust & Steel contains the detailed named-hull registry. A name has one Tier and one stat block. Its **Core Power** subsystem is an optional advanced module and is inactive unless the table adopts it before play; ignoring Core Power never changes the base hull statistics.

**Mount Rating.** Naval weapon damage never uses a separate naval Proficiency statistic. Every hull has a **Mount Rating (MR)** determined by its scale: Tier 1 = ×1, Tier 2-3 = ×2, Tier 4-5 = ×3.

Roll the complete printed weapon damage expression once, including its printed flat modifier, then multiply the result by MR. On a PC Critical, double the printed dice and add the flat modifier once before MR. On a Keeper Critical, maximize the printed dice and add the flat modifier once before MR.

**Character Proficiency and Mount Rating are separate mechanics.** Never substitute one for the other.

**Ship Heat.** Reaching the Heat Cap has no penalty. When an increase first takes Heat above the Cap, every system loses 1 Integrity, the Pilot makes an Instinct Roll, DC 15, or the Primary Drive loses 1 additional Integrity, and the ship is Visible for one round. Do not retrigger while it remains above the Cap; Heat must fall to the Cap or lower first. The crew does not become Overwhelmed from ship Heat. **Criminal Heat** defaults to one crew-wide 0-10 score; Rust & Steel Chapter 2.3 is its sole procedure. Its Individual and Factional Heat modules may replace that one score only when explicitly adopted before the campaign, never alongside it or each other. Keeper’s Companion expands how to present and manage the adopted procedure; it does not create another Heat track, trigger table, or reduction procedure. Ship Heat and criminal Heat never convert into one another.

**Sensor Lock.** Spend the Sensor station's Spotlight and roll Knowledge: Adjacent DC 5, Engagement DC 10, Standard DC 15, Long DC 20, Extreme DC 25. **Eligible targets are limited to vehicle- or starship-scale stat blocks. Personal-scale creatures and characters cannot carry a Sensor Lock.** It costs no path resource or Stress and requires a working Sensor Array. Success places one pending Lock on the target; the next Gunner attack made from the locking ship has Advantage, then spends it. A target carries at most one Lock. Evasive Pattern, Disengage, or opening range breaks it automatically at Long/Extreme, requires Pilot Instinct Roll, DC 15 at Standard, and cannot break it at Engagement/Adjacent. It also ends if the locking Sensor Array goes offline. At Extreme, only Guided or explicitly sensor-guided weapons can exploit it.

**Core naval tags.** Guided permits one missed-attack reroll per mounted weapon per scene and never creates a Lock. Anti-Fighter adds +1 to the attack and +1d6 before Mount Rating against Tier 1 craft and missiles. Plasma suppresses the targeted arc's next end-of-round regeneration after a hit removes a Slot or Hull; it does not stack. Disruptor applies double efficiency against Slots, then only half of remaining unmodified damage to Hull under the exact Chapter 17 formula. Shield-Piercing permits at most half of the arc's current Slots, rounded down, to absorb the hit. Heavy fires at most once per round. Fixed-Forward targets only through the Fore arc. Veil-Aligned permits damage during Veil transit and grants no penetration, damage, or Void type. Identical naval tag names must have identical effects across books; Rust & Steel is the expanded registry.

**Emergency jump.** Pre-Jump Calculation is Knowledge, DC 10, or DC 15 under fire. Success establishes the declared destination; Failure with Hope establishes none; Failure with Fear establishes none and marks 1 Heat. Jump Initiation is Pilot Instinct, DC 10, and may be attempted only with a solution. Success spends the Pearl and enters transit; Failure with Hope leaves ship and Pearl in place; Failure with Fear does the same and costs the Primary Drive 1 Integrity. One pursuing ship with a ready Pearl may make one Sensor-station Knowledge Roll, DC 15: success permits pursuit, Failure with Hope loses the wake, and Failure with Fear loses it and marks 1 Heat.

**Veil pursuit.** Each side starts at 0 Wake. Each round both Pilots roll Instinct, DC 15. A Critical Success outranks a noncritical success; otherwise higher successful rank and then total marks 1 Wake, and exact ties or two failures mark none. Each Pilot's Failure with Fear marks 1 Heat as its single consequence. At 3 Wake, choose Break Contact for the scene or Force Ejection: both ships return at Standard range, the winner faces the loser's Aft arc, and the loser marks 2 Heat. Only Veil-Aligned weapons and Mystic Veil-Sight deal damage in transit. A Pearl that cannot sustain transit ejects its ship at Standard range and marks 2 Heat. Wake always clears when pursuit ends.

A ship weapon fired at a personal-scale target attacks with Disadvantage, and the target cannot carry a Sensor Lock. Resolve the complete damage normally, including Critical effects, apply MR, then multiply by **×5**.

Personal shields and explicit raw-damage reductions apply normally. Personal armor gives limited protection: halve its Major and Severe Damage Thresholds for this attack, rounding each up, while Armor Slots are unchanged and spent normally. Resolve severity through those halved thresholds using the normal personal damage procedure, including Overkill. Ship-rated cover applies normally.

HP loss does not stop at 0 HP. Exactly 0 HP is Dying with the Death Move available; -1 HP or lower is killed outright with no Death Move.

## 8. ADVERSARIES, FEAR ABILITIES, AND OPTIONAL MODULES

Keeper's Companion is the canonical adversary registry. An expansion variant must have a distinct name if its stat block differs. Adversaries are attacked against Evasion; they do not possess a second Difficulty defense. A creature may use at most one Fear Ability per Spotlight cycle, plus one eligible defensive Reaction, unless a specific stat block explicitly says otherwise.

Optional modules must be labelled before their rules, state when they are adopted, define every new track and term, and describe their interface with the Core engine. An optional module is never active merely because its book is open. Social conflict cannot compel a player character's belief, identity, allegiance, Awakening, or final decision without that player's consent.

## 9. PUBLICATION GATE: RULES THAT MAY NOT REAPPEAR

Every future manuscript, reference card, pregen, and example must pass these checks:

- Matching Duality Dice always use the single Critical Success procedure. No negative-critical label, double-1 mishap, low-Fear-face malfunction, or generic mishap trigger may appear.
- Fear maximum is 12 everywhere, with session reset and explicit generation only.
- Success with Fear and Failure with Fear may apply only one predeclared or printed consequence; the consequence resolves with that Roll and is never banked or invented retroactively.
- No saves, rolled initiative, Spotlight contest, or Roll/bonus/penalty/Advantage/Disadvantage/speed that determines who takes Spotlight may appear as an active mechanic. A printed rule may only require a character to yield Spotlight, and the Keeper may only take it through the Fear procedure. No separate Awareness/Stealth/Deception/Tech skills, personal Medium/Short range, feet of Speed, Difficulty defense, undefined secondary ship-damage track, or undefined condition/damage/tag may appear as an active mechanic.
- Every DC uses the standard ladder or names its formal exception.
- Every mechanical noun is defined before use, including trigger, cost, target, effect, duration, stacking, and end condition where relevant.
- Resistance always uses the Core half-damage procedure; an armor property that increases Thresholds must say so and is not Resistance.
- Repeated rules and quick references must reproduce the Core procedure, not paraphrase it into a new procedure.
- Worked examples must execute every relevant rule in order, including costs, critical payout, end-of-round regeneration, Heat, and resource caps.
- The same named adversary, hull, weapon, property, and condition must have one mechanical identity. A variant needs a distinct name.
- Core authority, event-triggered Sleeping-to-Awakened conversion, two-Slot multiclassing, nonbankable Advancement Slots, rest choices, Recall costs, Reaction Rolls, personal damage, and starship damage may not be changed by implication.

## 10. CANON CHANGE PROTOCOL

A future rules change is valid only if the new Corebook version does all of the following in the same release: amends this Bible; updates the master rule in its chapter; updates every Core quick reference and worked example; propagates the change to every affected supplement and adventure; records it in each affected changelog; and passes a line-wide search for the retired wording. Until all six steps are complete, the change is a draft and the last complete canon remains in force.

**End of canon.**
